He'll give you another gesture, "Collapse" (9/33), after which you can move on to the main event, otherwise known as the beloved Fire Keeper in the center of the shrine. As the resident "stat waifu" of this game, the Fire Keeper will be the one you go to for leveling up...so go ahead and use the Soul Chunks you've got (the fastest way is to sell them to the Handmaid, but you haven't met her yet, so you can just do it the manual way for now) so you can raise your Ashen One up to level 14 with the following specifications: Talking to the Fire Keeper again will have her inform you that using the Coiled Sword in the central Bonfire will let you travel to the lands beyond and seek out the Lords of Cinder, but you're going to save that for later. For now, head up the stairs behind the five thrones in the room and drop down to the middle-left one to speak to the only Lord of Cinder who's made the journey: Ludleth of Courland. This guy will only give you a token explanation of what he's doing here for now, but truthfully, he's one of the most badass characters in the whole dang story. Drop back down to the ground and head through the arch underneath the entrance to the shrine to first meet the Shrine Handmaiden, sitting in a chair on the right: She sells a number of things worth buying (the sorceries, however, are available at half-price from other merchants, so you're not getting them from her at all), but seeing as you're almost broke right now, that'll have to wait...though she also serves the helpful purpose of buying stuff you have no interest in keeping, which you'll absolutely be doing as the game goes on.

Note: for the duration of your platinum playthroughs, the items you absolutely want to keep in your inventory are Blessings, Siegbräu, Pellets, Moss Clumps, Resins/Bundles, Coins, and Homeward Bones. Everything else not explicitly noted with something like (DO NOT SELL!), especially duplicate/excess/redundant armor pieces, can be sold at your earliest convenience. Now, it's time to reunite with the second-best character from the original game: Andre of Astora! As the game's one and only blacksmith, Andre will be crucial to your journey across Lothric for a number of reasons: With Souls and Titanite, he can Reinforce your weapons and armor, greatly raising their stats. After you bring certain Coals and Gems to him, he'll also become capable of Infusing weapons with certain elements that augment their damage output. If any of your equipment breaks, he can Repair it for Souls (you can avoid this with frequent Bonfire resting). Since this game uniquely gives you two types of Estus, he can also Allot how many you have of each (drawing one from the other); it's recommended that right now, you use this to give yourself a fourth golden Estus Flask, since you won't be using spells. Finally, with the aid of Estus Shards found throughout the land, you can Reinforce your Estus Flasks, letting them grant more HP with each use. All in all, extremely useful! You'll also want to Talk to Andre a few times to receive his gesture, "Hurrah!" (10/33). Before venturing into the lands outside, return to the shrine entrance and head up the stairs to the left (when facing the entrance) to head up a set of stairs leading to a tower outside. Just outside the columns here, there'll be a corpse of a Giant (as seen many times in Dark Souls II) that will occasionally drop a Seed of a Giant Tree, a very useful item that turns enemies against any invading phantoms you're dealing with. The tower at the top is locked, and the Shrine Handmaid will only part with the key for 20,000 Souls, so you're not going in just yet - but you can still collect the loot around said tower, such as the Soul of a Deserted Corpse on a, well, corpse to the left.

Return to the line of coffins next to the Giant tree and run off the far edge of them toward a ledge below, where another corpse holds a Homeward Bone; the stone path ahead will lead you to a corpse with another Ember. Further along this path, take out the two Hollows resting on the stairs and pick up the East-West Shield from a corpse in a tree...then look up the path for an enemy far, far stronger than Iudex Gundyr: the Sword Master. This guy is extremely lethal for where the game put him, owing to his use of an Uchigatana that deals high and fast damage across a wide area, so it may not seem wise to deal with him right now - but doing so will grant you quite a few advantages. It's entirely possible to bait him into falling off the edge of the cliff with one of his lunging attacks, after which you can exit and reload the game to spawn his item drops, but the author found it easier to just wait for him to attack, then capitalize on the recovery period afterward by getting in 3-4 R1 attacks (each of which will stagger him since he's not wearing armor) and roll away afterward to a safe distance so you can repeat the process. This will likely take a few tries, but when the Sword Master goes down (and doesn't respawn), you can collect his Uchigatana, as well as the Master's Set, and earn 2,000 Souls for your trouble. Since the door behind him is currently locked, this is as far as you'll go in the Firelink Shrine for now - return to the main hall and press at the empty fire to Embed the Coiled Sword in it, creating a central Bonfire to return to throughout the game, before Traveling to the High Wall of Lothric.

To start off, you'll find yourself in a room with no Bonfire, so open the doors at the other end and head down the stairs outside to reach the actual Bonfire of the area (perhaps after gazing across the gothic architecture in the distance). Look to the right of this landing from a broken section of the wall, which you'll want to walk through so you can dispatch the crossbow-wielding Hollow that would otherwise be sniping at you as you proceed along the wall here. Looking down, you'll see two more Starved Hounds walking along the wall; drop down and let them come to you one at a time, since if you stay on the wooden ramp, they'll more than likely both come after you simultaneously, which is too much to deal with right now. Once they're gone, carefully move ahead to take out the axe- and halberd-wielding Hollows patrolling the wall (also ideally one at a time). Once the area above is clear - you can kill the kneeling Hollows too for some easy Souls - descend the stairs to the right to kill a Hollow carrying his own Estus Flask (indicated by the orange glow) and collect a Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the body next to him. Back on the wall, head up the stairs on the far end and be prepared to start massacring worshippers; one of the Hollows to the right, near the one who'll begin shooting at you with a crossbow, is secretly afflicted with the same crap that took over Iudex Gundyr in the back half of his boss fight, and he'll transform once you get close enough. Don't let him do that - rush over and cut down the worshippers with a single attack, and the transformation will never happen. You can collect a Longbow and 12 Standard Arrows from the corpse here, but otherwise, that's the extent of this area for now. Return to (and rest at) the Bonfire, then head down the stairs next to it to another bridge filled with kneeling Hollows and a new type bearing lanterns; when you get close to one of these, they'll start drawing the attention of OTHER enemies nearby to rush over and attack you all at once, so killing them quickly is paramount. Run down and take out the one on the right, as well as the one down the stairs on the other side of the bridge (the wyvern is actually dead, so don't worry), leaving you free to deal with all the kneeling Hollows and collect another Soul of a Deserted Corpse from a corpse on the left side. Heading up the stairs to the left of the wyvern, you'll see more kneeling Hollows and a third lantern-bearing one on the far end - rush over and kill him before he can alert the others, which will let you take out the worshippers and the two sturdier Hollows up the stairs nearby at your own pace so you can claim the Binoculars from the top.

Instead of heading back down to the bridge, circle around to the wyvern corpse's left wing, where you'll see a narrow walkway you can drop down onto; doing so will bring you to a short hallway with a corpse bearing two Gold Pine Resins (applies lightning to your right-hand weapon). The room beyond, where you would've entered with the normal entrance, has three soldier Hollows waiting for you, though they can (and should) be engaged individually - once they're gone, collect 2 Firebombs from a corpse, descend the ladder and collect a Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the body behind the table in the next room, then head outside to engage a spear-and-shield-bearing Hollow. Now, the cluster of enemies at the end of the walkway and the group at the top of the stairs might seem like a tough battle at this point in the game...but don't worry, because you're going to replace it with an even TOUGHER encounter, because running up the stairs will cause a very much ALIVE wyvern to swoop down and begin breathing fire! The wyvern will first target the enemies at the top of the stairs and then the ones on your level, once you run back down the stairs for your life; he'll get rid of all of them for you, but that leaves you with a still-angry wyvern to work around. You can't hope to fight it, so instead, you'll be taking advantage of the gaps between its fire-breathing sessions to advance and collect some good stuff - a Club, a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse, an Ember, and a Claymore - before opening the door underneath the wyvern and heading inside the tower. Within, you'll find what looks like your first treasure chest...but true to form for this series, this is actually a Mimic (indicated by the lid of the "chest" raising and lowering like it's breathing). These guys are much, much tougher than they were in the previous two games, so like the Sword Master, you have to carefully wait for openings between his attacks (make especially sure to avoid his grabs, as they'll outright kill you if you're not at full health) - it's worth taking him out now, though, because he'll drop a Deep Battle Axe, your first option for dealing elemental damage (Dark, in this case) and a worthy replacement for your Long Sword for now.

Depending on how many Estus Flasks you're left with at this point, you may want to use a Homeward Bone to return to the Bonfire, refresh yourself, and make your way back to the tower interior, where you'll want to climb the ladder to the other wooden platform and open the door leading back outside. Quickly take out the two Hollow soldiers on either side of the stairs here, because you're going to want to take on the next enemy alone; a Lothric Knight will descend the steps to confront you. These guys, while not as damaging as the Sword Master, are just as fast and one-up him with a shield and proper armor - you'll be constantly strafing around him to get in your hits where you can, but know that you'll be facing several more of these guys in the future. Additionally, they have a chance to drop pieces of the Lothric Knight Set, which both looks snazzy and will protect you better than your starting armor, so swap in any pieces you get from them right away. Once the coast is clear, Pick up a Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the corpse to the left of the stairs and head up them to enter the next tower, where a Hollow rogue will leap out to attack you!...and promptly go down in a couple swings of your Deep Battle Axe. The doorway on the right will bring you to the top of the tower, where a new Bonfire (Tower on the Wall) awaits. After collecting the Titanite Shard from the corpse to the left of the broken stairs here, light and rest at the Bonfire, then use it to return to Firelink Shrine, where a new, uh, friend awaits you on the side of the middle throne: Ringfinger Leonhard. Talking to him will net you 5 Cracked Red Eye Orbs, which can be used to invade and attack other players (if you're into that). Now, return to the Tower on the Wall and head back down to the room below (waiting for the Lothric Knight to go back outside) before dealing with the rogue again and carefully walking along the beam to collect 3 Firebombs from the corpse at the end. The level below has two more Hollows that'll come at you fast with Throwing Knives and daggers, so take them on one at a time if you can before descending the ladder and dealing with the halberd Hollow below. Through the doorway here, run over to the Hollow behind the barrels and kill him before he can blow them up with a Firebomb, then pick up 8 Throwing Knives from the corpse to the right of the doorway and head through the next arch to take out a rogue to the left, with the corpse in front of the locked door bearing the recurring Mail Breaker.

Remember this area for later and double back to the tower to return to the floor with the two dagger-wielding Hollows, where you'll take the arch out to a landing with another dead wyvern. Once you've collected a Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the body on the right, dispatch the two Hollow soldiers that'll come up to attack you, as well as the two Hollows kneeling next to the wyvern, and go down the ladder to reach the rooftops. See the group of worshipping Hollows in the distance? One of them (raising his arms higher than the others) is another Pus of Man, so run over and kill him ASAP (after switching back to the Long Sword, as otherwise he'll heavily resist the damage you deal) before taking out the rest of them and collecting the 3 Firebombs from the corpse near them. On the other side of the roof, you'll see a proper-size Crystal Lizard in the far-left corner that faces the courtyard, and chasing it down + killing it will reward you with a Raw Gem; nearby, a corpse draped over the edge of the roof holds a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse. Now, descend the ladder and immediately run to the balcony across from the bottom to take out the two Hollow archers and two more soldiers that'll hop up to attack you. At the end is a corpse holding 3 Black Firebombs (stronger versions of the normal Firebombs), and once you've gotten those, double back to the ladder you came down on to pass through the arch next to it, where a Lothric Knight wielding a spear will come in to battle you - aside from his lengthened reach, fighting him requires more or less the same strategy as the last one. After picking up a Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the corner of the room, ignore the doorway that the Lothric Knight came through to pass through the one right next to the arch, where you'll want to immediately dispatch the Hollow soldier on the left and run up the stairs to deal with the archer. When you're ready, break through the pots to kill the Hollow soldier sleeping behind them and pick up 2 Undead Hunter Charms (blocks Estus usage within the area for a limited time). At the top of the stairs, you'll find the room you were overlooking from the sealed door and a rogue on the right, as well as a Hollow soldier that'll climb over the bannister to the left, that you'll want to deal with before collecting a Titanite Shard from the corpse.

Return to the main room and head through the doorway that the Lothric Knight came from to a walkway overlooking a large room filled with Hollow; first, break through some boxes on the right and run to the end of this side path to pick up 2 Green Blossoms (temporarily boosts stamina recovery). On the main walkway, watch out for the Hollow soldier that'll run out from a room on the left and collect a Broadsword from the room once he's gone. Going out the archway and down the stairs here will bring you to a wooden platform with stairs leading down to the floor, but before engaging the enemies down there, run over to the other end of the walkway here to not only kill the rogue and open the (real) chest at the end for a Silver Eagle Kite Shield, but take out the Hollow sitting on the broken end of the platform beyond them, as otherwise he'll start lobbing Firebombs down at you while you're dealing with the rest. With that done, you can head down to the floor and carefully start luring the enemies over to you one at a time - there's two Starved Hounds, a halberd-wielding Hollow, and two axe-wielding Hollows here, so be patient and don't let your guard down till all five are dead. Now that it's safe to do so, go back up both sets of stairs and return to the side path where you picked up the Green Blossoms, where you'll now want to drop off the edge past the corpse and open a chest on the other end of the second-floor walkway that you were cut off from earlier for an Astora Straight Sword (this used to be pretty damn good...till it got nerfed to hell). Drop back down to the ground floor to collect a Titanite Shard from a corpse underneath the stairs, an Estus Shard from a table on the opposite side of the room...and a Cell Key from a body at the bottom of a small set of stairs within the room itself, to the right of the exit. Know what this means? Your first time (of many) backtracking!

Go back up the stairs and retrace your steps through the rooms until you're outside with the wooden platform connecting you to the balcony; climb the ladder here and run across the roofs to the left (jump with L3 to make it onto the flat section at the end) to return to the tower, where you'll want to descend the ladder and head through the archway before turning right at the sealed door to go down the stairs and reach a prison cell holding a single prisoner: Greirat. When spoken to, he'll ask you to deliver a Blue Tearstone Ring (2/107) to an old woman named Loretta in the Undead Settlement beneath the High Wall, with a promise to repay you later, so accept and he'll depart to the Firelink Shrine. Now, at this point, you may very well be out of Estus Flasks and low on HP (like the author in the screenshots above); if so, backtrack to the Tower on the Wall Bonfire, rest at it, and head back down (re-killing enemies as needed) until you're at the balcony with the ladder leading down to the pavilion on the left. Below (past a couple more Hollow soldiers amidst some fallen suits of armor) patrols one of the tougher enemies you'll have to deal with: a Winged Knight, who doesn't stagger, has crazy reach with his halberd, and looooooooves to spam a move where he rapidly spins around with it and moves around the pavilion. Oh, and after he loses enough health, he'll start calling down pillars of light around himself! Real piece of work, this guy - as with the Lothric Knights, your best bet is to constantly strafe around him, wait for him to perform normal attacks (back away if he starts spinning or calling down light), and exploit the couple seconds of recovery he has after his combo to move in and perform a couple of attacks (this is a great enemy to use your Deep Battle Axe's Weapon Art of temporary damage buffing against).

Once this bastard finally goes down, search the surrounding battlefield for a Rapier (with a Hollow soldier sitting nearby) and 2 Embers. Through the archway up the stairs to the side, you'll have a crossbow-wielding one start shooting at you from the right and another Hollow soldier sitting near the stairs he's on. Past the archer, turn right at the top of the stairs to pick up a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the platform at the top; from here, run and jump over to the wooden window cover to pick up a Ring of Sacrifice (3/107). Drop back down to the pavilion and make your way back up the stairs, then go up the other set of stairs beyond the first one, where you'll find a Hollow soldier patrolling the clearing and be attacked by four quick, but otherwise normal Hollows once you engage him (consider retreating to the stairs so they can't surround you). Pick up 3 Green Blossoms from a corpse on the left side of the arch and enter the small tower on the other side to ride an elevator up to a door...that, when opened, will bring you back to the wall with the High Wall of Lothric Bonfire! Rest there and return the way you came to the pavilion, getting the 6 Throwing Knives from the corpse on the upper floor of the elevator as well. Back outside the pavilion and facing the cathedral with the large blue glass circle, pick up the Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the body nearby and look down to see three Lothric Knights patrolling the grounds. Engage them one at a time - dodge through their attacks to end up behind them for a backstab whenever possible - and collect a Lucerne from a corpse on the far side, then go up the stairs to the left of the cathedral entrance to face a stronger variant of the Lothric Knight with blue armor and red eyes; this guy hits harder and has more HP than the others, as well as the ability to enchant his sword for even more damage, BUT you can backstab him while he's waiting in front of the corpses and get in several attacks whenever he begins the enchanting animation, so he's not too hard so long as you wait patiently for his openings. Defeating him will earn you a Refined Gem, as well as (likely) pieces of the Lothric Knight Set.

Ignore the stairs for now and enter the cathedral to speak to Emma, the remaining priestess of the castle. She'll give you instructions on finding the four Lords of Cinder (i.e., reaching the bottom of the High Wall to enter their domains) and give you a Small Lothric Banner to raise in order to pass through the gate...and talking to her for a second time will reward you with the Way of Blue item, granting you access to the covenant of the same name that summons allied players to defend you when invaded! Now head down the stairs, take out the archer on the landing to the right just before the bottom, and dispatch the two spear-wielding Hollows before pausing in front of the gate below. If you've died and haven't already done so in the intervening time, use an Ember and you'll see a golden summon sign for the Sword Master since you defeated him earlier - bring him out if you want (he won't last long) and run up to the broken gate to face the boss everyone knows by his OST: Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Know what's not fun to deal with? A raging man-beast clad in full armor and inflicting frostbite with every attack to slow you down and decrease your defense. Remarkably, though, it's actually safer to stay close to him than to keep your distance (for the most part): in his first phase, Vordt attacks exclusively with swings of his giant mace, and while these DO hurt, they also won't hit you if you're staying close to or behind him (where you'll want to perform most of your attacks.) Per the tradition this game is setting, he'll go berserk at 50% HP and start performing fast, high-damage charges across the arena, as well as the occasional charged-up breath of frost that'll pan across a wide area. Obviously, dodge out of the way of the former - for the latter, get some attacks in if you're close, but otherwise, run the hell away so you don't get caught by the beam, and you should be fine in this phase as well. Vordt is tough for sure, but manageable once you know the nuances of his phases.

Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Vordt of the Boreal Valley For your troubles, you'll receive the Soul of Boreal Valley Vordt (do not consume this!)... ...and a new Bonfire (Vordt of the Boreal Valley). Rest here and return to the Firelink Shrine, where you're going to accomplish quite a few things.

Here, use all your regular Soul Chunks (again, leaving Vordt's alone) and raise your Ashen One to level 21 with the following specifications: With that done, head to the Handmaid and consider selling items you won't be using (such as the Cracked Red Eye Orbs) - the author got up to 4,756 Souls this way - before running over to Andre and Reinforcing your Estus Flask with the Estus Shard you found, bringing the total you can use up to 5. Now, it's time for the first of a few grinds; Travel to the Tower on the Wall Bonfire and: 1. Head down the stairs to the top floor with the thief and the crates, where the Lothric Knight will walk outside. 2. Kill the rogue and the Lothric Knight. 3. Go back up the stairs and rest at the Bonfire. You're going to be repeating these three steps - acquiring 250 Souls each time - until you're sitting pretty at 20,000 Souls, which will also help you get better at battling enemy knights AND likely get you the entire Lothric Knight Set to replace your starting armor (you can sell excess pieces to the Handmaid for 300 Souls each, as well as the extra Embers and weapons they'll sometimes drop for 1,000 and 500 Souls respectively, to speed up this process). Once you're done, return to the Firelink Shrine, purchase the Tower Key from the Handmaid, and head up the stairs to the left of the shrine entrance to reach the tower behind the Giant tree. After opening the door, ascend the spiral staircase and carefully cross the crumbling bridge to the other side, where an elevator will take you even higher within the shrine. At the top of the stairs here, you'll find the pitiable corpse of a Fire Keeper long past with a Fire Keeper Soul- this is used to avert one of the endings of the game, so you won't have reason to use it, but it's certainly interesting for the lore. Once you take the elevator back down, look into the pit below the short bridge on the right side, where you'll see an item lighting up a corpse among the coffins; this is the Fire Keeper Set, and it's most easily reached by de-equipping your Deep Battle Axe with , then running off the edge of the bridge toward the corner where the item is and pressing R1 to perform a falling attack with your bare fist, which will land you squarely on the coffin without sliding off (thanks to the Fextralife page for the set for this strategy!). From here, simply drop to the floor and pick up the Estus Ring (4/107) from a pile of Fire Keeper corpses (equip this immediately, as it'll increase how much HP every Estus Flask restores!).

Now, exit through the door (where you would have had to face the Sword Master if you hadn't already killed him) and return to the crumbling bridge outside, where you can drop onto a lower portion of the middle pillar to reach the roof without killing yourself. On the left side of this, kick down the ladder connecting to the base of the tower; then, drop off the other end of the roof and run around the back to kill the Crystal Lizard for a Twinkling Titanite. On the edge of the roof, you'll see yet another large nest - this is indeed for THIS game's incarnation of the item-trading and unseen crow girl, Pickle-pee Pump-a-rum! Uniquely to this game, you can only trade in each kind of item once, which is a shame since there's some good stuff to get - but just like in Dark Souls I, the results are guaranteed, so you'll never waste anything. For now, leave a Firebomb to get a Large Titanite Shard and drop off the edge of the roof facing the tower to reach a corpse holding 3 Homeward Bones on an encircling ledge, then run around toward the "front" of the ledge and re-enter the shrine through a small arch in the wall. By carefully walking along one of the three walkways connecting in the center of this area (where Pickle-pee will address you again), you can reach a corpse carrying another Estus Shard...then head down the walkway that leads right into a wall and attack that wall, which will disappear (hello, first illusionary wall of the game!), letting you walk to the edge of the walkway behind it, drop down, and open a chest to the right for the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring (5/107), which you're going to also immediately equip since it increases how many Souls you get for defeating enemies (this will, unfortunately, put you just over the 70% equipment load threshold, so you may want to unequip your helmet for now to preserve your roll).

From here, drop down to the area behind the main throne, return to Andre to Reinforce your Estus Flask up to 6, and Travel back to the Bonfire you came here from to advance through the open doors. At the edge of the path, press to raise the Small Lothric Banner...and none other than a few Batwing Demons will crawl up to fly you down to the Undead Settlement!

First and foremost, light the Bonfire (Foot of the High Wall) and look around at the massive area you'll be traveling through here. After walking down the stairs, head over to the other platform on this level and pick up a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse, then descend the rest of the stairs toward the road below, where the gate will open suddenly to release three Starved Hounds to attack the praying Hollows and then you; they can be a bit tough to field all at once, but there's a chance that one or two will die from being crushed under the gate when it goes back down, so let's hope that happens in your run too. Behind a fallen carriage on this side of the gate, you'll find two more Starved Hounds chewing on a corpse carrying 2 Alluring Skulls (draws weak enemies to the location where they're thrown). Now, head into the sea of dead pilgrims...and on the right side, you'll find one that hasn't petrified: Yoel of Londor. Excuse the sudden change in equipment - the author had to get these screenshots on the second playthrough. This guy is actually very important for the third and most secret ending of the game - but since you're not aiming for that until the third and final playthrough, for now, he's just a friendly yet weird guy. Talk to him, and he'll offer to pledge himself in service to you; accept this, and he'll teleport to the Firelink Shrine. After picking up two Homeward Bones from a corpse on the far corner of the broken bridge, return to the Firelink Shrine for a second and find him at the end of a passage (go down the stairs past where Hawkwood usually sits, then turn left), where talking to him will give you a new gesture, "Beckon" (11/33). Go back to the Foot of the High Wall, take out the Starved Dogs, and pull the lever to raise the gate, beyond which lies...well, another Bonfire (Undead Settlement). This will respawn the Peasant Hollow that was opening and closing the gate at the

other lever, so kill him and head down the road to face two more, who attack slow enough that you shouldn't have any trouble taking them out. At the end of the path, head inside the building to find what's definitely not the set of a horror movie. Attacking the wriggling body on the right will let you pick up a Small Leather Shield, and destroying the crates nearby will let you go up the stairs to get the jump on a Thrall, who would otherwise be leaping at you like a rogue (and who might do so anyway even as you walk up behind him!), though he's otherwise pretty weak. Drop down to the floor below and pick up 2 Charcoal Pine Bundles (a variant of the Pine Resins that quickly applies fire to your weapon...but only for 10 seconds) from a corpse on the other end of the room, then head onto the balcony to see the mob that's awaiting you outside and cut down a hanging body with an item you'll collect soon. Around the corner of the balcony to the right, cut down the Peasant Hollow that's waiting for you and collect 2 Repair Powders from the corpse behind him. Return to the building and descend to the ground floor, where three Thralls are lying in wait for you; once they're gone, pick up another 2 Charcoal Pine Bundles from the corpse in the corner and walk down the stairs into a hall leading out of the building, where you'll be on the ground level with the mobs of enemies surrounding the burning tree that you saw earlier. You can take out five of these Peasant Hollows by slowly walking over to the groups standing in front of barrels - these can be detonated, killing them instantly, by throwing a Firebomb at them from close range. Once they're gone, engage the remaining Peasant Hollows who are standing up (the kneeling ones won't attack you until you damage them), and prepare to deal with the tough enemy of this area: the Evangelist, a.k.a. the fat lady in front of the tree. This enemy (and there are quite a few more like her) is stronger than the damned Winged Knights, to give you an idea; they have just as long a range with their mace and their attacks hit just as hard, but they also have even more HP and are just about impossible to stagger while ALSO having a ranged projectile attack (in the form of Gnaw) and a grab move where she speaks plain English, sets herself on fire, and lunges toward you for MASSIVE damage. Prepare to take quite a bit of damage while engaging her.

Once the coast is clear, it's time to loot the place - the corpse you knocked down earlier holds Loretta's Bone (yes, THAT Loretta whom Greirat wanted us to find...yeahhhhh, get ready for a lot of sad endings in this game), while a body at the bottom of the tree (where the Evangelist was sitting) bears an Estus Shard. Past the former location of the second pile of barrels, a corpse pinned underneath a gate holds a Soul of an Unknown Traveler, while the body on the other side of the tree contains an Ember. Lastly, equip your Longbow and shoot down (by two-handing with and aiming with L1 , then releasing the arrow with R1 ) the body with an item glow that's hanging from the tree, and you can pick up 9 Kukri (throwing item that builds up Bleed). From this open area, you'll see three paths leading onward: a bridge to the right, a tunnel running along the edge of the cliff to the left, and a gap between buildings to the left of the tunnel. You'll be entering the tunnel first to dispatch two Thralls that were waiting to jump down on you - then, head back outside and onto the ledge to the right to collect a Titanite Shard before entering the gap between the buildings. Opening the wooden door here will bring you to a room filled with hanging corpses and cages stuffed with bodies, on the far wall of which sits a body with an item; however, if you look carefully at the cage next to it, you'll see that the limbs sticking out from between the bars are moving... and that it can be locked onto with R3 , because this is ACTUALLY an enemy, a Cage Spider, that'll attack you once you get close enough, though you can easily kill it with a single charged (held) R2 attack. Collect the 2 Charcoal Pine Resins (at last!) from next to it and cut down the corpse hanging over the nearby stairs to pick up a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse, then walk over to the opposite side of the room and drop through the hole in the floor to reach a hidden chamber with a couple interesting things: a pot of Estus Soup that'll completely refill your HP (one time only, but refills whenever you rest at a Bonfire or die) and a talisman for the Warrior of Sunlight covenant (lets you leave your summon sign for other players to use in jolly cooperation for boss battles)!

After exiting this chamber through the door, prepare to deal with more Cage Spiders and a red-eyed Peasant Hollow that'll come at you from the end of this hall with a pair of sickles and some really fast attacks - wait until he's completed a combo to start your own. Beyond the hall, you'll find yourself in a long alleyway with several more Peasant Hollows and another Evangelist standing on a bridge further down who'll start hurling more Gnaws at you the second that you enter her line of sight; the best way of proceeding is luring one Peasant Hollow at a time back to the hall exit and taking him out there, out of the range of the Evangelist. During this process, destroy the crates and rubble blocking the gap between the hall and the adjoining building to reach a cliffside pathway, at the end of which lies a corpse holding a Soul of an Unknown Traveler. When the stairs appear to be clear, head down, hugging the right side in case you need to duck behind a wall or into a room to avoid the Gnaws, and upon reaching a doorway covered in boards on the left, a Peasant Hollow will burst through. Take him out and run into the room, then kill the Thrall and pick up the Whip from the corpse before rushing out to dispatch the Peasant Hollow patrolling the flat area nearby. With that done, head down the side path and around the wall at the end to reach a corpse carrying another Titanite Shard. As for the Evangelist, she'll hopefully drop down off the bridge to attack you on the ground - otherwise, a ladder to the left on the other side of the bridge will bring you to her (and yet another Titanite Shard-bearing corpse). Down the stairs past this, if you're still Enkindled, you'll be invaded by your first mad spirit who'll possibly give you an even harder time than Gundyr and Vordt: Holy Knight Hodrick. This bastard not only loves to hit-and-run with a greatsword and rolls, he ALSO uses miracles that gradually heal himself (and you, in the case of the orb he creates) over time...AND he'll use and abuse Estus Flasks like there's no tomorrow if you give him the chance. Oh, and he can actually parry and riposte you as you can do to other enemies, so...yeah, huge pain in the ass. The author found that constant, constant offense was the best defense against him, both to interrupt his healing animations and to counteract the constant healing from his orb once he got it set up; spamming the Deep Battle Axe's Weapon Art is also critical here. For your troubles, you'll receive a Vertebra Shackle, an item that you'll need 30 of for a certain covenant later, as well as 3 Estus Flasks.

Outside (hopefully, he didn't come to gang up on you with Hodrick), you'll encounter your first Hollow Manservant, a hulking jackass who wields a large saw like a guillotine blade and likes to unleash up to 6 attacks in a row - like the Evangelists, he's basically impossible to stagger, so focus instead on rolling behind him as he begins his combos and attacking him while he can't turn around, then backing up to repeat the process. When he's gone, you'll be free to run up the path with the wooden fence and kill a Crystal Lizard for a Sharp Gem, then double back to the alley with the (ideally, but not necessarily) formerly alive Evangelist, where running up the slanted roof to the side of the stairs will let you jump off to a wooden balcony with more broken stairs and collect 2 Rusted Coins (temporarily boosts item discovery) from a corpse. Then, at last, you can drop down and light the nearby Bonfire (Dilapidated Bridge). Now, Travel to the Undead Settlement Bonfire and retrace your steps to the burning tree; it's time to cross the bridge here (you can reach it and NOT alert the enemies here if you just hug the right side of the open area). After dispatching the two Peasant Hollows that cross the bridge toward you, look to the right of the entrance and you'll find a cliffside path behind some breakable crates that leads to a set of wooden houses, where a quintuplet of Thralls wait for you - and two of them are wielding blowdarts! What you'll want to do is run toward the rock wall and draw out the first Thrall, then kill him while the wall shields you from the Thralls on the roofs; then, rush ahead and engage the two Thralls on the ground so you can lure them back behind the wall. When all three are dead, run up the sloped roof to the left to take out the first blowdart Thrall (as well as a companion of his on the adjoining rooftop) before climbing the nearby ladder to dispatch the other, which will leave you free to loot the area. On the other end of the roof you're currently on, a corpse draped over a ledge carries 2 Homeward Bones - then, a body in front of the ladder has a Fading Soul, while the corpse in the path winding around the left of this same house bears a Plank Shield. To the right of it, you'll see another Cage Spider...but he's not a foe and will actually talk to you if you go up to him, though his words are extremely cryptic and meant to lead us to a certain covenant soon. Finally, pick up 6 Firebombs from the roof of the house past the stables, and you'll be done here.

Go back up the ladder and drop off the right side of the roof so you can head down the path here to another Hollow Manservant...but unlike the last, he's ALSO not hostile and, in fact, has a good use. Before doing anything with him, though, carefully walk onto the stones below the corpse hanging from the tree at the end of the path and position yourself so you're standing between the corpse and the open air, as pictured: Why the precision? Well, when you cut this down with an attack, it'll be sent flying in the direction of your attack - and if you were to do so from the path, it'd fall right in front of the cathedral below, which is a fatal drop if you tried to get down there immediately. Plus, you want to stay up on the path! So knock the corpse down and collect the Flame Stoneplate Ring (6/107) (reduces fire damage taken) from it, then go over to the Hollow Manservant and press to be transported to a massive pit in a cutscene. Here, running over to the far shore with its candles will bring you to the guy that was kicking your butt earlier: Holy Knight Hodrick. Talking to him three times will give you quite a bit; he'll tell you that this place is for people piling up "shackles of the gods" (a.k.a. Vertebra Shackles) and give you not only a Homeward Bone to get out of there with, but the Mound-maker item to join said covenant with! Now, you won't be able to advance in this covenant for quite some time, but keep it in mind as it's the source of a couple spells you'll need later. For now, collect the Wargod Wooden Shield from the corpse to the right and use a Homeward Bone to leave (returning to the last Bonfire rested at).

From said Bonfire, retrace your steps across the bridge, where you're ACTUALLY going to enter the stables this time. Once you're in, kill the two Peasant Hollows slumped down inside on the right and collect the Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse from the body on the left. Advancing into the next building will cause a Thrall wielding a greatsword to drop down from the rafters in front of you -he's got over three times as much HP as normal ones do and hits quite a bit harder due to his choice of weapon, but if you lay into him with an R1 combo right away, he'll go down without putting you in danger. Open the door here and collect the Caduceus Round Shield from a corpse on the right before looking over the bridge to the left to see an even more ominous section of the village. Here, to avoid getting pelted with a ton of Firebombs and blown up by the barrels strewn about the area, you're going to be crossing the bridge partway and beating the enemies to the punch by throwing one of YOUR Firebombs at the cluster of barrels on the other end, blowing up a few Hollows and letting you head across to the pavilion . Here, hug the right side by running on the rocks, and when you reach the corner of the building there, drop down (or get knocked down, in the author's case) to the path below, where two Peasant Hollows are patrolling. Take them out as fast as you can and collect a Titanite Shard from a corpse underneath the bridge, then double back and enter the building at the other end of the path to reach the next Bonfire (Cliff Underside). From this, head outside and turn right to reach the roof of the building, where you can shoot down a corpse hanging off the side of the tower ahead with your Longbow to pick up the ever-recurring Partizan (you can switch to this for now if you want to counter the longer ranges of the enemies in this area), then proceed through the towers and kill the three Hollow Peasants that were pelting you from above.

At the end of this walkway, you'll reach a man in a cage - better known as this game's pyromancy teacher, Cornyx of the Great Swamp! Talk to him and Ask to learn pyromancy, and Cornyx will teleport to the Firelink Shrine to become a vendor for that very art. In fact, while he's fresh in your mind, return there yourself and speak to him twice (to the right of Andre); this will result him giving you your first Pyromancy Flame and his gesture, "Welcome" (12/33). Additionally, you'll want to head over to Greirat and choose to Give Loretta's Bone to him - he'll accept this and let you keep the Blue Tearstone Ring, but once you exit and resume the game though the menu, he'll be in a fetal position, and talking to him again will teach you his gesture, "Curl Up" (13/33). Return to the Cliff Underside, take out the three Peasant Hollows again so they won't be pestering you, and drop down from the side-rooftop next to the long one to engage a third Hollow Manservant (the author found out the hard way that the Partizan doesn't do much damage to these guys, so consider switching back to the Deep Battle Axe for this one). In the pavilion beyond, there's a Soul of an Unknown Traveler on the torture platform, and at the end of a crumbling bridge past it, there's a corpse (underneath a Hollow) that's bearing a Fire Clutch Ring (7/107) (increases fire damage, but decreases defense). Now, walk down the long set of stairs that the Hollow Manservant was on, killing the Hollows as you go, and before descending the next set of stairs into the valley below, turn left and head up a small cliffside path to the right of a house to collect a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse (and also be attacked by another Thrall). As for the valley itself, there are two Starved Dogs, three Peasant Hollows, and an Evangelist spread across the area - you'll want to engage them one at a time if you can, saving the Evangelist for last (if she doesn't fall down into the not-bottomless pit below) and collecting an Ember from a corpse behind a tree next to the large set of stairs as well. You're going to ignore those stairs for now and instead head to the short bridge at the other end of the valley, then enter the arch on the right to reach a sewer area with rodents of unusual size. Since these are easy to kill, keep going and pick up a Caestus from the body in the water, then cautiously approach the fog for a LARGE rat to come out swinging. It'll take you about 4-5 hits to kill this thing, but you'll be rewarded with the Bloodbite Ring (8/107) (increases bleed resistance, worth equipping right away) for doing so.

Climb the ladder at the end and open the door here to return to (and rest at) the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire so you can backtrack to the small bridge (clearing out whatever enemies you need to along the way) and begin slowly crossing it: first, a Peasant Hollow on the other side will approach... followed by TWO HOLLOW MANSERVANTS AT ONCE, in another stunning display of fairness from FromSoftware. You'll want to run back along the valley to try and get them to separate - easier if you get one of them to throw their bowl at you, which will cause them to break out their blade and start sprinting - because taking on both simultaneously is way more trouble than you need right now. When they're both dealt with, fully cross the bridge (picking up the Ember there along the way) and take out the remaining Hollow Manservant on the other side; up the stairs next to him lies a corpse with a Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse and two Starved Dogs standing between you and a corpse with 3 Alluring Skulls behind the house itself. With that done, head along the path connected to the bridge toward the large tower you saw in the distance earlier - there's a Giant with a bow and equally massive arrows at the top of it, but he won't shoot down at you here (though he WOULD be if you'd gone to other areas earlier). On your left, you'll meet a new NPC: Eygon of Carim. He's kind of a douche, but he won't attack you, and you can talk to him twice and receive some mildly cryptic advice. There's a cell to his left that you can't open yet, so open the doors to the tower for now and enter the main chamber. Here, you'll see an elevator in the center that'll start going up as you approach it...delivering another new NPC that's simultaneously all too familiar:

Siegward of Catarina! Just like your dearly departed Siegmeyer from the first game, Siegward is in a bit of a pickle here; like you, he's trying to reach the top of the tower, but he's stuck on an elevator that only goes down from this floor. The solution, of course, is to step on the elevator trigger and quickly run off, dropping it and bringing the elevator ABOVE it down so you can ride that to the top floor, where a corpse on the side of the room opposite the stairs holds a Soul of a Nameless Soldier for you. The stairs will bring you to the top of the tower, where the Giant awaits - and unfortunately for him, he has a ring that you need. You can get this by completing an unmarked questline involving collecting a bunch of items from three different areas in the game, but it's not easy to find them; the simpler and much faster option, painful as it might be, is to kill him here and now (for less emotional trauma, don't talk to him first) for the Hawk Ring (9/107). He'll be a helpful ally in NG+ and beyond, rest assured! Go back down with the elevator (which will make Siegward move on) and return to the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire, where now it's time to proceed through the stone arch into the veritable forest of massive arrows beyond - if you hadn't killed the Giant Archer earlier (or befriended him, as you'll do in the next two playthroughs), you'd be getting pelted with these same arrows while ALSO dealing with the eight Peasant Hollows in here, so you've made your life easier for now by eliminating that first risk. This graveyard has a ton of loot for you to grab: an Ember, Fading Soul, Reinforced Club, Large Soul of a Deserted Corpse, and 3 Young White Branches around a white tree in the center (part of the Giant Archer's questline), while the broken chunk of earth nearby - reached by jumping -bears your first Undead Bone Shard (increases the potency of your Estus Flask, VERY important).

Jump back to the mainland and turn left at the building at the other end of the graveyard to reach the upper area, where a corpse on a wooden deck holds the Cleric Set (along with another greatsword-wielding Thrall that'll drop onto you once you pick it up) and a body to the left of it holds the Mortician's Ashes, which you can use to get new items from the Handmaid. Inside the building here, there'll be another normal Peasant Hollow that lunges at you through the doorway, as well as a red-eyed one sitting at the other end of the room (rushing over to attack him as fast as possible is a pretty safe strategy). Going up the stairs here and jumping to the broken section of the floor from the platform at the top of the steps will lead you to a Great Scythe; the hallway here leads to the next boss fight, but you're only going to go as far as the door within it and open that, creating a shortcut back to the arena that you'll use later, Now, return to the Bonfire and Travel to the Firelink Shrine so you can hand the Mortician's Ashes over to the Handmaid (via the Give umbral ashes option), which will let you buy the Grave Key from her for 1,500 Souls -while you're here and flush with cash, you may as well get Heal Aid (1/35) for 500 Souls too. Talk to Ludleth if you'd like for a hint at a future questline, then give the Estus Shard to Andre and burn the Undead Bone Shard in the Bonfire to go up to 7 Estus Flask+1. With all that done, return to the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire and double back into the sewer; this time, you'll be opening the gate in the illuminated archway here, which will bring you to a misty tunnel. To the right, you'll find a Loincloth next to a statue of Velka, which can be prayed to if you ever aggro an NPC by attacking them in order to make them neutral again; the opposite path will bring you to another doorway, to the left of which is a corpse with a Red Hilted Halberd. Past this doorway, you'll begin encountering Skeletons, which can be killed by any kind of damage this time around but are still a pain in the butt - to avoid getting ganged up on by a bunch of them at once, rush through the catacombs, stopping only to pick up the Soul of an Unknown Traveler, and into the rocky crevasse beneath the small bridge, where turning right will let you pursue another

Crystal Lizard for a Heavy Gem. However, you'll ALSO have to contend with one of the Manservant Hollows from above, who'll drop down to attack you once you go far enough (thankfully, he'll take some damage from doing so). Collect the 2 Titanite Shards from the corpses and head into the adjoining crevasse, where you can shoot down a hanging corpse just before the doorway on the left to pick up a Blessed Red & White Shield+1. Through the doorway, you'll drop into a room with a single patrolling rat, which will seem familiar to anyone who played the second game; as soon as you start attacking him, a whole BUNCH more rats will start pouring out of the walls. It's up to you if you want to engage them all in melee or climb up the entrance ladder and hurl Firebombs down at them, but when the coast is clear, you can pick up the Saint's Talisman in the corner and climb the ladder next to it to reach the interior of the cell mentioned earlier, where a new NPC awaits: Irina of Carim. This poor girl needs you to prove that you're real and not another illusion, so when talking to her, choose to Touch her, and she'll reward you with her gesture, "Prayer" (14/33). Talk to her again and choose to Accept her service, and she'll teleport to the Firelink Shrine in order to become your miracles vendor! Open the gate to the outside and talk to Eygon, who'll begrudgingly agree to ally with you (e.g., let himself be summoned for some future bosses) for as long as you assure Irina's safety, and use the elevator inside the tower to head up...and walk OFF of it halfway through to land on a wooden walkway, where Siegward has ventured. Talking to him, you'll have your attention drawn to the Fire Demon stalking the burning village below...and though Siegward may claim to be too scared to face it, dropping down to start hacking at its shins will make him demonstrate his true bravery by joining you for some jolly cooperation. The Fire Demon itself has the HP and attack strength of a boss, but Siegward and his mighty miracles do a good job of keeping its attention while you cut down its health; staying close to it (ideally between its legs) is the safest place to evade its sweeping axe attacks, though it can still knock you down with some radial effects.

Once the demon is vanquished (earning you a Fire Gem), talking to Siegward will result in him making a hearty toast to you, giving you not only a flagon of his trademark Siegbräu, but also his gesture, "Toast" (15/33) - talking to him twice more after this will prompt him to take a nap and let you learn THAT gesture, "Nap" (16/33). From here, pick up a Homeward Bone from a corpse draped over the cliff near the roof you dropped onto and shoot down the two item-bearing corpses flanking a triangular rooftop near the big bonfire in the town square to collect not only the Northern Set, but a Pale Tongue, which is ANOTHER covenant item that you'll have to grind for later. With a Large Club available at the foot of a nearby tree, use a Homeward Bone to return to Firelink Shrine and talk to Leonhard next to the throne, where he'll tell you that you can acquire an uncracked Red Eye Orb by killing the Darkwraith in the deepest cell in Lothric. With the Tower Lift Key that he gives you, Travel to the Tower on the Wall Bonfire in the High Wall of Lothric and head down to the bottom floor, where you can now unlock the gate behind the ladder and descend the lift; along the way, you'll want to equip your Longbow to cheese the hell out of this guy. At the bottom, in a cell lined with empty and broken suits of armor, the Darkwraith will be waiting for you - this fucker hits HARD and fast too, so...we're NOT going to take him on legitimately! Instead, stand right in front of the elevator, aim at him with your Longbow, and hit him with an arrow to get his attention; then, when he's running at you through the archway, step back on the lift and ride it up. If you time this right, the Darkwraith will perform a lunging attack that pushes him over the edge of the pit underneath the lift, and like Wile E. Coyote, he'll proceed to fall to his death, netting you almost 3,000 Souls and the Red Eye Orb (this is also a decent early-game farming spot for Souls if you want to put in the time for it). Victorious, you can now return to Leonhard, who'll reward you with his gesture, "Applause" (17/33), as well as an invitation to join the Cathedral of the Deep...hoo boy.

Now, Travel to the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire, then make your way back to the area that you fought the Fire Demon in and head into the stables between the cliff and the pyre - with a bunch of inert Cage Spiders hanging from the ceiling - to acquire 2 Red Bug Pellets (temporarily reduces fire damage taken). Up the stairs and around the corner, you'll see a corpse holding 2 Alluring Skulls, but two of the Cage Spiders above will drop down and attack when you head over to get it, so be careful. Through the hallway here, there's another Cage Spider on the left side for you to take out with a charged R2 attack, and the broken wall to the right hides two Starved Dogs that'll run out to attack you as you kill the former, though you can hilariously knock them off the building if you properly aim and time your attacks while they're near the ledge. Beyond this broken wall, there's a chest to open...but once you do, FOUR Cage Spiders will drop down from the ceiling, so roll out through the wall and kill them one at a time with charged R2 attacks, then collect 4 Human Pine Resins (applies dark damage to your weapon...gross) from the chest. Up the stairs, you'll be confronted with not one, but TWO Evangelists all too happy to mess you up together; feel free to start this off by lobbing a few Firebombs at them to get splash damage in on both, then do your best to lure one down the stairs/off the ledge to split them up and start carving them up. Outside, ascend the stairs and climb the scaffolding on the roof to find Flynn's Ring (10/107) (increases attack power as you decrease your equipment load), then face the cathedral and drop off the edge of the roof near the tower to land on a wooden platform, which you can then walk off of onto the tower itself. On the far side of the tower balcony, you'll find a corpse with 2 Homeward Bones to replace what you used earlier, and inside the tower, you'll have to run off the edge of the platform to a narrow set of wooden beams, then onto the floor to avoid taking too much fall damage; here, you can pick up the Mirrah Set (the headpiece is available as an optional trade with Picklepum) and the Chloranthy Ring (11/107) (raises stamina recovery speed, swap the Bloodbite Ring out for this one right now!)

Through the archway on this floor, turning right will bring you to the top of the stairs you were ignoring earlier...and since you've already opened the door, head through it to reach the arena of the Curse-rotted Greatwood. You'll have some time before engaging the actual boss, so walk over toward the bulbous tree in the corner, where you'll see seven Peasant Hollows kneeling in worship around it. Starting from the right side (with the red-eyed one), dispatch these enemies one at a time, and when all but the last Curse-rotted Greatwood (closest to the tree) are gone, approach the last one, which will alert both it and the Curse-rotted Greatwood - take out the Peasant Hollow and prepare to deal with the boss. The Curse-rotted Greatwood is slow-moving, but don't let that fool you into thinking he'll be easy -his long limbs mean it's very easy for his strikes to hit you, and if you stay close all the time, he'll just start lifting himself in the air and dropping himself onto you butt-first. Additionally, most of his body is invulnerable to damage; you actually have to focus on the gross white sacs found on his crotch, back, ankles, thighs, and wrists, which will pop and take off huge chunks of his HP once you attack them enough times. The trick here is to be constantly circling around the Curse-rotted Greatwood, focusing first on his limbs and then on his crotch, to avoid being caught up in his sweeping strikes and largely evade his radial attacks (shaking the limbs of his branches to drop acidic projectiles), as well as stay away from the additional Peasant Hollows that'll drop into the arena (and promptly be crushed by the object of their adoration). At 50% HP, the Curse-rotted Greatwood will lift himself up and stomp the ground hard enough to break it, dropping both of you into the pit you visited earlier to join the Mound-makers in! Oh, and this will also kill that asshole Hodric, so be glad you talked to him and got the trophy earlier. Now, the Curse-rotted Greatwood will sprout a creepily long and thin white arm/shoulder from its chest that'll perform even faster strikes and grabbing attacks (in fact, the whole body will be moving and turning faster in this second phase), so you're going to be leaving the new set of pustules on his crotch (below the arm) for last - instead, focus on the pustules on the Curse-rotted Greatwood's back and right elbow (when he stands up and falls over) to get him to the last 5% of his HP before moving to attack his crotch again. You're liable to get grabbed and thrown down a few times while doing so if you just attack continuously, so either be prepared to heal or cycle between getting a few attacks in and running away just as the grabbing animation begins; either way, this should only take about 7 more strikes to finish.

Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the gross tree getting cut down to size, you'll receive the Soul of the Rotted Greatwood, which can be consumed... ...and the Transposing Kiln, a.k.a. the item that Ludleth wanted. You'll also get a convenient Bonfire (Pit of Hollows) down here - use it to return to the Firelink Shrine, where you have some things to do.

First things first, talk to Hawkwood, who now has new dialogue - alongside some dreadful lore about Aldrich and a tip on where to go next, he'll give you a Heavy Gem. Next, head up to Ludleth and give him the Transposing Kiln, which will allow you to transpose the Soul of Boreal Valley Vordt into the Pontiff's Left Eye (12/107) for free! Now, head to Greirat, who'll offer to go steal stuff for you - choose to Send him out to pillage, and his questline will advance. Turn left from here and walk over to Yoel, from whom you'll want to buy your first sorceries: Soul Arrow (1/34) Heavy Soul Arrow (2/34) This'll cost you 3,000 Souls, though you'll make that back just by consuming the boss soul that you picked up from the last fight. From here, go to Cornyx and purchase your first pyromancies: Fireball (1/27) Fire Surge (2/27) Great Combustion (3/27) Flash Sweat (4/27) This'll total to 6,500 Souls - it's the only place to get them, unfortunately. Now, turn right to find Irina at the end of a hall, from whom you should now buy the following miracles: Heal (2/35) Replenishment (3/35) Caressing Tears (4/35) Homeward (5/35) This'll run you another 6,500 Souls, but Irina is, as with Cornyx, the only place you can get them from, so you've got to bite the bullet here. While you're here, you should also purchase the Saint's Ring (13/107) (which adds an additional spell slot) from her. With all that done, use your Soul Chunks (which should raise you back up to almost 32,000 Souls) and raise your Ashen One to level 28 with the following specifications: If you're curious, you're raising INT so you can bring an NPC in the next area home with us, VIT to go back to wearing a helmet (and not worry as much about the granularity of ring weight)...and DEX to turn on easy mode with a weapon you're going to pick up soon. Now, return to the tower (from the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire) and take the lift down this time to a hidden chamber, where a new and not-fun enemy awaits: the Boreal Outrider Knight. This guy is basically a smaller and way faster version of Vordt, and he's not worth taking on legitimately - instead, you'll want to quickly pick up the Ember here and run right past him to open the large wooden doors, which will let you go outside...but prevent him from following, since his AI doesn't let him go through the doorway. From here, the slow and safe method is to wait for him to attack a couple of times and turn around to begin walking away, at which point you can run in to attack his butt and then run back out to repeat the process. For your trouble, he'll drop the Irithyll Straight Sword (which you can immediately swap your Deep Axe out for, as its stats and attacks are pretty much objectively better - thanks, meschejre!)...and you'll be on the Road of Sacrifices.

Light and rest at the Bonfire (Road of Sacrifices), then proceed down the path to encounter your first Corvian - crow-like enemies that seem meek at first, right until wings rip out of their backs and they start clawing at you. They'll take about 6 hits to take down, so keep an eye on your stamina and be ready to roll as needed. Look over the ledge to your left and drop down onto the next one, then collect the Shriving Stone (unique in that it reverses infusion of any element without lowering the weapon's reinforcement level). Up the slope from here, run off the edge and drop attack the Corvian huddled below before returning to the main path, where you'll see not only two regular Corvians ahead, but a staff-wielding one to the left; this is a Corvian Shaman, and they've got a whole host of tricks up their sleeves, including the ability to generate poison clouds AND a bird screech that automatically transforms all nearby Corvians to set them on you. To avoid dealing with either of these, hug the left side of the clearing to avoid drawing the aggro of the two normal Corvians and rush toward the Shaman, then attack him rapidly - each strike with the Deep Battle Axe should stagger him enough that he won't be able to perform any attacks. With the coast clear, pick up the Soul of an Unknown Traveler from behind the overturned wagon here, and head past the corpse of the shaman to drop off a short ledge, where you'll want to head through the arch and turn left up the slope to reach the top of the arch. You'll see one Corvian patrolling as normal and another lying down, seemingly dead - it is not, so hit the bastard with a charged R2 attack and get your licks in while he's still transforming before dealing with the other one. Retrieve the Titanite Shard from beyond them and return to the road leading into the arch, where taking the path down underneath the cliff will get you into a confrontation with this game's incarnation of the recurring female marshland cannibal, Isabella the Mad, who wields the Butcher's Knife that restores her HP with each hit and has quite a bit of range to it. She's annoying

to deal with at close range, so your best bet is landing single R2 attacks in-between rolling around and away from her to avoid that damn blade as best you can. Once Isabella goes down, you'll receive the same Butcher's Knife and can retrieve the Brigand Set, as well as Brigand Quickdaggers and Brigand Axe, from the corpses behind her. With that done, return to the arch and approach the bridge beyond it, but don't cross yet; you'll see a lone Corvian on it...and a Corvian Shaman behind him that'll shriek and transform a whole row of Corvians on the other side of the bridge if you get too close. The trick here is to take out just the lone Corvian first when he transforms and rushes over, then provoke the Shaman into transforming the others and run back to the top of the arch so you can force them to fight you single-file and ideally one at a time, more or less. Once that's done, kill the Shaman, collect the Ember he was guarding, and return to the other side of the bridge to drop down to a ledge below it on the right side, where two Starved Dogs (and potentially another Corvian) are waiting for you with quite a bit more HP than the ones you've faced previously - kill them both and collect not only Morne's Ring (14/107) (increases miracle power), but the Braille Divine Tome of Carim, which you'll be giving to dear Irina later. With all that done, head up the path on the other side of this cavern and drop down where the Corvians were. Through the arch behind them, you'll reach the next Bonfire (Halfway Fortress) and meet TWO new NPCs: Anri of Astora (left) and Horace the Hushed (right). Talking to Anri will give you some insight about the next leg of your journey...and "talking" to Horace will get you the Blue Sentinel covenant item, allowing you to be summoned to protect members of the Way of Blue while it's equipped!

Additionally, if you hop back to Firelink Shrine right now, you'll meet ANOTHER new NPC: Sirris of the Sunless Realms. For now, just talk to her once to initiate her questline and return to the Halfway Fortress to pass through the gate, which will take you further down into the forest. Here, you'll encounter your first Lycanthrope Hunters - Hollows wielding large tree branches/logs sharpened like spears - but you shouldn't have to worry about their range if you just rush in right after they attack to combo them to death. If you look down to your right as you descend the hill here, you'll see a couple more net to a shimmering body of water...well, it's a swamp alright, but not a poison one (yet). At the bottom of the hill here, turning right and walking along the shore will bring you to a Titanite Shard guarded by a Starved Dog and a Lycanthrope Hunter. Before dealing with the marsh itself, return to the bottom of the hill (where you'll probably have to deal with the two Lycanthrope Hunters you saw earlier) and head along the rocky right side of it to reach another Titanite Shard...along with a few Poisonhorn Bugs, returning from the previous game, that you'll want to take out with charged R2 attacks before they can produce their clouds of, well, poison. Return to the top of the path and, where the road makes a full turn, drop off the side onto a series of ledges, one of which contains a Soul of an Unknown Traveler, until you reach the ground again. Ahead, there'll not only be three Poisonhorn Bugs clumped together that you can take out in a single charged R2 attack, but one of the things apparently being hunted here; a Lycanthrope, which is in fact NOT a werewolf, but just a beastly Hollow with a cross on its back. This guy takes a lot of punishment and moves pretty fast - sneak up on him to get a charged R2 attack in, then alternate between dodging and R1 combos (which WILL stagger him, at least) as you're contending with him.

Take out the next three Poisonhorn Bugs on the left and the Lycanthrope hiding behind a tree ahead, then enter the building and turn left to meet your first (returning) Black Knight, an elite enemy that's legitimately stronger than the early-game bosses and can actually kick the ass of MID-game bosses. However, they CAN be backstabbed and have well-telegraphed attacks, so as long as you keep rolling, you'll do fine against them (and this one). Once he's dead, walk out onto the balcony you passed and turn left to reach a corpse with the Sellsword Set (a.k.a. the "armor" of the Mercenary class)...and underneath that balcony in the main building, you'll find a body with the Sellsword Twinblades. The Sellsword Twinblades (and others of the same category) are distinct from the Twinblades of Dark Souls II in that they're two separate blades, one held in each hand (when two-handing with ), and they have no blocking capability when two-handing, instead performing attacks with both blades when you press L1 . What it DOES share, though, is an overwhelming capacity for damage - attacks come out fast and do even more damage than those Deep Battle Axe strikes, letting you shred through every HP bar you come across. Plus, they can be Buffed with Resins and Infused if you want for elemental damage, giving you even more adaptability against enemies with weaknesses. Widely regarded as the "easy mode"-enabling weapon of the game and acquired so much earlier than the Red Iron Twinblade was (in fact, you could've started the game with this in the Mercenary class, though it would've come at the cost of decreased starting stats elsewhere), accept no substitutes for the Sellsword Winblades. With the game-winners in hand, proceed to the end of this hall for a corpse bearing the Farron Coal, which you'll give to Andre for infusions later. Now, use a Homeward Bone and retrace your steps down the path, testing out the Sellsword Twinblades along the way; in basically every combat encounter going forward, you'll want to just spam L1 and watch enemies break down under your flurry of blows. At the bottom, turn left and walk along the shore, taking out the Lycanthrope Hunters as you go. Next to a thick tree on the left, pick up a Twin Dragon Greatshield and eradicate the several Poisonhorn Bugs guarding another Titanite Shard below. To the right of the stone arch, you'll find a Fading Soul, after which you can pass through the arch and turn right to find the next Bonfire (Crucifixion Wood)...as well as, uh, a giant crab of the enemy variety roaming the swamp below with some of his offspring. Hoo boy.

At the tower ahead, go along the right-hand path to pick up another Soul of an Unknown Traveler and dispatch another Lycanthrope, who should prove much easier to handle with your Sellsword Twinblades, then collect an Ember from the corpse next to the bonfire ahead. On the cliff to the left, a couple Lycanthrope Hunters will spot you as you move toward the corpse below, so kill them and collect an Estus Shard from it before taking out the OTHER Lycanthrope resting to the right of the bonfire. Return to the real Bonfire, use it to return to the Firelink Shrine and get yourself up to 8 Estus Flasks with Andre, and return before bracing yourself: you're going to be dropping into the swamp. Thankfully, standing in the water doesn't automatically poison you as in other games, but that doesn't exactly make it less dangerous - focus on massacring the cute little crabs first, THEN start engaging the Great Crabs, one at a time. They move way faster than they should and hit brutally hard with their claws, as well as using a bubble attack that, while not damaging, greatly slows you down for several seconds; your best bet is to keep dodging to and attacking them from the side, particularly when they hunch down to unleash the bubbles. Attacking their legs enough will also make them collapse for a couple seconds, which helps a lot if you need to heal (and you probably will). The annoying part is that they have tons of defense, so even with the Sellsword Twinblades you'll be chipping away at their health for quite a while. Midway through this, you're liable to be invaded by Yellowfinger Heysel - she does have a questline for a gesture, but because it's mutually exclusive with pursuing Sirris's, you're going to be saving it for NG+ and instead focusing on kicking her ass here. Heysel attacks with rapid-fire ranged sorceries, a crossbow, and her trademark pick/staff, all of which serve to either stunlock or knock you down...and just like Hodrick, she can use Estus Flasks! You'll want to stay as close to her as possible and interrupt her attack/healing animations with your L1 slashes as often as you can, particularly the healing one, and keep on the offensive with her for as long as you can - when she does pull off a sorcery, hide behind a tree for the duration of it and then resume your assault.

For your trouble, you'll receive Heysel's Pick and the Xanthous Crown, at which point you'll probably want to return to the Halfway Fortress Bonfire (via the slope that leads into the water near the second Great Crab) and return to the Firelink Shrine to Reinforce those Sellsword Twinblades to 3 with Andre. Back at the Crucifixion Wood Bonfire, drop down and re-kill all the crabs, Lesser and Great, so the latter isn't bothering you as you take on the other one across the pond. When that one goes down too, you'll receive the Great Swamp Ring (15/107) (increases power of pyromancies) and are now free to loot this damned area. Collect the Grass Crest Shield (slightly increases stamina regeneration - this is what you'll be wearing on your backs once you have the VIT for it) from under a tree in front of the bottom of the slope, 4 Green Blossoms from a tree further on, and not only the Conjurator Set, but a Great Swamp Pyromancy Tome for Cornyx. Nice! On the other side of the marsh, there's a corpse near where you dropped down with 2 Green Blossoms and one on the bank of the landmass in the middle of the swamp with the Fallen Knight Set. Before returning to the mainland, collect the Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler from here, being veeeeeery careful to avoid aggroing the enemies under the arch here. Return to the Halfway Fortress Bonfire and Travel to the Crucifixion Woods one - time to get out of here. Return to the building past the Bonfire, where you're going to be ignoring the purple summon sign on the far left (it'll bring out Mad Knight Hodrick to fight again instead of an actual ally) in favor of entering the building through the hole in the wall. Here, you've got a bunch of Hollows to take out, so start spamming L1 and save the one with the staff firing sorceries for last (in fact, hide behind the wall while you're taking out the others if you can), then pick up the Heretic's Staff from the corner and go up the stairs to cross a bridge to a spear-and-shield-wielding Hollow that'll go down as easily as the rest. Take the left path here first past the bonfire from earlier and up a set of stairs to an open-air room filled with scrolls, where you'll meet a new NPC: Orbeck of Vinheim.

Since you have 10 INT, he's willing to talk to you - and once you choose to Ask to learn sorceries and Make a promise with him, he'll teleport to the Firelink Shrine to become your resident sorceries teacher...in exchange for, as you might've guessed, bringing him tomes of sorceries to expand his knowledge with. Before you head back, cross to the other side of this broken floor and go down the stairs to pick up 2 Blue Bug Pellets (temporarily increases magic resistance). Back at the crossroads, head down the right path and kill the Crystal Lizard there for a Crystal Gem before taking out the Hollow that'll attack you from the nearby doorway. In the room beyond, there'll be another staff-wielding Hollow and a spear-and-shield one up the stairs from him, so dispatch them both and head out of the opening on the stairs to a pathway of ledges leading back down into the swamp, where you can pick up a Golden Falcon Shield from a corpse near the tree. Now, return to the swamp and hug the right edge to reach not only a set of stairs leading back into the building, but a flooded passage with a Lycanthrope inside waiting to pounce from the right. With him taken care of, you can now retrieve the Sorcerer's Set and Sage's Ring (16/107) before going up the stairs. You'll return to the room you were in; dropping down from the balcony at the top of the stairs will let you pick up another Ring of Sacrifice if you wanna sell it later, but either way it's time to tackle the main room. There's two sorcerer Hollows and four melee ones in here, so rushing the former will leave you free to clear out the latter at your own pace. When they're all gone, you can call upon Eygon of Carim from a summon sign behind the pillar to the left and head up the hill path beyond the room to reach the Crystal Sage.
