This guy is annoying, but simultaneously the easiest boss you'll have fought so far. His gimmick is that - akin to the Fool's Idol from Demon's Souls - he'll show up in one place, take a few hits from you while casting his sorceries, then disappear and reappear somewhere else in the arena while ice spikes form all over the place. This first phase isn't too hard as long as you keep your head on a swivel to catch him as soon as he pops up again, and between your Sellsword Twinblades+3 and Eygon's own damage output, you can burn through half his HP in under a minute, especially since your attacks will stagger him and disrupt his casting. The fun part comes when, like the other bosses, the Crystal Sage decides that 50% HP means it's time to lock in, which for him results in copies of himself popping up every time he does. These shadow clones look just like him and hit just as hard, but they all go down in one hit and/or when the real Crystal Sage pulls his disappearing act...and you can tell them apart because the REAL one's projectiles are purple, while those of the clone are blue. With Eygon likely taking out multiple clones per instance by himself, you're free to just watch for the purple one, rush over, and cut him to ribbons - it's not too hard to dodge all the sorceries, either, so you should barely take any damage during this. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Crystal Sage With Logan's successor collapsing for the last time, you'll receive the Soul of a Crystal Sage (do not consume this!)... ...and a new Bonfire (Crystal Sage) to light and rest at. Time to return to the Firelink Shrine once more.

You've got a couple of things to do this time around. First, go to Ludleth and Transpose that Soul of a Crystal Sage for Crystal Hail (3/34)(alternatively, you can make the Crystal Sage's Rapier with it instead, as it'll greatly boost your item discovery while equipped and you'll be getting two more copies of the Soul in future runs - thanks, meschejre!). After giving the Farron Coal to Andre, speak to Greirat again and gain access to his expanded inventory by progressing his questline, then go over to Cornyx and give him the Great Swamp Pyromancy Tome, which will expand HIS inventory of pyromancies!...and they're a bit more expensive than the last batch was, so you won't be buying them right now. Instead, go over to Orbeck, sitting opposite Cornyx, and peruse his selection of sorceries; he's starting off with a whopping 11 for you to buy, but almost all of them cost 2,000+ Souls, so as with Cornyx, you'll save it for later. Now, run over to Irina and give her the Braille Divine Tome of Carim, which not only expands her selection as well, but advances her storyline, weeeeeeee. With her new offerings ALSO being a bit too pricy for where you're at, let's leave her alone - once you reach the optimal Soul farming location later in the game, you'll buy all these up. For now, go to the Handmaid and sell everything that you don't want or need to keep around, e.g., excess armor, before consuming all your Soul Chunks and raising your Ashen One to level 36 with the following specifications: With all that done, return to the Crystal Sage Bonfire and take the left-hand path, which will bring you into the mountains where two Hollow Manservants are patrolling. Once they're dead, look over the left edge of the path (next to the large stone protrusion) to see a Crystal Lizard that you can

drop down on and kill for a Twinkling Titanite. Drop off the end of this path to return to the main path and descend toward the bonfire, where you can take out an Evangelist (look at how much easier it is to kill them now!) and pick up the Herald Set from the corpse in the corner. From here, cross a bridge and you'll reach a set of stairs...leading toward the Cathedral of the Deep.

Light the Bonfire (Cathedral of the Deep) and turn left from the base of the stairs down a slightly-hidden path, where you'll be set upon by the Fallen Knight, a unique and non-respawning enemy that has the durability and damage output of a mad spirit without the spells or ability to heal that they bring. He'll be wielding two blades, just like you, and has a habit of rolling away just as you start your combo, so wait for him to finish an attack before you slash at him and the battle should go fine (though you should keep an eye out for the Kukris he throws). When it's safe, go down the path he was guarding to retrieve the Paladin's Ashes. Halfway up the first flight of stairs, a path through the trees to the left will bring you to a corpse with a Titanite Shard (in an alcove to the right halfway along), while the path to the right of the top of these stairs will take you on a short drop and then up the mountainside to a row of gravestones with the Crest Shield. Now, return to the stairs and prepare to fight the also-non-respawning Brigand at the top of the next set - an axe-and-shield wielder, this guy likes to spam Kukris and the Warcry Weapon Art to increase his attack power...but he's substantially easier to deal with than the Fallen Knight was since your combos can stunlock him and he has less HP overall. When he's gone and you've picked up the Spider Shield he drops, return to and rest at the Bonfire before heading through the arch at the top of the stairs into a more forested area, chock-full of Starved Hounds and with a perimeter patrolled by more crossbow-wielding Hollows. No two ways about it, this area sucks to get through; your best bet is to advance slowly, hiding behind the trees where you can, and take out the Hollows as soon as you can while TRYING to only take on one Hound at a time. After grabbing the Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler from next to the first Hollow, proceed through the graveyard ahead until you see a Hollow wielding a Pyromancy Flame - once he sees you, he'll set himself on fire like the Evangelists and rush toward you, but he'll only make it a dozen yards or so before exploding and dying, so backing up when he starts sprinting will keep you safe.

Through the front entrance of the least-evil-church-ever ahead, open the wooden doors to the main hall, where you'll find not only the next Bonfire (Cleansing Chapel), but - if you bought the Ashes of Ariandel DLC or are playing the complete version of the game, The Fire Fades - the one and only Slave Knight Gael. Note: via Gael, you can access the Ashes of Ariandel content starting from this very moment in the game. Now, you're not remotely equipped well enough to properly tackle this challenge right now, and the game itself will tell you that if you proceed...but if you're interested in acquiring a Titanite Slab way earlier than you're supposed to, check out the Ashes of Ariandel section below! Light and rest at the Bonfire, pick up the Notched Whip from the corner, and (since the doors in here are currently locked) head outside to turn right toward an obelisk being worshipped by four Hollows. Since the corpse in front of them holds an Estus Shard, take them out as quickly as you can before they can draw their weapons and collect that before proceeding along the path up to another graveyard...where the dead rise from their graves! These Reanimated Corpses spawn endlessly from their graves, but while they're not that tough, you better watch your ass if a group of them come at you. Proceed along the main path here until you reach a side path going up a slope to the left, at the end of which lies an Astora Greatsword, then double back and drop off a ledge to the right (of the path leading to the item), where you'll run along a walkway overlooking the main path until you reach a clearing with several "sleeping" Reanimated Corpses and a couple of items. Read this next paragraph all the way through before you move from here, as things are gonna get hairy really fast. The corpses here hold a Fading Soul and an Executioner's Greatsword...but as soon as you pick them up, a solid dozen Reanimated Corpses are gonna pull themselves up from the ground and advance on you. Rather than attack them, flee for your life through the horde and take the first left you come across, which will lead you to a narrow, crumbling bridge with a new variant of Reanimated Corpse that has, uh, a second torso made of maggots protruding from its stomach that'll lunge toward you for high damage and take several more hits than the normal ones (Infested Corpses). Worse yet, taking hits from this will leave maggots on your Ashen One that slowly build up bleed, so try your best to dance around these guys (if you're really having trouble with them, purchasing the Torch from the Handmaid will let you instantly shake them off by equipping it)! Head up the stairs behind him and face your first Grave Warden (no, not the one from the last game, unfortunately); they wield twinblades like you and can also breathe fire while moving pretty darn fast, so don't underestimate them.

When he's dead (and won't respawn like the rest), take a right into the field of arrows below to collect some goods - 3 Repair Powders, 2 Large Souls of an Unknown Traveler, and an Undead Bone Shard, to be precise, killing Infested Corpses as needed all the while. Back up the stairs, take a right toward a large crypt and check the left side of the building for a Titanite Shard, then the interior for a Curse Ward Greatshield before descending the stairs and kicking down the ladder at the bottom, which will let you head back outside once you slide down it. Out here, you'll encounter your first Corpse Grubs, larger and animalistic masses of maggots that hit harder and move faster than the Infested Corpses, though they go down about as easily. From here, go up the path and climb the hill to the right to find a corpse with another Titanite Shard; drop down from here to return to the chapel and use the Bonfire to return to the Firelink Shrine for a second. Once you Reinforce your Estus Flask with Andre and burn the Undead Bone Shard at the Bonfire to go up to 9 Estus Flask+2, return to the Cleansing Chapel and head out the front door to the obelisk, then turn right and drop down to the valley with the running water where you were previously. Climb the stairs to the split path you were at before, and you'll see another Ravenous Crystal Lizard chilling in the middle of a bunch of crystals; this time, you're equipped to kill this guy, so lay into him with your Sellsword Twinblades (rolling through his strikes and rolling, natch), and you'll receive a Titanite Scale (used to level up boss weapons). Head through the gap in the buildings next to the crystals to find a Corpse Grub guarding a corpse with the Poisonbite Ring (17/107) (increases poison resistance). Going up the stairs to the left here, you'll reach a corpse with another Titanite Shard, and in the alley between the building at the base of the stairs, you'll find not only a Crystal Lizard that'll drop a Twinkling Titanite, but a corpse with ANOTHER Titanite Shard near the set of stairs leading down to the water valley that'll return you to the other set of stairs, along the way of which you can pick up a Saint-Tree Bellvine (notably allows for gradual HP recovery with its Weapon Art).

Now, return to the building entrance and climb the ladder - unfortunately, the Grave Warden will be waiting for you at the top since you used a Bonfire, so be prepared to fight him again. When it's safe, head up the other set of stairs toward the cathedral, which is sealed for now, and to the left side to collect 2 Rusted Coins from a corpse behind some boxes, then to the right for a Red Bug Pellet ahead of a small set of stairs leading to a patrolling Hollow with a flaming spear and shield. However, not only are there two self-immolating Hollows hiding out for when you go down and engage with this one, but a Hollow with a flaming crossbow will appear in the archway above the platform here to start shooting at you when you get close to the stairs; you'll want to lure him out and wait for him to drop to the cobblestones so you can take him out first before dealing with the others. From here, cross some planks on the left and descend the slanted roof beam toward another connected to the main roof of the building. Before you go any further, kill the Hollow waiting to ambush you on the wooden platform attached to the intersection here. In addition to the Hollow patrolling the main roof, there are several Thralls waiting to drop down and attack you when you walk to certain parts of the rooftop - you can force them down earlier with Throwing Knives, if you want. The corpse on the balcony holds a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler, but when you collect it, two more self-immolating Hollows will clamber up over the sides, so dispatch them immediately and proceed along the roof to another slanted beam, at the bottom of which stand three crossbow-wielding Hollows that'll be pelting you with flaming arrows as long as you're in their line of sight. Run down, kill them and the spear-and-shield Hollow hanging out near them, and head up the stairs to find 3 Red Bug Pellets (along with two Thralls that'll drop down when you collect it).

To the left, you'll find an Evangelist and three more self-immolating Hollows that'll aggro you as soon as you get close to them; run back down the stairs (ideally, one or more of the Hollows will kill themselves following you) and the Evangelist will sprint over with surprising speed, allowing you to take her on in a wider area before you collect 3 Undead Hunter Charms from the corpse they were huddled by. Return to where you fought the Evangelist and descend the stairs, where you'll want to let the halberd-wielding Hollow come to you before taking him out so as not to alert the Thrall in the archway to the left, who has two friends that'll all bumrush you as soon as they see you - they're tough enough to take on as it is, so don't add the Hollow to the mix. In the room they were hiding in, you'll find a Soul of an Unknown Soldier...and two greatsword-wielding Thralls that'll drop from the ceiling when you pick it up. At the sets of stairs ahead, kill the three Hollows waiting for you and advance up the stairs parallel to the path to find two more Grave Wardens patrolling; lure them back down the stairs one at a time for a battle that's actually manageable, then let the self-immolating Hollows coming down the set of stairs to the left of this enclosed space see you so they kill themselves. At the top of these stairs, after another self-immolating Hollow jumps out at you from the left, you'll see a group of Hollows praying in front of a corpse holding an Ember - when you approach them, you'll want to dispatch the greataxe-wielding Hollow around the corner and the Hollow hanging over the balcony to the right before engaging the rest so you don't get overwhelmed. Through the large doors here, you'll finally enter the cathedral itself, where you can gaze upon the magnificent chandelier, ornate interior decorating...and a Giant Slave slumbering on the ground below. Poor guy.

The passage to the left of this balcony will take you first to a slime enemy that, while durable, really doesn't fight back unless you actively allow it to. Behind it lies a corpse with a Duel Charm that you'll probably never use, and to the right of that are your first Deacons; fire-slinging enemies that are worth equipping your Flame Stoneplate Ring to face, though they won't take more than a few hits to kill. Outside the room you fight them in, a lift will take you down to an outdoor passage where - past a gate and a set of doors - you can create a shortcut right back to the main Bonfire, which is well worth resting at right now. Return to where you were and take the stairs to the right of the archway leading further in down to reach an Evangelist guarding a Deep Gem (on the way back up, another slime will drop on you from the top of the stairs leading into the room where you were, so be ready to roll). Now, through the aforementioned archway, you'll be attacked by the Giant Slave, who'll unleash wide and immensely hard-hitting punches and arm sweeps so long as you're within his reach and line of sight. The trick here is to run, run, RUN across the ledge connecting this walkway to the other side, which should keep you from getting hit...and along the way, you'll want to pick up the Soul of a Nameless Soldier, 6 Exploding Bolts, and Lloyd's Sword Ring (18/107) (boosts damage output when HP is full), which you'll want to slot into your fourth ring slot. Down the stairs you end up, you'll come across a branching path of a hallway to the left and another set of stairs down -proceed into the hallway, and you'll see a bridge running across a large room. There's a Thrall hanging off either side of this bridge and one clinging to the ceiling at the end; knock down the one on the right with a Throwing Knife and advance slowly to provoke the other two into attacking you one at a time, then head to the end and kill the slime so you can collect Seek Guidance (6/35) from the corpse.

On the starting end of the bridge, you'll see a ladder at the end of the hall - climb it to battle another Evangelist and collect an Ember from the corpse beyond her before returning to the branching path to descend the stairs, where you'll see another chest in front of an altar. Only...it's not a chest at all, but another Mimic; hack it to pieces and pick up the Deep Braille Divine Tome that it drops (we will, in fact, not be giving this one to Irina for her sake), then descend the stairs next to the ones you entered this room from to reach the ground floor of the larger chamber you were in earlier, where you'll face a new fearsome type of warrior: Cathedral Knights, slow and powerful with a greatshield that blocks most damage and a mace that can be enchanted to leave light landmines in the wake of its brutal attacks. You'll want to dance around him and wait to attack until he either has his back turned or is casting a miracle, which will let you cut through his HP pretty quick (though he can heal himself if left alone). When the knight is down, head over to the doorway he came from and look in...seems conspicuously barren aside from the item at the end, right? Yeah, no, this isn't that kind of a game -when you enter the room proper, the first of two Deep Accursed will drop down onto you! These guys are not only creepy, but vile to fight; they've got a long reach with their limbs and speed, and they can spew a liquid that inflicts rapid curse buildup, so taking them on legitimately is all but suicidal...which is why you won't be. See, in this specific instance, retreating through the doorway will leave the Deep Accursed unable to follow, so you can dart in, attack it once with L1 , and roll back out while it attacks until another opening presents itself (occasionally, it'll collapse and let you attack it a couple extra times), which should leave you completely safe so long as you get the hell out of there when its curse vomit starts spewing. Upon death, this Deep Accursed will drop Aldrich's Sapphire (19/107) (restores FP with each critical hit...and has messed-up flavor text), leaving you free to collect the Ember from the corpse.

Return to the main chamber and take the exit to the left of this doorway to reach an even larger hall where, if you're Enkindled, you'll be invaded by Longfinger Kirk, wielding equipment that damages you and builds up bleed when you're in physical contact with him - however, he almost never heals himself and doesn't have any spells, making him drastically more manageable than the rest of the mad spirits have been. Lure him back into the previous room for a solo duel and receive his Barbed Straight Sword + Spiked Shield for defeating him, then proceed into the hall and take out the three Thralls before you do anything else (ideally one-on-one). To the left, you'll see the Giant Slave that was giving you grief earlier - time for payback! Though the sludge he's standing in will slow you down, this will still be an easy "fight": head over to him and start slashing at his ankles, making sure that you always stay behind him while he performs his swipes and stomps. You won't be able to see his HP during this, but he'll go down in about a minute if you're consistent in attacking him, leaving you free to collect the Maiden Set, Soul of a Nameless Soldier, Large Titanite Shard, and 4 Dung Pies from the surrounding corpses. Additionally, you can open the blue doors at the end of the sludge pool to head outside, where corpses bearing the Saint Bident and 2 Homeward Bones await you. Back in the hall, proceed to the other side and dispatch the Cathedral Knight and two Thralls patrolling there, then pull the lever to raise a massive gate that doubles as a bridge for the upper floor. Through the doorway on the right, descend a set of stairs and open a gate at the bottom to head outside, where the main path leads to two sets of doors. Open the one at the end of the path to return to + rest at the Bonfire, then return to the main hall of the cathedral, where running over to the waterlogged area opposite the Giant Slave will bring you to a lever in the left corner that, when pulled, will raise another gate platform to use later. Now, it's time to kill the other Giant Slave - but this one is surrounded by

slimes and a new enemy, a Man Grub, that'll vomit maggots at you if you're caught unawares. Rather than take them all on at once while trying to dispatch the Giant Slave, lure as many of the slimes over to you and kill them one-by-one while remaining out-of-range of the Giant Slave to keep him asleep, then wake him up and try to have him kill as many of the remaining enemies as you can with his attacks. Once they're all dead, you can loot the area for a Titanite Shard, 4 Dung Pies, Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler, Drang Set, and Pale Tongue. Return to the Bonfire if you need to replenish your Estus Flasks after that, and once you're ready, head up the stairs here to reach the main congregation area, where an interesting mechanic comes into play; there are quite a lot of enemies here, but most (excepting two patrolling Deacons and a stationary Cathedral Knight facing the altar) are seated in the pews and won't attack you unless you attack them first...or if their pews are broken by any attack or roll. As such, this can be very hard or pretty darn easy to get through depending on your method; you're going to be doing it the easy way by first luring away the Deacons to the stairs you just ascended, then taking on the Cathedral Knight there as well, staying well away from the pews all the while. Collect an Ember from a corpse overlooking the area below at the back of the pews and cross to the other side of the congregation, where a small archway on the left leads to a lift that'll bring you to the front doors of the cathedral! Open these to create another shortcut and head down the other set of stairs to reunite with, um...Siegward? Well, he's acting weird, but surely he can still be trusted, so start walking across the bridge you raised and- oh, son of a bitch, it was Patches all along! That's right, this man has stuck around for thousands of years since the original game solely to be a hater; admirable dedication, if nothing else. His plan was to sic the Giant Slave on you, but since you killed it, that's been foiled - pull the two levers to raise both gates again and run back to the Bonfire, where (without resting) you'll want to head outside and turn right toward the well, where the real Siegward has been trapped and robbed of his armor. You can't do anything other than sensibly chuckle at his ruminations right now, so return to the path you've been taking to the main cathedral (to the left of the Bonfire), where you'll want to open the set of doors to your left just after exiting the church so you can take the lift inside up the tower...which just so happens to be where the Hollow that was shooting at you earlier is patrolling. Kill him and walk through the archway onto the ledge, which leads to a ladder on the left; climb this and take out the Deacon at the top for his Deep Ring (20/107) (provides additional attunement slots).

Now, exit through the broken corner of this room and run/roll onto the buttress below, where you'll find yourself above the main roof you were exploring earlier. Head over to the other end of the buttress to get the Thrall hanging off the side to pull himself up, then quickly kill him so you're not dealing with too many flaming arrows from the assholes down below. At the top of the buttress, deal with the greataxe-wielding Hollow that'll emerge from the alcove on the left and proceed right, taking out another Thrall and a Hollow using a halberd along the way. Keep going along this walkway until you see a Thrall hunched over in the distance - the last tower on the right here connects to a buttress leading to an Arbalest, though another Thrall will drop down behind you as you go to pick it up. Returning to the walkway, kill the Thrall at the end (and another that'll ambush you from behind) to pick up your third Pale Tongue; take these easy ones while you can. With that done, walk through the doorway leading into the cathedral a few pillars away to reach the rafters, where several more Thralls and three Cathedral Knights await you. While the former can be taken on as usual, the latter you'll want to bait into falling to their deaths by luring them to the intersections/corners of these rafters and having them attack you across the gap, which will usually result in them finishing their animation in empty air and plummeting to the floor below for a fatal landing - much easier than doing this legit! When the coast is clear, you can pick up a Blessed Gem at the rightmost rafter intersection. From the intersection where the middlemost Cathedral Knight was standing, you can drop down onto a platform, and dropping off the left side of that will bring you to a hallway where a Man Grub will attack you with miracles, though he's just as easily dispatched as the last one. And to his left...the Unbreakable Patches!

This miserable lout will claim to not know you at first, but selecting the "You know who I am." option will have him give up the ghost and make "amends" by gifting you both a Rusted Coin and his gesture, "Prostration" (18/33). He'll also become available as a middling merchant, and his main draw there is selling the Catarina Set...a.k.a. Siegward's armor, which you'll need to buy off of him (for 15,000 Souls, Gwyn almighty; you may want to sell some stuff to him now to make up for it) before pulling the nearby lever to raise the final gate, which will let you cross back to the entrance area and provide a handy shortcut. Make use of it (or a Homeward Bone) to return to the Bonfire and then the well, where you can throw Siegward's armor down to him and receive his next gesture, "Rejoice" (19/33), as his sincere thanks. Retrace your steps to Patches and go up the steps to find a whole horde of Man Grubs - let them all come to you and dispatch them as best you can before going any further so you can contend with the miracle-throwing one alone. When all your attackers lie dead at your feet, take out the pacifistic Man Grub at the other end of the hall for the Red Sign Soapstone. Now, you can open the large doors here to light and rest at the last Bonfire (Rosaria's Bed Chamber) of the area before talking to the long-built-up Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth herself. You can (and should) ask to join her covenant, which will give you, uh...Rosaria's Fingers... ...but do not choose to Offer Pale Tongue right now, as that will lock you out of Sirris's questline. You'll also see that Rosaria grants you the option to reallocate your stat selections, a returning mechanic from Dark Souls II (though here, it can only be done 5 times per NG cycle); though this "costs" a Pale Tongue, it does not piss off Sirris, so you'll be making use of that right now in order to make better use of the points you put into STR and INT since you don't need them anymore:

Oh, and you can change your Ashen One's appearance!...but this ALSO costs a Pale Tongue and counts as a "rebirth", so it's not really worth the price for this playthrough. Now, backtrack to the main altar of the chapel (the one with the two Deacons and a Cathedral Knight patrolling) and head behind it to find two summon signs for Anri and Horace, whom you'll want to call upon before heading through the fog gate at the bottom of the stairs to face the least evil Catholics, the Deacons of the Deep. Despite appearances, this is also one of the easiest bosses in the game, though you can still get overwhelmed if you're not careful. The first phase of this fight will have you surrounded by dozens of Deacons...and while they all go down as easily as the normal ones, attacking just any of them won't decrease the overall HP bar. Instead, you'll need to look for the one that's been possessed (indicated by a red glow around their body) and kill him, which will take a chunk off the boss HP. Repeat this several times, with Anri and Horace acting as brutally effective crowd control, and at half HP... ...the real main boss, Archdeacon Royce, will appear and be your sole target for the rest of the fight (though he'll be joined by new blue-robed Deacons that like to cast Heal and Force when it's least convenient). Now, the battle will be faster because you only have one target (and a non-shifting, slow-moving one at that), but you'll also be getting ganged up on by the Deacons a lot more, and they can quickly shred through your HP with their melee attacks if you're not careful. Additionally, Royce will sometimes start charging up a dark sphere above his head while the other Deacons help him charge it up - attack him immediately when this starts and don't let up until the animation stops, as letting it finish will result in a VERY powerful attack that moves through pillars/walls and might very well one-shot you. Just keep the pressure on, roll out of the crowd if you need to heal up, and this'll be over in about a minute.

Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Deacons of the Deep With religion dismantled forever, you'll receive the Soul of the Deacons of the Deep (do not consume this!)... ...and the Small Doll, needed to enter a story area later. Light and rest at the Bonfire (Deacons of the Deep), which will uniquely respawn the body of Royce nearby to collect the Archdeacon Set from, and return to the Firelink Shrine.

From the Bonfire, head up the stairs to the left so you can speak to Anri and Horace again, where you'll learn that their (and your) next destination is Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, through the dreaded Farron Keep. Next, head to Ludleth and Transpose the Soul of the Deacons of the Deep for Deep Soul (4/34), then run over to Andre and Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades to +4. One day, you'll get these bad boys to +10... Before doing your leveling-up, go up the stairs to the entrance and to the left to reach the tower that you unlocked and explored earlier - when you take the lift in the center of the building (across the bridge from the top of the tower) up, you'll hear the gate closing behind you, and returning to it will reveal that bad ol' Patches has locked you in!...or so he thinks. Just like before, you can drop off the bridge (using the previous method or the safer, but slower one of aiming for the coffins on the right side) to reach the bottom and head outside; from there, go back inside Firelink Shrine and return to the archways leading outside, now blocked off by fog. At the end of this hallway, Patches is standing and will be quite surprised to see you've made it out of his latest trap, but will offer his definitely sincere wishes to let bygones be bygones - Refuse to accept this, and he'll give you a Rusted Gold Coin (better version of the Rusted Coin) while still becoming a merchant for you. Finally, leave Firelink Shrine, then come back (via the Bonfire) and you'll catch him squatting; talking to him here will give you his other gesture, "Patches Squat" (20/33). With all that done, use your remaining Soul Chunks and head over to the Handmaid to not only give her the Paladin's Ashes, but sell all your excess inventory off to her (particularly the Archdeacon Set) so you can raise your Ashen One to level 44 with the following specifications:

And now, you're ready to venture forth to the forbidden keep. Travel to the Crucifixion Woods Bonfire and drop down into the swamp (on the left side, so you don't piss off the Great Crab) to set foot on the small island you skirted around the edge of earlier, where the two Exile Watchdogs are that you were warned of earlier. If taken on in an actual fight, these guys are still pretty tough, even with your improvements - but the trick to beating them easily is as simple as running past them through the arch they're guarding and climbing onto the ladder to the right, as staying at the top of it will make them continue to attack you...and almost assuredly push themselves over the edge of the pit to fall to their deaths. Collect the Great Club and Exile Greatsword in the aftermath, as well as the 2 Homeward Bones from the corpse on the balcony, and descend the ladder fully to progress toward Farron Keep.

Light and rest at the Bonfire (Farron Keep), then head outside to look at an honest-to-god poison swamp, lovingly brought back by Miyazaki the Masochist himself after its sole disappearance in Dark Souls II (just like Patches!). For the duration of this level, you'll want to swap out your Lloyd's Sword Ring for the Poisonbite Ring to keep your resistance high and keep any Purple Moss Clumps in your inventory equipped as a Quick Item in case you do get fully poisoned. Turn around the right corner to pick up 3 Purple Moss Clumps (especially if you don't have any to start with), and once your poison gauge completely drains, look out into the copse of trees beyond for this item: Running out to retrieve this will definitely poison you (since the swamp is deeper there), but it'll be well worth it because this is none other than Iron Flesh (5/27). Use a Purple Moss Clump and then, to the left of the exit, you'll see two Rotten Slugs that will spit poison sludge at you; run in and cut them down quickly, which will also help you determine how long you can spend standing in the swamp before you get poisoned. Around the left corner, four more Rotten Slugs guard a Ragged Mask, which you'll want to keep equipped for now for its extra poison resistance, and proceeding to the next landmass beyond the previous duo of Rotten Slugs will let you run out to pick up a Titanite Shard from the swamp, where four more Rotten Slugs are patrolling. At the next landmass with the bonfire, turn right toward the broken tower and run out to collect an Estus Shard from in front of it before turning left and picking up a Titanite Shard from the landmass here, killing Rotten Slugs all the while. Head up the stone steps from here and prepare to face off against your first

Ghrus, berserker enemies with poison-coated weapons that are best engaged one-on-one (in this case, attack the stationary one while the patrolling one is far on the left). Then, on the right, you'll see the first of the three flames that must be snuffed out to proceed: Pressing here will trigger a cutscene, showing you've snuffed one flame and lit another elsewhere. After heading under the arch here to collect 2 Rotten Pine Resins from a corpse, double back to the bottom of the steps and onto the island to the right to pick up 10 Prism Stones; from here, run out into the swamp to pick up a Stone Parma and 4 Rotten Pine Resins to the left and right, respectively, then (if your poison gauge is low enough) keep running to the tower beyond the corpse on the right, where you'll have to fight another Darkwraith with no exploit this time. Get in single attacks after he finishes each combo or heavy attacks, and he should go down without too much trouble, giving you his Dark Leggings and a Cracked Red Eye Orb - and after that, you can head inside the tower for the real prize, the Sage's Coal, on a corpse. From here, running over to the other side of the larger island where the first flame was snuffed will bring you to more solid ground in the form of the stairs running down the other side of the landmass. Kill the Ghru here (you can sneak up on him by walking) and collect a Titanite Shard from the base of the broken tower to the right before running to the base of the crumbling bridge, at the top of which lies a Greatsword. You'll also see that the bridge is surrounded by more, ah, feral Ghrus on all fours - they can't poison you, but they move and attack much faster, and killing one is likely to draw three more here. From the lower end of the bridge, roll to the other half of the bridge sticking out of the swamp several yards away for 4 Purple Moss Clumps before returning to the landmass where you killed the Ghru, where a Titanite Shard waits for you on the far side near the stairs; take these up, dispatch the Ghru waiting to ambush you on the right side near the top of the stairs, and collect 2 Purple Moss Clumps before snuffing the second flame nearby, which will play an abbreviated version of the previous cutscene.

The bridge on the left has three Ghru standing menacingly: two wielding a spear-and-shield combo, and one who acts as a shaman that can spew a HUGE cloud of poison gas. Don't engage them all at once, and instead approach slowly to lure the first melee Ghru over to you, then the shaman Ghru, and finally the other melee Ghru. After lighting and resting at the Bonfire (Keep Ruins) beyond, proceed down the ramp and head along the side of it once you're in the swamp to find a Titanite Shard in an arch near the back of it - then, clear out the Rotten Slugs in the tower to the right of the ramp to obtain another Undead Bone Shard. You know what that means: pop back to the Firelink Shrine really quick and visit both Andre and the Bonfire to go up to 10 Estus Flask+3. After returning to the Keep Ruins, look to the left and you'll see some items in the distance; it's a veritable bounty over there, buuuuuuuut another Great Crab is standing guard...and he's holding the Lingering Dragoncrest Ring (21/107), so you do have to kill him and contend with the poison all the while. Stick to the shallow areas of the swamp to maintain your mobility and keep using Estus Flasks instead of Purple Moss Clumps, and once he's dead, you'll be able to loot the area behind him for a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler, Soul of a Nameless Soldier, 6 Gold Pine Bundles, Ember, Crown of Dusk, and 2 Young White Branches. To the left of this area, you'll find the tragic scene of the Mushroom People, having been slaughtered by the Ghru; massacre the three still there in turn so you can collect the Sage's Scroll and (to prevent him from bailing on us) hop back to Firelink Shrine once again and give this to Orbeck to expand his collection of sorceries.

Go back to the Keep Ruins again and, this time, circle around to the left side of the building (from where you exit to the ramp leading down into the swamp), where you'll see an item in the distance surrounded by three large figures: These are Elder Ghrus, and they pack a much meaner punch than the normal variety while also taking much more punishment (about 3x more attacks, to be specific); they attack with brutal slams of their staves and like to summon skull-shaped projectiles that home in on you as you're fighting them as well as plant their staves in the ground to release a wide-ranging blast of force, making combat with more than one at a time pretty much suicidal. Approach them slowly to lure them away one at a time, and taking out all three will not only let you collect a Black Bow of Pharis and Pharis' Hat, but a Poison Gem as well. With all that looting done, head to the right past the ladder with the three Rotten Slugs (we'll come back to this later) to pick up a Wolf's Blood Swordgrass, another covenant item you'll be farming later - the small island beyond holds a Sunlight Talisman and another Estus Soup, while the landmass with the first bonfire adjacent to this (you'll want to circle back past the ladder and run along the land adjoining the two islands rather than trek through the deep swamp between them) has another Titanite Shard. The area ahead is going to be one of the most frustrating in the game for a number of reasons: 1. The trek between your current location and the final fire-to-be-snuffed (marked by the string of bonfires) is almost entirely deep swamp outside of the patches of land, so you'll be both poisoned quickly and contending with reduced mobility most of the time. 2. Another Elder Ghru waits ahead...and guess what? You've got a narrow patch of land to fight him on if you want to move faster than a crawl! He can be burned by the bonfire here, but it's not guaranteed that you can lure him into it, and avoiding his projectiles + staff attacks in the deep swamp is a pain in the ass. Oh, and a second one will come at you just as you reach the stairs!

3. Most fun of all, if you're Enkindled, you'll be invaded once again by Yellowfinger Heysel (either on the set of stairs behind the fire or right next to the fire, depending on an unknown trigger), who'll most likely accost you just as you reach the fire-to-be-snuffed at the end of the path. She doesn't have any different tricks than before, thankfully, but you're forced to fight her in a much smaller area and with fewer obstacles to hide from her sorceries behind due to the deep swamp surrounding you. Along the way between the bonfires, make sure to collect 2 Titanite Shards and the Nameless Soldier Set from corpses against the left wall of the swamp. At the top of the stairs, once the coast is clear, snuff out the third flame and watch the doors to the next area open, then go through the arch nearby and collect 2 Homeward Bones. Kill the Ghru at the top of the stairs and descend into the next area of the swamp, where you'll have to contend with everyone's second-favorite enemy type: Basilisks, who look just as they did in the past two games and retain the same annoying attack of breathing curse-building gas. Letting this gauge build up is much, much worse than poison, so stay away from those clouds at all costs and finish off the Basilisks quick as you can. To the right of the stairs (through a lot of deep swamp) is a Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier, while the landmasses to the left of the stairs will lead you to 4 Repair Powder, unfortunately surrounded by four Basilisks as well. On the elevated ground beyond the gaggle of Basilisks, turn around and you'll see a cave entrance on the left: Run over to here - thankfully, it's shallow water - and you can retrieve not only the Golden Scroll from a corpse, but the Antiquated Set from a chest on the right; bewilderingly, someone's already opened the one on the left. Back on the elevated ground, run across the swamp toward the tower from the leftmost side, and you'll return to the opened doors and the tower with the ladder -which you're now going to climb. After circling the perimeter of the walkway at the top to find and kill a Crystal Lizard for a Twinkling Titanite, head inside the archway next to the ladder to find not only a Bonfire (Old Wolf of Farron), but, well...the Old Wolf of Farron himself, petrified long ago.

Not to worry, though; you can still pray to him for his gesture, "Legion Etiquette" (21/33), and join his covenant, the Watchdogs of Farron! See the corpse with the item in the top-right corner? You can reach it by heading outside, going up the right set of stairs, and attacking the doorway in the inward corner of the building just after the top of said stairs, which will dissipate to reveal itself as an illusionary wall and let you collect the Dreamchaser's Ashes. From here, return to the Firelink Shrine and hand these over to the Handmaid, then exit and return via the Bonfire to find Sirris sitting near the Fire Keeper again -talking to her now that you've done something, ah, "kind" will have her offer to aid you in battle and give you her gesture, "Darkmoon Loyalty" (22/33). Now, return to the Old Wolf of Farron and ride the lift in the corner to the top of the tower for a breathtaking vista...as well as an optional (but not really) boss fight. Up the stairs to the right here, you'll reach the top of (part of) the massive bridge you've been seeing this whole time, and turning right again will bring you to a broken section of the railing that'll let you drop down onto a series of long platforms on the side of the wall, leading to a twisted and upturned section of the bridge beyond - as it so happens, the exact area you saw when meeting Yoel for the first time. Here, there's a Crystal Lizardto your left that'll drop a Heavy Gem, as well as some normal Hollows to kill for a change of pace...and on the right side, near the dragon corpse, you can kill two more Crystal Lizards for 2 Large Titanite Shards and pick up not only the Dragon Crest Shield from the corpses nearby, but Lightning Spear (7/35) as well. Head up to the top of the arch opposite the dragon and drop down the center to return to the bridge, where an all-too-familiar enemy awaits: the Stray Demon.

He doesn't get a full-screen HP bar, but don't let that fool you into thinking the Stray Demon is less dangerous than the other bosses. The mace he wields hits like a freight train and covers so much distance, so rolling behind/under him constantly is the name of the game here; he'll also attack with tail swipes and butt stomps (after flying into the air for a couple of seconds), but these are easily avoided. Aim for his thighs, one in particular if you can, and they'll eventually crumble, causing him to collapse and preventing him from following you anywhere, though he can still turn and attack - this creates a great opening for you to keep attacking him in, as he won't be able to hurt you while he's crumbling. Stay close to him so he doesn't spew rocks at you, and this will be over quickly; not so tough when you're not fighting a level 8 Chosen Undead, huh, jackass?! Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Stray Demon With the stone devil taken for granite, you'll receive the Soul of a Stray Demon (do not consume this!) and can retrieve 2 Embers and a Greataxe from the surrounding corpses, leaving you free to return to the Bonfire and descend the ladder to the swamp. Now, it's time to head through the door you put so much effort into opening, where more Corvians wait...well, not for you, as they're actually just praying and can be safely ignored. However, you'll want to slowly walk up the left path and approach a Corvian Shaman who's chanting to the others so you can kill him, as otherwise, he'd alert all the others and get you swarmed by crazy birdmen. When it's safe, collect the Shriving Stone from the corpse just beyond the doors and proceed up the path to come upon a rare enemy-on-enemy battle taking place, where a pair of Darkwraiths are absolutely slaughtering some Ghrus.

Wait until they're done and lure the Darkwraiths over one at a time to engage them solo, which won't be too hard with your stats and equipment, then turn around to head to this building on the left: Inside is a Bonfire (Farron Keep Perimeter) to light and rest at before you kill the Ghru ahead and drop through the opening in the wall to the right of him to drop down to a section of the swamp, where you'll want to pick up the Hollow Gem and Atonement (8/35), then use a Homeward Bone to return to where you were. Take out the three Ghru in the passage so you can engage another Ravenous Crystal Lizard, who'll go down fairly easily if you're relentless in attacking and will drop 2 Titanite Scales. After picking up Great Magic Weapon (5/34) from the corpse past him, you can open a gate that'll create a shortcut between this area and the Road of Sacrifices. Return to the forest of swords, wait for the Darkwraiths to attack the Ghrus, and repeat what you did earlier (or just run up the stairs to the gate, then exit and reload the game to spawn the Darkwraiths down the path) before summoning Black Hand Gotthard from near the gate and learning his gesture, "By my sword" (23/33). Head through the gate, and you'll face your first Lord of Cinder - the Abyss Watchers. Befitting one of the four main bosses of the game, these guys (or rather, this guy) do NOT mess around, and it'll take twice as much effort to kill them as any other boss up until this point. This battle starts off with an interesting mechanic: first, you'll be fighting only one Abyss Watcher (the main one), who's dangerous enough on his own with lunging and wide-reaching slashes and combos - plus an annoying tendency to roll away just as you start your own attacks - but at around 60% HP, a second Abyss Watcher will rise to aid him. This one has reduced HP and doesn't share it with the main boss, but he's just as deadly so you'll want to focus on taking him out quick...and a moment later, a third Abyss Watcher with red eyes will rise that's on YOUR side (until you damage him). With Gotthard fighting valiantly, this can turn into a 3-on-2 or even 3-on-1 fight very quickly, so long as you don't attack the red-eyed Abyss Watcher, and it's up in the air who the main Abyss Watcher and his ally will focus on at any given moment; sometimes it'll always be you, sometimes they'll focus on Gotthard until he's dead, and sometimes they'll make a beeline for the friendly Abyss Watchers

Abyss Watcher the moment he gets up. Gang up on the main Abyss Watcher whenever you can, roll through his combos until they're done, and eventually, he'll go down... ...but not really, as he'll absorb all the wolf blood of his fallen comrades to rise once more, imbued with flame and hitting harder than before. Now, all of his attacks will leave a fiery trail that'll inflict damage for a couple of seconds after each slash, making rolling around his attacks even more paramount than before, and some strikes that hit the ground will even create explosions! Ideally, you'll want him to focus on Gotthard while you attack him from behind, and don't risk healing yourself until you're safe while he's reaching the end of a combo. The one upside is that no other parties will be joining the chaos now, but it's still plenty dangerous, even 2-on-1. Be patient, above all else. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the undead legion finally put to rest, you'll receive the first Cinders of a Lord and the Soul of the Blood of the Wolf, which can safely be consumed... ...as well as a new Bonfire (Abyss Watchers) to light and rest at. Before going any further, it's time for another trip to Firelink Shrine.

There are quite a few new things you can do now that you've defeated a Lord of Cinder. First and foremost, go up to Ludleth and Transpose the Soul of a Stray Demon into the ever-recurring, ever-useful Havel's Ring (22/107) (increases maximum equipment load); since you're out of the swamp, you'll want to swap the Poisonbite Ring out for Lloyd's Sword Ring and the Life Ring out for Havel's Ring, which will greatly increase your options for equipment-swapping without putting more points into VIT for now. Next, talk to Hawkwood twice on the stairs (or outside, by heading out through the front entrance and turning left toward the grave guarded by the Starved Hound) to receive Farron's Ring (23/107) (reduces FP consumption of Weapon Arts) - exiting and reloading the game will also spawn Hawkwood's Shield by that same grave. Back in the Firelink Shrine, you'll see Eygon of Carim standing next to the leftmost throne, so talk to him if you want some unkind words about the state of your hub. Head down to the right of Andre so you can give the Golden Scroll to Orbeck and stay on good terms with him, then return to Andre to not only hand off the Sage's Coal, but Infuse your Sellsword Twinblades+4 with a Sharp Gem, which will raise their DEX scaling to A and let them do even more damage (as well as contribute to a future trophy)! Additionally, you can safely equip the Grass Crest Shield in one of your Left Hand Weapon slots - two-handing your Sellsword Twinblades+4 will keep the shield on your back while also maintaining its buff to your stamina. After doing your usual selling with the Handmaid and consumption of your Soul Chunks, speak to the Fire Keeper and raise your Ashen One to level 51 with the following specifications: Finally, place the Cinders of a Lord atop the throne second from the right - you'll have to drop down from the stairs behind it, where you'll find the front decorated with swords - and return to the Abyss Watchers Bonfire, where the candle-adorned wall will push back...giving you access to stairs that descend into the Catacombs of Carthus.

From the entrance, turn left at the pillars to encounter your first Skeleton - as in previous games, these guys have the unique trait of coming back to life, but they can only do so once and not all of them will (only the ones with white eyes). Keep an eye on your Souls as you fight them; if you see the counter go up after cutting one down, it's actually dead, and if not...get ready for a quick rematch. Pick up 2 Carthus Rouges (makes your weapon inflict bleed) from the corpse at the end of the hall and cross the bridge, where you'll encounter a Skeleton Swordsman that's larger, sturdier, and stronger than the normal ones, but who can easily be knocked into the abyss if you position yourself right (just watch out for his bleed infliction). As you reach the end of the bridge, two more Skeletons will rush toward you from the archway as a skeletal archer begins firing down at you from the platform on the left side - kill the Skeletons real quick and run through the archway to a room filled with pillars. Going up the stairs in here, you'll take out four more Skeletons (including the archer) and can turn right from the top of the stairs to reach a Soul of a Nameless Soldier past two more Skeletons wielding greatswords (watch out for when they're holding it in a block, as that means they're about to parry and Riposte you if you attack). Down the stairs from the pillar room are two more normal Skeletons and two Skeleton Swordsmen, all wielding greatswords, though they'll go down easily (and the latter will each drop a Carthus Rouge and Titanite Shard), with 2 Titanite Shards on a corpse next to the bottom of the stairs. Now, back at the bridge, look along the left side for a platform jutting out from the wall: Run off the side of the bridge onto the pillar and drop from there onto the platform, where you'll have a Skeleton on the right side to quickly kill as it comes to life. Through the arch here, you'll want to roll to avoid the impressive corkscrew stab of another Skeleton, and when he's out of commission, pick up the Carthus Pyromancy Tome from the body beyond him, then head into the hallway to the right of the arch, where attacking the wall at the end will reveal it as illusionary and let you pass into a chamber with a red-eyed, shotel-wielding, and very dangerous Skeleton Swordsman. This guy loooooooooves to dodge just as you begin your attack and hit you from any distance, either with his weapon or thrown Kukris, so be on your guard and press the attack; at the very least, your attacks will stagger him. When he's down for good, retrieve the Sharp Gem against the wall and turn left from where you came in through a hallway leading to another Soul of a Nameless Soldier. The ladder here leads up to the hall where you fought the first set of greatsword-wielding Skeletons, so double back and head through the OTHER hallway in that chamber to return to the stairs you were at earlier.

From here, head into the archway on the opposite side, dispatch the four Skeletons that rise there, and head down the stairs to the left (NOT the ones leading into the open air) to reach...Anri? Turns out they've been separated from Horace and intend to remain in the catacombs so he can make his way back, leaving you with a request to tell Horace this if you find him first. Just out the door from here, you'll find a Crystal Lizard - letting it run off the edge to its death will count as you killing it, netting you an easy Twinkling Titanite - and can pick up 3 Bloodred Moss Clump from the corpse in the corner. Return to where you were and head out the other archway onto the open-air stairs...then hop to the right so your first Skeleton Boulder can scream past without harming you. This thing is invulnerable and delivers plenty of knockback to everything it runs into, so make sure that isn't you; after it's gone up and down the stairs once, run down after it begins another descent, kill the Skeletons that attack you at the bottom (ideally fighting on one side of the platform there so you don't get slalomed) and wait until the Skeleton Boulder starts its ascent to head inside the tunnel here. On the right side, just past the arch, you'll see a Skeleton that's wearing a hat and...isn't attacking you. As it happens, this guy is CONTROLLING the Skeleton Boulder, and cutting him down (he'll try to run away when you do) will make said boulder explode into a comical amount of bones when it next hits the gate in this tunnel (you COULD use this to reach the Bonfire if it weren't broken...alas), allowing you to retrieve an Undead Bone Shard from the wreckage. Clear out the Skeletons in the hall past the gate - there's a new variant that throws dark projectile-spawning urns, so prioritize those first and foremost - and destroy the central row of vases here with Firebombs, as some will release more dark projectiles, to collect the Carthus Milkring (24/107) (raises DEX by 3 and obscures you when rolling, swap out Lloyd's Sword Ring for this immediately). You'll probably have noticed flaming arrows being fired at you from the wall at some point in this level; these are triggered by pressure plates on the ground, taking the form of these slightly-out-of-place square blocks:

Do your best to notice and step around these as you continue down the hall to an alcove with another Skeleton Swordsman and two regular Skeletons, one of which has more urns to throw. Down the hallway to the right here, there are two more Skeleton Swordsmen, these ones armed with leather shields that'll be hard to damage them through unless you get behind them, and a body with a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler (watch out for the pressure plate in front of it!). The end of the hallway has a pit you do not want to drop down into yet, but you can circle around it to collect an Ember before walking through the arch to the right, where another Skeleton Boulder will begin rolling along the perpendicular path at the end when you get close. Wait for it to pass, retrieve the Large Titanite Shard from the corpse to the left, and proceed along the path before taking the first left to reach and rest at the Bonfire (Catacombs of Carthus) that you saw before. Use this to pop back to the Firelink Shrine and burn that Undead Bone Shard to get an Estus Flask+4. When you're ready, return to the path, wait for the Skeleton Boulder to roll past to the right, and run down the stairs at the end of the path to reach another sewer area, with more Hound Rats waiting along with the Skeletons...and slimes, if all that wasn't enough! Turning right here will take you to another Large Hound Rat and down a hall with 2 Titanite Shards on the left (where a slime will drop down as you get close), where up ahead lie EVERYONE'S favorite enemy: Bonewheel Skeletons. While nowhere near as bad in this game as they were in the original, these guys can still be aggravating if you let them gang up on you. They move pretty fast when rolling, making them hard to hit, and only stop when they run into something or get far enough away from you - roll out of their way as they're moving, then run after them to cut them down right away. At the end of this hall, turn left to kill some slimes that drop from the ceiling collect the Carthus Bloodring (25/107), then return to where the Skeleton Boulder is rolling and (after making a backup save, if you like) enter the first doorway on the right toward a gate.

There's a large bridge beyond here and an Ember to pick up, but that's not the point (though you'll need to use the latter if you're not currently Enkindled); you're here to spawn in one of the most brutal mad spirits in the game, Knight Slayer Tsorig (whom you'll want to run past as he's spawning so you can battle him in the sewers). Fittingly dressed in Tarkus's armor and wielding the Fume Ultra Greatsword of DSII fame, Tsorig hits like a jet airliner to the temple and can easily three-shot you if you're not careful. Your best bet if you want to do this legit is to wait for him to complete a combo or heavy attack (where he pauses for a moment with the Fume Ultra Greatsword in front of him before bringing it over his head in a slam), then move in, perform maybe three attacks at most, and get out of range to repeat - it's suicide to try and tank his hits to keep attacking through them. If you're having trouble and/or want to cheese him, there's a method that will be described later on for taking him out easily (you can only spawn him here once, though, hence the backup save advice); whichever way you do it, his demise will reward you with his ironic gesture, "My thanks!" (24/33), and his stolen Knight Slayer Ring (26/107) (makes enemies lose more stamina when blocking your attacks). The next doorway near the corpse with 2 Titanite Shards, lit by candles, has stairs leading up to a Skeleton Swordsman wielding shotels, a red-eyed Skeleton shooting flaming arrows, and...another hat-wearing Skeleton that's controlling the Skeleton Boulder below (save him for last). Start by luring the Skeleton Swordsman down the stairs so you can engage him in a wider space without getting hassled, and once he's dead, kill the archer so you can collect the 3 Carthus Rouges from around the corner. After taking out the hat-wearing Skeleton, head through the hall behind the stairs to find another Skeleton Swordsman with shotels, this one with a fondness to hurl Throwing Knives at you, though he's not tougher than the rest beyond that. When the coast is clear, pick up a Large Titanite Shard and the Grave Warden's Ashes, then descend the stairs in this section of the upper area and attack the illusionary wall at the bottom to dispel it...and be immediately set upon by the Skeleton Swordsman a few steps away if you didn't take him out earlier.

Go back up the stairs to get the Skeleton Boulder rolling down again (it'll drop a Dark Gem...and a Lesser Crab...when it hits the wall and explodes) and rest at the Bonfire before you return to the last door, past the aforementioned Skeleton Swordsman, that leads to a cavern with the bridge you saw earlier. The Crystal Lizard here drops a Fire Gem when killed (try running to the side of it before it notices you so it runs into the cave wall instead of through the other entrance) and the Skeleton Swordsman looking out at the bridge can be backstabbed right off the damn cliff if you walk up to him, leaving you free to pick up the 3 Yellow Bug Pellets (temporarily reduces lightning damage taken) in the corner. The note on the ground here will warn you that the bridge is weakened, which you'll want to keep in mind - head through the stone arch, kill the Skeletons that get up, and pull the lever to open the gate you saw earlier - this will be crucial to the cheese strategy for Tsorig if you want to use it. Collect the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier and 2 Black Bug Pellets (temporarily reduces dark damage taken) from here before advancing toward the bridge. Prior to crossing it (or even getting close to its start) take a right and head up the slope to find Anri again, whom you'll have to tell that you still haven't seen Horace yet. When you go back down...oh boy, that's a ton of Skeletons, yeah? The usual strategy is to run across the bridge and have them follow, then attack the ropes on the side to make the bridge collapse and force all the Skeletons to fall into the pit - HOWEVER, if you're looking to cheese your fight with Tsorig, this is the main piece of the puzzle. It'll take some doing, but clear out the room of Skeletons beyond the now-opened gate and walk through that to spawn him; then, run back across the bridge, wait for him to cross it, aaaaand cut it down to send him plummeting to his death, which will earn you the same rewards as a proper fight with none of the hassle!

Regardless of what enemy you do it for, cutting down the bridge will actually turn it into a ladder, letting you descend to the dark depths below. Turning left from the bridge and entering a chamber at the end of the path will confront you with a second Fire Demon - and with no valiant Siegward around this time, you'll have to rely on other assistance. Specifically, before you even engage him, run right past the Fire Demon and toward the end of the upper platform to find a Mimic...and attack it once to wake it up, then double back toward the Fire Demon to lure them toward each other so you can watch the Mimic promptly KICK HIS ASS (then kill it yourself afterward to pick up the Black Blade). With the Fire Demon dead and a Soul of a Demon (safely consumable!) in your inventory, kill the Skeletons that rise up to retrieve the Large Titanite Shard and Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier before entering the hall beyond, where the corpse at the end holds the Old Sage's Blindfold and the Witch's Ring (27/107) (greatly boosts the power of pyromancies). Light + rest at the Bonfire (Abandoned Tomb) to the right, then double back to return to the bridge, climb it, and head through the cramped cavern beyond to reach a set of stone doors. Push these open, and you'll come to an ornate, but depressing room with a lone skull goblet sitting on a table before you. Well, your mother probably didn't warn you not to touch things what don't belong to you, so press in front of it and the Abyss will come pouring out, transporting you to a strange slope in pitch-black darkness, with only a corpse bearing the Grave Warden Pyromancy Tome lighting the path ahead. Nothing better to do than pick that up, right? Go right ahead...so you can come face-to-chin with High Lord Wolnir. Boo.

Despite being one of the largest and scariest bosses period in all of Dark Souls, High Lord Wolnir isn't too bad...if you fight him as intended. First and foremost, you'll notice the dark fog around his chest and occasionally being breathed out from his mouth to spread across the ground - this stuff will take off large chunks of your HP every second that you're in it, so you can't stay too close to him and need to run back up the slope until it dissipates whenever it comes from his mouth. Secondly, he'll attack with very long-reaching swipes of his arms, but these can be rolled through and are telegraphed pretty well, so don't panic about them. Thirdly, he can also summon Skeletons to attack you, but if you're fast enough he won't get the opportunity to...and if he does, well, he's liable to just kill them himself. There's admittedly a very damaging sword attack he can pull (telegraphed by a golden glow), but you're not likely to see it if you're efficient about this. See? Not as intimidating as he looks... ...if you're quick. Wolnir has the most absurd defense of any boss in the game and takes, at most, chip damage from direct attacks to his arm bones because the three glowing bangles on his wrists are the real targets of this battle; every time you destroy one with about 5 attacks, you'll vaporize over a third of Wolnir's HP, so getting rid of all 3 means you win. Simple, right? Well, the other mechanic at play here is the slope you're fighting on - you'll see Wolnir gradually pull himself up it as the fight continues, and while destroying a bangle will send him sliding down several yards, he'll just keep on pulling himself up otherwise...right up until you're trapped between him and the wall at the back, with nowhere to run and nowhere to hide when he breathes the fog down on you. Consequently, there's a time limit to this battle; it's honestly hard to actually reach said High Lord Wolnir

time limit because of how easy it is to destroy the bangles, but don't get complacent and keep attacking whenever you can until the bastard slides down to hell. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the past and former king claimed by the Abyss, you'll receive the Soul of High Lord Wolnir (do not consume this!)... ...and use the newly-formed Bonfire (High Lord Wolnir) to, once again, return to Firelink Shrine.

First off, head over to Ludleth and Transpose the Soul of High Lord Wolnir into Black Serpent (6/27) before giving the Grave Warden's Ashes to the Handmaid; you should also take the opportunity to purchase Lloyd's Shield Ring (28/107) from her. Next, go to Andre and Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades to +5, then descend the stairs to the right so you can give Cornyx the Carthus Pyromancy Tome you found - he'll actually refuse to take the Grave Warden Pyromancy Tome because of how dangerous it is, so you'll have to find another teacher for its spells. In the passage past Greirat, you'll discover that Yoel of Londor has suddenly ceased to breathe, he's pushing up daisies, and so on...this won't mean anything for your current or next playthrough, but it'll be a crucial step in your third playthrough, so keep that in mind. With everything else handled for now, return to the Fire Keeper and raise your Ashen One to level 57 with the following specifications (you might be a few hundred Souls short of the final level, so Travel to the Abyss Watchers Bonfire and run outside to kill Ghrus if you need it): Now, you're ready to move on; but before you can enter the mysterious valley, you're going to Travel to the Abandoned Tomb Bonfire that you set up earlier so you can enter an optional area: the Smouldering Lake.

From the Bonfire, running through the arch into the cave, where you'll emerge to a surreal vista of burning trees and...an ominous rumbling sound. Advance into the thankfully benign water, and you'll discover that the noise is coming from a gigantic triple crossbow, the Giant Avelyn, mounted high up in the cavern - this thing shoots equally gigantic bolts at you in bursts of three, and your only hope of avoiding them is to hide behind the nearest tree, then wait for the lull between the third bolt of the current set and the first bolt of the next to run to the next tree as you explore the lake. First and foremost, get to the closest tree on the right, then dash to this opening in the rock wall behind and to the right of it: Inside, you'll find a Crystal Lizard that drops a Twinkling Titanite and another that'll give you a Titanite Chunk, and in the body of water beyond (directly underneath the former bridge), you'll find Horace!...who, regrettably, has gone Hollow and will attack you on sight. He's not too strong, but his spinning attack with his halberd is one you'll want to watch out for - once he's down, collect his Llewellyn Shield and the 2 Large Titanite Shards + 2 Yellow Bug Pellets from the surrounding corpses before returning to the lake. There are items and enemies here that you simply cannot deal with while the Giant Avelyn is active, BUT you're going to make use of them to access a few things you can't otherwise. First, cross the lake toward this conspicuous stack of bricks: After the current round of bolts ends, stand in front of the bricks and look up at the Giant Avelyn so you can see when the next bolt fires, then run like hell once it is so that it hits the bricks, destroying them and revealing a body with the Speckled Stoneplate Ring (29/107) (slightly raises

defense against all elemental attacks). Then, head to the middle of the lake and stand on this arrangement of cobblestones: When the bolts strike this, they'll break open a large hole in the ground, letting you drop through into a stone tunnel. In here, run past the enemy and turn left to light and rest at the Bonfire (Old King's Antechamber), then Travel back to the Abandoned Tomb to return to the lake and head to the left...where you'll be jumpscared by the local Carthus Sandworm, a massive and extremely powerful miniboss that spits fricking lightning and would most assuredly kick your ass if you fought it head-on. Luckily, because the Giant Avelyn is still active, you don't have to; navigate around the right side of it, dodging its beams as best you can, and turn left when you see the fog door in the distance to reach a small path against the rock wall, where you'll want to position yourself behind this boulder at the bottom of the path like so: The Giant Avelyn will continue to shoot at you here, but the rock will protect you from pretty much every shot (assuming you're in the right place)...unfortunately, the Sandworm won't be so lucky and will go down in about 10 hits, giving you Lightning Stake (9/35) and an Undead Bone Shard. Additionally, the bodies now exposed where the Sandworm was hold a Large Titanite Shard and the Shield of Want (Vendrick's shield, increases how many Souls you absorb from enemies - swap out the Grass Crest Shield for this right away). You're going to be ignoring the fog door for now in favor of heading up the slope to the right of it, which will take you to another Large Titanite Shard and the next Bonfire (Demon Ruins) - use this to pop back to the Firelink Shrine and not only burn the Undead Bone Shard, but Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades to +6.

Back in the Demon Ruins, advancing down the stairs beyond the Bonfire will bring you to a hall filled with dead demons, Ghrus, and Demon Clerics that'll prove themselves dangerous up close and from afar with their greatswords and fireballs. Prioritize them, then the Ghrus in any encounter as you explore and collect a Titanite Shard + Ember from the corpses. Descend the stairs, and you'll be confronted by two Demon Clerics that'll likely have set up several floating fireballs to pelt you with projectiles while you're fighting them, which you can make less aggravating by hiding behind the pillars as much as you can. At the far end of the hall, a dead Stray Demon will be lying in front of another Undead Bone Shard (and a lava-like slime will drop onto you just as you get close, so be wary). Return to the upper floor and cross to the other side of the hall, where two normal Ghru and a Ghru Shaman await you; once they're dead, proceed into the hallway next to them. Here, you'll find a Ghru sitting in front of a much larger and dead demon - walk forward slowly and turn your camera to the left so you can see a second Ghru standing around the corner and take him out first before the sitting one. Through the archway in the corner of this room, you'll find not only another lava slime above an Ember, but a Demon Statue, returning from the first game; these guys breathe fire with quite a bit of range, but go down in a couple of hits. Rather than drop down through the hole here, go back to the main floor and head into the hallway on the left (the one with the dead demon lying in it), where a Ghru will run at you from the left when you reach the corner -kill him, then attack the arch-shaped wall at the end to dispel it as an illusion, bringing you to a room where another Black Knight is in the process of curb-stomping a Ghru. This guy will be a hell of a lot easier to kill than the first one you encountered with how much more damage you're putting out, and especially if you start attacking him while he's finishing off the Ghru (though you'll want to watch out for his greataxe combo and dragging attack), so once he's down, pick up the Black Knight Sword from next to the pile of Taurus Demon corpses in the corner of the room and head back to the hallway.

Turning right to face the direction that the Ghru ambushed you from, proceed and dispatch two more Ghrus and Demon Statues, then advance into the next room filled with pillars. Here, you'll want to take out the patrolling Ghru first and foremost so you can turn left into the hall adjacent to the set of stairs in the right corner of the room, where turning right in the middle will show you a corpse with an Ember sitting at the end of the corridor. The end of the hall brings you to a sitting Ghru with a spear and shield; take him out right away to prevent him from jumping you as you turn left again and kill the Ghru Shaman that's sitting to the left of the entrance. Now that the room is clear, go up the stairs and you'll return to the Old King's Antechamber Bonfire for a much-needed rest. Here, in the far corner, you'll find another arch wall: Attack this to dispel the illusion and run through, then turn left before the end of the hallway (which leads into the air above the larger hall you were in earlier with the Demon Clerics) to find a corridor with five lava slimes on the ceiling. You'll want to lure them into dropping down one at a time so you can kill them all safely before collecting the Estus Shard at the end - now's a good time to return to the Firelink Shrine and use this, as well as the Undead Bone Shard, to get up to 11 Estus Flask+6 before going any further. Through the doorway next to the Bonfire, you'll have to dispatch a Demon Cleric and, in the room beyond, lure out the two Ghrus flanking the doorway one at a time (or just get one out, then kill the other while he's sitting down) prior to taking out the Ghru in front of the large demon corpse to collect the Izalith Pyromancy Tome; additionally, returning to the corridor linking the two rooms and taking a few left turns (you'll recognize this as where you fell down from the lake earlier) will let you find and hunt down a Crystal Lizard for its Chaos Gem.

To delve deeper into what remains of Lost Izalith, retrace your steps to the main hall and, without engaging the enemies there, run into the tunnel to the left of where you emerge (the one with a Hound Rat waiting in the distance). Turn right at the stairs in here and enter a room with a central pillar, dispensing of Hound Rats all the while - the wall directly opposite the stairs here is another illusion, and striking it will let you enter the other side of a hallway you were cut off from by a hole earlier, where the corpse of Quelana lies with her sister and the Quelana Pyromancy Tome... take however long you need to compose yourself and turn left from this sorry scene to reach a pit of molten lava. There's only one thing you need from here - the item closest to you - but braving the forbidden candy will require you to briefly swap out the Carthus Milkring for the Flame Stoneplate Ring and get ready to chug Estus Flasks, as well as evade or preemptively kill the lava slimes that'll approach you here. Run into the lava, down 1-2 Estus Flasks whenever your HP gets dangerously low, and collect Toxic Mist (7/27) before hightailing it back to dry land; there's a decent chance you'll die if you're not very trigger-happy with , but it won't take long to get back here if you do, and you do want that trophy...
