After returning to the Bonfire to recoup whatever you spent, heading back to the pillar room, descend the stairs through the archway on the right and follow them to a hall with a Giant Hound Rat at the end - take him out (and the five Hound Rats hiding behind him), then descend the stairs to reach a room filled with several Basilisks. Because of how quickly your curse gauge will build up from being ganged up on by these guys, you'll want to dispatch them one at a time, either by expertly snaking your way through the pillars to sneak up behind them or getting their attention and running back up the stairs to engage them in a more open space. When the coast is clear, pick up a Titanite Scale from the end of the room and return to the hall, where striking the left wall just before the (former) location of the Giant Hound Rat will dispel it as an illusion, revealing a chest with 3 Large Titanite Shards...and attacking the wall behind that will let you drop down to a ledge with the Izalith Staff!

Now, heal up and proceed into the corridor opposite the ledge once you drop down from it, which leads to another set of stairs; at the base of these, turn left to enter a tunnel that leads to a lake of lava...and the real Knight Slayer Tsorig, back for a rematch! If you beat him legitimately last time, same rules apply (waiting for him to perform a heavy attack before exploiting the pause afterward with your own attacks) - if not, you can cheese the hell right out of this fight by running past him to the lava and throwing an Alluring Skull into it, which will compel Tsorig to run right in and burn to death in seconds flat without laying a finger on you. Once he's dead (you'll have to reload the game if you use the latter method), collect his Fume Ultra Greatsword and Black Iron Greatshield before re-equipping your Flame Stoneplate Ring and running into the lava toward the item on the left side, a.k.a. Sacred Flame (8/27) (you should be able to just barely make it there and back if you have 6+ Estus Flasks left; if not, return to the Bonfire to replenish them first). After replenishing yourself at the Bonfire (again) and making your way back to the aforementioned second set of stairs in the Basilisk room, which you'll want to ascend to a bridge running over the lava pond. On the other side waits another Black Knight, who'll be more threatening than usual since you run the risk of falling or being knocked off the bridge into the lava as a sure death sentence, though you can still shred through his HP with a combo after he performs a heavy attack; opposite his starting position, you can pick up a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight before heading out to the ladders in the rocky quarry beyond. From the top of the second ladder, drop down to the right to collect the Dragonrider Bow and again to climb back up the ladder, where running ahead will bring you to a crumbling brick wall...beyond which lies the Giant Avelyn! The brick walls will only offer protection once against the massive bolts, so you'll need to line up the trees and proper rock walls between yourself and the machinery to actually survive.

From where you are now, turn left and run into a lower section of the cliff (with a corpse bearing 2 Homeward Bones in the corner) that leads to a tunnel, at the end of which lies a forked path - to the right, you'll see three Bonewheel Skeletons ready to ruin your day, while the left only has a couple Skeletons at first...and then two Skeleton Swordsman, more than happy to mess you RIGHT up if you aggro both of them at once. Lure the closer one down to you while the upper one is walking toward the Giant Avelyn, then deal with the second one when he's alone. At the top of the slope, you'll find that the Giants mean to man this gigantic weapon are long dead, leaving you free to turn it off yourself by walking up to the right side of the lever and pressing . It'll be safe for you to return to the lake below (well, relatively safe - the Great Crabs are still patrolling there), and you can do so quickly by dropping off the cliff to the right of the Giant Corpses onto a series of rock ledges. On the lake once more, collect whatever Large Titanite Shards remain and return to the Old King's Antechamber Bonfire, then Travel to the Demon Ruins Bonfire, where you'll see a summon sign for Knight Slayer Tsorig in the corner - call upon him and head down to the stairs leading to the fog door, at the base of which you'll find another summon sign for Great Swamp Cuculus, a pyromancer that you'll want to bring along as well. After equipping the Flame Stoneplate Ring one more time and equipping (+using) Red Bug Pellets in a Quick Item slot, head up the stairs and through the fog door (first of its kind in the game!...if you haven't died, at least) to face the Old Demon King. Perhaps the most ancient and wizened demon to ever live, the Old Demon King is still far from a pushover, and you're gonna need those two spirits to help see you through this. The main danger of this guy is the hits from his massive hammer, which can easily take off a third of your HP with each blow and covers a ridiculous range; even if he's focusing on Tsorig and Cuculus, it's still pretty likely that those swings will hit you and hurt. When you're up-close and personal, he also enjoys smashing his hammer end-first right in front of his feet and/or vomiting lava that'll spread outward in a decent-sized pool. As such, the key to staying alive and relatively un-burnt is to constantly weave in and out of his close range, getting a few attacks in and then retreating to a safe distance so you can continue rolling through his strikes. Tsorig will function as an excellent tank and Cuculus will poison him pretty effectively if given the opportunity, so they more than pull their weight here.

At 50% HP, the Old Demon King will flare up with flames and not only start doing more damage, but gain two new wide-ranging attacks - a smash of his hammer on the ground that will create an expanding ring of fire around himself, and a raising of it above his head that will create several large fireballs in the air before they start homing in on you and the spirits. For the former, run the hell away (in the direction with the most room... it can get a little cramped during this fight, what with all the mounds of demon corpses) and wait for it to subside; for the latter, you'll want to retreat to a medium distance so the Old Demon King doesn't capitalize on the distraction by crushing you to a paste, then roll through the fireballs as they approach you. Otherwise, the strategy remains the same, with one caveat: at roughly 10% HP, the Old Demon King will go through a unique and somewhat slow animation where he'll huddle down and release a massive explosion that, if it hits you, is almost guaranteed to kill you...but also leaves him near-helpless and unable to fight back. It's up to you if you want to exploit the animation to get your last few hits there and then, risking the OHKO, or retreat to a safe distance and finish him off in that weakened state. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Old Demon King With the last of the demons (well, sorta) reduced to ashes, you'll receive the Soul of the Old Demon King (do not consume this!)... ...and a new Bonfire (Old Demon King) to light and return to the Firelink Shrine with.

Not as much to do here this time, but still worth detailing. First, as you're probably getting used to by now, run up to Ludleth and Transpose that Soul of the Old Demon King into Chaos Bed Vestiges (9/27); then, head over to Cornyx and give him the Izalith Pyromancy Tome (while grateful for the chance to look upon it, he won't accept the Quelana Pyromancy Tome since it has to be read by a female pyromancer; what a king). After selling whatever you don't need at the Handmaid (this can include the Titanite Shards and Large Titanite Shards, since you won't need to level up any more weapons and armor can't be Reinforced in this game), use your two Soul Chunks and raise your Ashen One to level 61 with the following specifications: With all that done, return to the High Lord Wolnir Bonfire and proceed through the door at the top of the stairs, then up the steps beyond it, to reach the only Dark Souls location cool enough to host an aurora borealis: Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

Take a moment to gaze out on the beautiful vista before turning left and lighting the Bonfire (Irithyll of the Boreal Valley) on your way to the prominent bridge below...and as you cross this, keep the camera pointed behind yourself at the archway, like so: Why? Well, around when you reach the halfway point of the bridge, a new and quite fierce enemy will appear - Sulyvahn's Beast, a large dog-like monster that hits hard and moves way faster than it should. Your best bet for dispatching this (thankfully non-respawning) bastard is to first use a Carthus Rouge to apply bleed to your attacks, then roll through his bites and swipes until he bites twice in a row; after the second bite, he'll pause momentarily, giving you a window to get a couple attacks in (ideally on his head, where he takes the most damage and can be stunned) before resuming your evasion. For your trouble, you'll receive the Pontiff's Right Eye (30/107) (slightly increases attack power with consecutive attacks) and can safely cross the rest of the bridge, where you'll see a unique mist wall just before the plaza on the other side (as well as a corpse with a Homeward Bone against the left railing). If you didn't have the Small Doll from the Cathedral of the Deep, you'd be blocked from passing through here - good thing you were efficient and picked that up already! On the other side, light the second Bonfire (Central Irithyll) and briefly return to the Firelink Shrine to talk to Greirat, whom you can send out to plunder the city now; because you saved Seigward earlier, you'll be able to properly progress their storylines now. Back in Central Irithyll, pick up the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier from the body on the railing to the right of the bridge, the Rime-blue Moss Clump (cures frostbite and reduces frost buildup) from in front of the Bonfire, and the Soul of a Weary Warrior from the opposite side of the main fountain here - then, double back onto the bridge and head over to the red-orange message sign that you may have noticed earlier, where there will now be a new type of summon sign to the right:

Instead of bringing a spirit into your world, this sends you to the aid of a spirit in their world...in this case, your new friend Sirris, who seeks help against a foe that may be familiar to players of the previous game: ! Turns out he's a murderer (and one of Rosaria's Fingers) and must be punished, so gang up on him with Sirris - she doesn't have a lot of HP so you'll have to SHOW SPOILER carry the battle for her, but with your damage output, you shouldn't have much trouble even with the significant chunks of HP that he can take off. Afterwards, you'll return to your own world and should, once again, return to the Firelink Shrine to talk to Sirris, who'll reward you with the Blessed Mail Breaker and her very unique Silvercat Ring (31/107) (prevents damage from falling unless it's a lethal drop). Now, Travel back and head up the stairs beyond the Bonfire to face your first Pontiff Knights, ethereal-yet-brutal warriors that attack very fast and can close a large distance in seconds, either with a lunging slash or a dark projectile - crucially, though, they don't have much HP and will go down in two L1 attacks if you can roll through their combos and get behind/to the side of them. There are two patrolling the main road, and you'll want to lure them over one at a time if you can; going too far ahead will attract the attention of a third on some stairs to the right that'll happily surprise-attack you while you're engaged with the others, so try to leave him for last. When the coast is clear, collect another Soul of a Weary Warrior from a corpse hanging over the railing next to the initial set of stairs and a Large Titanite Shard from the body at the top of the side-set of stairs before proceeding long the main path, which will bring you to another new enemy type: Irithyllian Slaves. These guys don't look imposing, but it's difficult to stagger them (unless you hit them with a running L1 - thanks to YostYosteen94 for the tip!) and they do quite a bit of damage with their swords, even the non-infused ones - it's almost impossible to not take them on 2-3 at a time, but be ready to roll at any moment when you do so you don't get combo'd to death.

Then, of course, there's the guy leading the second group of Irithyllian Slaves that you come across, down the steps to the left; a Fire Witch, which is more of a large knight wielding a giant stave that can cast unfair pyromancies (they pass through walls and go WAY further than the ones you can cast do). You'll want to first lure the Irithyllian Slaves away from him, then rush in to attack him up-close - ironically, he CAN be staggered by your attacks, so he should go down quickly, leaving you free to pick up a Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier and a Budding Green Blossom (stronger version of the Green Blossom) from the small fountain here. Now, go up the stairs along the main path and hug the right side as you run past the flames from the Fire Witch on the balcony to the right, which you can reach at the top of the path by turning right onto a set of stairs; kill him and collect the Large Titanite Shard from the nearby balcony, then head back to take on the two Pontiff Knights coming down the way one at a time (even if they both notice you at the same time, one is likely to stay back and cast those dark projectiles while the other rushes toward you). The set of stairs on the left ahead bear a Crystal Lizard that'll give you a Twinkling Titanite, but there's more to this balcony than meets the eye. See this well-lit section of the railing on the right-hand side? Attacking this will reveal a hidden set of stairs leading into the courtyard below, which will bring you to another Large Titanite Shard (and a Pontiff Knight hiding in the alley to the left of the stairs) and lead down to a bridge overlooking a strange, shrieking Evangelist hunched over in the snow. Drop down and kill her - she won't attack you until you attack her, so you can take off most of her HP before she even gets to her feet - and you'll receive Dorhys' Gnawing (10/35). After retrieving the Witchtree Branch from underneath the tree here, open the gate and retrace your way back up to where you were. Through the large arch at the end of the path, you'll see another Fire Witch flanked by two Pontiff Knights, as the game was simply too easy up until this point; before you get close to the arch (which will cause the enemies to start approaching you), collect the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier from the corpse in front of a statue on the left, then a Large Titanite Shard from a body on a balcony to the right, and finally ANOTHER Large Titanite Shard on

a corpse next to a tree on the left side just before the stairs. As for the enemies: the best way to engage this group is to stand still until the Fire Witch stops and starts firing off pyromancies while the Pontiff Knights keep walking, which will let you battle them apart from the Fire Witch (and likely take them both out with a couple attacks) before you finish him off. Past the arch, turn left and quickly run over to the next Fire Witch to cut him down, then pick up the Soul of a Weary Warrior that he was guarding and head up the stairs, where advancing along the walkway to the left will bring you to a second Soul of a Weary Warrior. From the gate at the top of the stairs that you passed earlier, turn right, take out the Pontiff Knight, and pick up the Lightning Gem next to him before attacking the wall opposite the archway you just passed through to dispel it as an illusion, allowing you to head over to a corpse on the railing and pick up the Magic Clutch Ring (32/107) (increases magic damage, but decreases defense). Now, go out through the arch and turn right to head up the stairs you ignored earlier, where the next Bonfire (Church of Yorshka) lies...and to the right, Anri! Since you killed Horace after talking to them, they won't know of his fate but will thank you for hearing them out with the Ring of the Evil Eye (33/107) (restores HP every time you kill an enemy) - talking to them a second time will also give you their second gesture, "Quiet Resolve" (25/33). After retrieving a Proof of a Concord Kept (yet another covenant item that you'll be farming later), go over to these statues in the corner: The one directly in the corner is, in fact, an assassin out for Anri's head, and you can't have that! Attack and cut her down in a couple strikes, and you'll not only gain Chameleon (6/34), but have access to Anri as a spirit to summon for a future boss fight (and trust us, you'll want their help).

Head down the stairs opposite Anri into a graveyard (turn right just after the stairs, and you can pick up a Roster of Knights on a corpse), where you'll start seeing smoky orbs with two pinpricks of light hanging in the air; these are Irithyllian Slaves that only become visible when you get within a couple of feet of them, so attack as soon as you can before they jump you. After collecting the Fading Soul on the cliff here, turn right up the path toward a Corvian praying at a gravestone...and as you approach (and collect another Fading Soul), good ol' will spawn at the nearby tree to get revenge on you for his humiliating defeat earlier! While you won't have Sirris to help you this time around, you can defeat the bastard far easier by simply pushing him over the nearby edge with a few attacks, netting you his Dragonslayer's Axe - then, dispatch the Corvian and collect not only the 3 Homeward Bones in front of him, but the Undead Bone Shard that's behind the grave. Return to the "start" of the graveyard and take the stairs leading down to the left of the entrance, which will bring you between a few buildings. To the left, after ridding yourself of another hidden Irithyllian Slave, head through the alley to face three of a new variant of Starved Hound that have human skulls...somehow...and hit harder than the others, though they'll go down just as easy. Once you've retrieved the 8 Kukris and Rusted Gold Coin from the corpses here, return to the alley and descend into a basement filled with invisible Irithyllian Slaves, visible only by their smoke and eyes. Go down the stairs and slaughter them all; be wary of the ones whose eyes are lower to the ground, as they're crawling and are not only harder to hit, but liable to attack you as you're trying to slash them. When the coast is more or less clear, pick up 2 Blue Bug Pellets from the left and climb a ladder on the right to reach the rafters, where a few more Irithyllian Slaves await (some may have fallen down while you were clearing out the others), with one on the far side liable to sling sorceries at you too. Pick up the Shriving Stone to the left and cross the rafters to the far end on the right, where you'll see a wooden platform to this right below:

SHOW SPOILER Drop down onto this and open the chest to collect Yorshka's Spear before returning to the floor below, killing any stragglers, and going outside onto a long set of stairs where even more Irithyllian Slaves await. When you reach the bottom (just before the water) and turn right, one in front of the tree at the far end will let out an ear-piercing shriek, signaling the others to start running over and attacking you, so prepare for some bullshit as you try and fend off half a dozen mostly-invisible enemies. At the tree, take out the asshole and retrieve the Blood Gem, then enter the water, collect the 3 Green Blossoms, and turn right toward an item. As you get close, the lump in the water will bolt up and reveal itself to be a Sewer Centipede, a creepy multi-armed thing that likes to scuttle around and jump at you with its chest-mouth wide open, though it thankfully goes down in a couple of attacks. Once you've taken the Ring of Sacrifice next to it, head down the river path toward a wider area where, since you killed it earlier, you thankfully WON'T have to contend with Sulyvahn's Beast and can not only freely collect the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier on the right, but head even further in this direction to find two more Sewer Centipedes half-hiding in the water (kill them while they're hunched over) as well as a Man Grub corpse bearing Great Heal (11/35), after which you can return to the main river, pick up the 4 Green Blossoms along the wall, and head into the building at the end to light and rest at the next Bonfire (Distant Manor) - for now, do not go down the stairs past this Bonfire, as it'll trigger the death of an NPC. After briefly returning to the Firelink Shrine so you can burn the Undead Bone Shard and go up to Estus Flask+7, double back to the river and look along the wall on the right to enter a sewer filled with Sewer Centipedes (noticeable in this lighting for their long hair floating in the water), whom you'll want to approach and engage one at a time while circling around the room; when it's clear, pick up the 6 Dung Pies on the two corpses here and the, uh...Excrement-Covered Ashes from an alcove next to the stairs on the opposite side of the room, which you'll want to ascend to find none other than Siegward, now dozing by a cozy fire. Talk to him a few times, and he'll not only give you Emit Force (12/35) and another hearty Siegbräu, but mention that he has a "grave promise" to keep in the Profaned Capital, an area you'll be visiting later. Oh, and he'll heal you right up too! Plus, there's another Estus Soup waiting for you on the stove nearby - keep it in mind for after the next battle.

Now, going up the stairs and to the right here will bring you to a familiar-feeling area (for players of the first game), complete with another enemy returning from the same title: Silver Knights, one of whom is admiring a portrait of Gwynevere - understandably so - while another is waiting on the balcony to the right of where you walk in, ready to put a bolt in your back the moment you move to engage the first one. These guys are demonstrably tougher than they were in their first appearance, not only having quite a bit of HP but also being able to infuse their swords with lightning to hit for a third of your HP. The best course here is to first lure the admiring Silver Knight back to the previous room so you can fight him without being shot, then head up the stairs to the left of the Gwynevere Painting and kill the Silver Knight waiting for you there before dispatching the archer (who'll unfortunately pull out the same sword-and-shield combo when you get too close), allowing you to cross to the other side of the balcony above the painting and open three chests for Smough's Great Hammer, a Divine Blessing, and the iconic Leo Ring (34/107). You might be starting to wonder why all this is here... From behind the Gwynevere painting, exit the building and ascend the stairs to the left, along the way of which you'll be attacked by two more Starved Hounds and (if you're Enkindled) invaded by a Londor Pale Shade, who attacks with claws and dark projectiles; he can certainly shred through your HP in seconds if given the opportunity, but you can do the same to him so long as you continually strafe around him. Once you've received his Manikin Claws for defeating him, continue up the stairs and take out the two Irithyllian Slaves firing sorceries at you and another two Starved Hounds, double back to pick up the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier from a corpse next to a tree next to the penultimate set of stairs, and head to the top to find yourself being bombarded by two more Irithyllian Slaves. After cutting down the Starved Hound waiting behind the fountain/statue here, quickly take out the Slaves and retrieve the Large Titanite Shard from the balcony near the doorway on the left, which you'll want to pass through to ride a lift up to a gate that connects to the large archway you were battling the Pontiff Knights and Fire Witches at earlier.

Ride the lift back down and climb the curving stairs up to a building chock-full of Irithyllian Slaves, with two more sorcery-casting ones waiting at the top. Before you deal with them, lure all the normal ones on the ground floor outside onto the stairs so you can engage them with less risk, then run up and kill the sorcerers before descending the ladder to collect another Large Titanite Shard (there's also 2 Blue Bug Pellets on the ground floor if you want them). Through the archway at the top, you'll go outside once again to collect a Soul of a Weary Warrior...then wait at the bottom of the stairs here for the patrolling Pontiff Knights above (one of whom is wielding a scythe for some reason, giving him even more range) to come down and attack you one at a time. Once you've done so, descend the stairs on the other side of the pavilion here to reach the locked gate from earlier, which you can open now, as well as an Ember (and the last two Irithyllian Slaves that'll jump you), before returning to the front of the cathedral and looking over the ledge between the two statues here: This is the only way to reach the item on the throne you saw earlier, so after going through the gate on the side to clear out the enemies below or preparing yourself to run for your life once you land in front of them, equip the Silvercat Ring in a slot of your choice and drop down to pick up the Ring of the Sun's First Born (35/107) (increases miracle damage). After making your way back up to the cathedral, summon Anri of Astora from in front of the statue on the left (facing the fog), equip Charcoal and/or Gold Pine Resins, and pass through the fog door to face the most lore-important midgame boss in any Soulsborne title ever: Pontiff Sulyvahn. Befitting his important role in the story, Pontiff Sulyvahn does not mess around. He'll be standing still at first (use this time to apply your Pine Resin of choice, as he's weak to both damage types), but when you get closer to him, he'll light up his greatswords and leap over to start swinging; these slashes have huge arcs and hit for a lot of damage/stagger, so rolling through them is imperative to survival. Thankfully, Anri is pretty beefy at this point and can not only dish out damage only a Pontiff Sulyvahn

little below your own, but take quite a lot in return and heal right back up, so rely on them to draw Sulyvahn's attention while you attack him from behind. Above all else, avoid being caught in one of his rapid combos and stay either to the side or behind him at all times. At 50% HP, Sulyvahn undergoes a couple of drastic changes - first, he'll kneel down and release an explosion of dark while sprouting two wings from his back, which you'll want to be far away from him during, and then not only start dealing more damage, but unleash aerial diving attacks (telegraphed by him leaping up high) and fire sorceries from his blue blade, though you can evade or prevent the latter pretty well by simply staying close to him. The true danger here, though, is the clone that he repeatedly spawns following this; composed of an ethereal pink energy, the clone hits just as hard as the real Sulyvahn AND performs the same attacks as him (about a second ahead), making for double trouble if you happen to be caught in the path of their techniques...and it likes to teleport around after a couple of attacks, just to make your life more interesting. Thankfully, Anri will still draw their attention/let you go 2v2 a lot of the time and the clone has its own, much smaller HP bar, so you can kill it pretty quickly (and damage Sulyvahn with the same attacks if he's close enough) and get back to the main event, which should be over quickly if you capitalize on attacking the real Sulyvahn during the periods where he's without his clone and exploit those damage weaknesses. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the most moral politician forced into a permanent retirement, you'll receive the Soul of Pontiff Sulyvahn (which CAN be consumed!)... ...and a new Bonfire (Pontiff Sulyvahn) to light and rest at. Before going any further, pop back to Firelink Shrine for a minute - time to level up!

Since you don't have anything to Transpose for this time around, you can safely consume all your Soul Chunks and give the Excrement-Covered Ashesto the Handmaid, whom you should also sell your excess inventory to (which should put you at or above 199,000 Souls - grind for them around Central Irithyll if not); then, raise your Ashen one up to level 69 with the following specifications: With that done, return to the Pontiff Sulyvahn Bonfire and head outside to find two Crystal Lizards, each of whom will drop a Twinkling Titanite upon death - turning right from the exit will also bring you to a Large Titanite Shard. Now, head up the stairs on the other side, where you'll see...a castle that couldn't possibly be here, could it? Oh, make no mistake at all - that is indeed Anor Londo.

Turning right after the stunning sight at the top of the stairs here, you'll see a pavilion of (mostly) dead Giant Slaves and two all-too-alive enemies waiting for you on the other side - but you do not want to engage them right away. Instead, head toward the walkway running through the middle of this area and drop down into the pillar-filled hallway underneath it, where going right will bring you to four Irithyllian Slaves and a body with the Dark Stoneplate Ring (36/107) (reduces dark damage taken). Up the stairs on the opposite end of this hallway (closer to where you dropped in), you'll reach the top of the walkway and be faced with the Devouts of the Deep, identical to the Deacons of the Deep...though as you might expect, these guys don't share an HP bar and thus go down much easier than the actual boss did (aside from the fat one patrolling closest to you, who has more HP than the others and is hard to stagger). So long as you keep moving to avoid the fireballs that they'll all be casting, it's relatively easy to move through the crowd and cut them down one at a time. However, leave the one at the end of the walkway for last... ...because once you get close enough to him, you'll attract the attention of the Drang Knights that you were avoiding below. Hailing from none other than Drangleic, these guys dual-wield spears and hammers for hard-hitting combos and possess quite a bit more HP than most non-bosses, so you'll want to engage them one at a time (thankfully, they're liable to run up either one at a time or far apart enough that this is doable) and roll through their attacks until you see an opening to strike; if they don't roll out of it, you can easily kill them in one L1 L1 L1 combo.

When the coast is more or less clear, descend the stairs to the pavilion and carefully pick up the 2 Embers and Soul of a Weary Warrior between the bodies - one of the Giant Slaves is liable to get up and start attacking you during this, but you can trick him into getting stuck by luring him toward the stairs, going up one set, and coming down the other to attack him from behind. You can also collect a Large Titanite Shard from the balcony facing that beautiful moon before going back up the stairs and doubling back across the walkway to the stairs you originally ascended. From here, turn left along a snow-covered path toward the corpse you likely saw earlier, which carries another Large Titanite Shard, prior to re-entering the cathedral from the archway past the stairs. Here, you'll first want to take the lift down on the left to create a shortcut back to the Bonfire, then ride it back up and turn right toward the curving set of stairs to reach the other side of this upper floor, where you can find a Crystal Lizard around the corner that'll drop a Simple Gem...which, as it happens, is the fifteenth and final type you can collect, though you don't yet have the Embers to use them all. Now cross the bridge next to the lift and, on the right, you'll see a chest - nice try, Mimic! Kill it for the Golden Ritual Spear, and you can return to the tower on the other side of the walkway/at the top of the stairs leading up from the Giants (you'll have to clear out the Deacons of the Deep if you rested at the Bonfire during all this, though). Inside the tower, turn left and find this wall in the corner: Attack this to dispel the illusory wall and descend the ladder behind it to find...well... TWO Sulyvahn's Beasts. The same tactics apply as when you fought the first one on the bridge, but to avoid getting absolutely curb-stomped by facing both at once, hug the right wall and engage the one on the right first, staying firmly on that side of the room, BEFORE taking on the other one. It'll probably eat through most of your Estus Flasks, but the reward for slaying both is well worth it: the Ring of Favor (37/107) (increases max HP, stamina, and equipment load), which if you have the requisitely light armor shown above by now, you'll want to swap out Havel's Ring for right away because, with your heightened VIT, you'll maintain your roll while also boosting your stats.

Additionally, you'll be able to collect a Deep Gem and Human Dregs (covenant item, yippee), and in the corner, you'll find the corpse of Archdeacon McDonnell, which you can pray to in order to join the Aldrich Faithful! Light and rest at the Bonfire (Water Reserve) before climbing back up the ladder and ascending the stairs in the tower. On the landing at the top of the stairs, you'll find a Titanite Scale on the corner facing the main cathedral and moon. From the opposite corner, you'll be dropping down onto a buttress with a Large Titanite Shard on the other side and facing more Silver Knights that'll be sniping at you from afar (sorry for the PTSD, players of the first game). First, you're going to run up to the one on the buttress you're currently standing on so he switches to his sword and shield, then lure him down onto the ramp portion you used to approach him so you can fight him with substantially more breathing room. Continue up the buttress once he's out of the picture to the landing at the top, where another Silver Knight awaits; if you stay at arm's length until he starts nocking an arrow and THEN run over to attack him, you can actually shred through his HP before he can properly draw his sword. Proceeding along this familiar walkway, you can sneak up on the Silver Knight looking out over the vista and cut him down in seconds before doubling back to the landing and descending the narrow set of stairs to the side to pick up the Easterner's Ashes. Back on the walkway, drop down from the upper section of one of the buttresses onto the wide ledge below, then off of that ledge onto the one connecting to the diagonal roof that leads back to the "floor" of this area near the tower where, on the left side, you can find the Dragonslayer's Greatbow and 5 Dragonslayer Greatarrows. Once you've made your way back up through the tower, head over to the far side of the walkway and, around the corner, run up on another Silver Knight while he has his bow drawn to make him regret targeting you before briefly equipping the Black Bow of Pharis to draw the attention of the rightmost Silver Knight on the landing below, which will let you lure him up to fight solo without being pestered by the other Silver Knight who already has his bow out. After running down and taking out that same Silver Knight with the trick you've been using so far, you're going to descend the buttress here, collect another Large Titanite Shard on the opposite side of it, and go down a ladder at the end of the path to open a gate near the elevated cathedral entrance, creating yet another shortcut!

When you've returned to the landing, head into the archway next to the short buttress to reach...well, a chamber that will be strikingly familiar to players of the first game, complete with a statue of Gwyn that you'll want to attack just like you (may have) did then, dispelling it as an illusion and leading you to the once-infinite hallway where Gwyndolin was fought...sure hope he's doing okay now, yeah? This place isn't super important in this playthrough beyond nostalgia, but you can find the Brass Set of the Darkmoon Knightess on the left-hand side (the Helm and Gauntlets of which are suitable replacements for your current armor) and, in Gwyn's Tomb at the very end, going to the rightmost side of the coffin will let you retrieve the Reversal Ring (38/107) (swaps the gender of your Ashen One's animations...yeah, more important for the trophy and lore than actual gameplay). Return to the chamber and head outside, where a corpse with an Ember and a lever await you - and when you pull that lever, the eons-old staircase mechanism will function once more to descend its walkway to where you're standing. Run inside and up the stairs to push the lever contraption at the top, and you'll be able to reform (part of) the bridge leading to Anor Londo itself. You're home. After lighting and resting at the Bonfire (Anor Londo) here (you'll notice that you get 105 Souls from an enemy dying nearby every time you do so; funny, but not necessarily worth using as a grind spot at this point in the game), go back down the bridge stairs to the walkway you got on it from, which is now pointed at a nearby tower. You might think that you need to perform some kind of long jump to get over there - but as it turns out, you've got an honest-to-god invisible bridge on your hands here, which using a Prism Stone for the only time ever will demonstrate to you:

Cross this and, when you reach the tower, drop off the right side to light the next Bonfire (Prison Tower) and speak to Company Captain Yorshka, a heretofore unknown child of Gwyn that now leads the extinct Blades of the Darkmoon. However, since you learned the covenant gesture from Sirris, you can choose to perform it when talking to her, and she'll induct you as the first (and only) member. You'll be coming back to her later as one of the several covenants you need to rank up in, but for now, head into the tower and drop down through the wooden platforms to collect the Painting Guardian Set spread across two corpses (the first is on a set of beams, so be extra careful in aiming where you fall) before using a Homeward Bone and Traveling back to Anor Londo, which it's time to enter. Up the large flight of stairs here, you'll find two more Silver Knights that'll run down to engage you one at a time, though rolling behind them as they perform their opening lunge will let you cut them down with ease. At the top of the stairs, ignore the summon sign in front of the locked doors - it's another reverse sign that'll bring you into Anri's world, but it's for the next boss fight and you want to clear that yourself first - and instead, turn right through the doorway to find a red-eyed Silver Knight guarding the second Soul of a Crestfallen Knight. Back at the main doors, there's a Soul of a Weary Warrior on the balcony to the left before the other doorway, which will lead you to another familiar locale: the former home of the Giant Blacksmith, whose corpse still clutches the Giant's Coal for you to take. Poor bastard... As you take the stairs up here, you'll notice (and hear) sludge coating every other step; this crap won't attack you like the slimes (though those ARE here, and perhaps it's better to call them by their proper name - Rotten Flesh of Aldrich), but it's an ominous portent of things to come. Keep going along the stairs until you enter the main cathedral, far dimmer than it used to be, and turn left to descend toward several more Devout of the Deep, whom you'll want to roll through the fireballs of so you can cut them down and retrieve the Proof of a Concord Kept next to them.

Double back up the stairs and go past the entrance to the walkway bridging this set of stairs with the one on the other side of the cathedral, where you can pick up 6 Moonlight Arrows at the landing just before the ground floor. Now, when you reach the floor and dispatch not only the three remaining Devout of the Deep in front of the fog door, but also the many Rotten Flesh of Aldrich lining the ground and dropping down from the ceiling, be wary as you head toward the main doors...because as you may have seen on the walkway above, another Deep Accursed is clinging to the ceiling and waiting for you to pass under him so he can drop down and start assaulting you. However, just like in the Cathedral of the Deep, there's an exploit to make killing him much, much easier; he simply cannot ascend the stairs here, so you can keep him stuck at the bottom, like so: It won't be as easy to land your attacks on him this time, as he'll frequently leap around and get stuck on the side of the stairs instead, but if you patiently wait for the brief lull period after he completes a lunging attack to run down and press L1 , you can cut him down without much hassle and receive Aldrich's Ruby (39/107) (recover HP from critical attacks), completing the set. After opening a chest on the right-hand side (facing the main doors) behind the stairs for an Estus Shard, push the lever to the left of the doors to open them and return to the Bonfire to rest, as you've likely consumed many Estus Flasks in the cathedral. Equip Charcoal/Gold Pine Resins or Bundles if you want, then run back into the cathedral, past all the enemies, and toward the fog door to take on what's unquestionably the most vile character in the entire setting - Aldrich, Devourer of Gods.

When you pass through the fog, you'll see that Aldrich looks unnervingly familiar - that's right, he has that epithet for a damn good reason, as he's gone and consumed Gwyndolin himself! This has given him the latter's sorcerous powers, and in tandem with his own sludge body, you're in for one hell of a boss fight. For the duration of this fight, Aldrich is far and away at his most dangerous when he's at a distance from you so he can start unleashing long-range attacks; either dark projectiles or, much more dangerously, a rain of Moonlight Arrows (telegraphed by him pulling out a bow and aiming it at the ceiling) that persists for several seconds and expands in range as it continues. You can roll through the former attack just fine, but no matter where you are in the boss chamber, when you see the latter revving up: run the hell away, hiding behind any intact pillars remaining if you can, because it will kill you dead if you're caught in it for more than a couple seconds. With all that said, your best bet is to act like YOU'RE the boss in this battle and run up on Aldrich at every chance you get to start hacking and slashing at him - even if you don't use Resins or Bundles, you can easily take out large chunks of his HP with every combo. The caveat is that, after taking however many close-range attacks, Aldrich will disappear into the sludge coating the ground (heralded by him raising his staff and unleashing a large cloud of dark fog that'll hurt quite a bit if you don't roll away) and reappear elsewhere in the room, forcing you to run after him and renew your assault. Additionally, simply being close to him will not prevent Aldrich from unleashing that awful arrow rain, and in fact you need to run away IMMEDIATELY if you see that animation starting unless you're in the mood to cosplay a pincushion; aside from that, though, you won't have much to worry about in his first phase, especially if you wait to attack him until after he performs very slow melee attacks (if you can, aim for the "head" and not the tail of his body to do the most damage).

At 50% HP (yes, mercifully, there's no second HP bar this time), Aldrich will add pyromancy to his arsenal, mainly by augmenting his physical attacks with waves of flame that trail after the tip of his staff, and his rain of arrows will start homing toward you when fired, since they were just too Aldrich, Devourer of Gods easy to deal with before. However, it's entirely likely that you won't see any of the latter during this phase because Aldrich becomes so much more physically aggressive - keep running after him wherever he reappears, and the bastard will go down quickly enough. Ultimately, this battle can be very easy or maddeningly difficult, and it's dependent almost entirely on how much he wants to spam the arrow rain on a given run; the author had attempts that ended almost immediately and those where he took almost no damage solely through keeping the pressure on. Expect to retry this a couple of times if you're not lucky on the first go. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the saint decanonized, you'll receive the Soul of Aldrich (do not consume this!) and his Cinders of a Lord... ...as well as a new Bonfire (Aldrich, Devourer of Gods). Before going any further, how about you complete Anri's questline? Travel to the Anor Londo Bonfire (or run back through the cathedral) and go up to the open doors to use the summon sign avoided earlier, which will pull you into Anri's world to help them fight Aldrich in Horace's stead. This will be quite cathartic if you were struggling in the boss fight yourself, as Anri will be tanking all of Aldrich's attacks while he focuses entirely on them, leaving you free to bumrush him from the side and cut him to pieces without much resistance - the author was able to get through almost half of Aldrich's HP before he teleported for the first time. For beating him again, you'll receive 12,500 Souls and an Ember, as well as Anri's thanks, and will be returned to your world.

Once you're back at Aldrich, Devourer of Gods (the Bonfire), you'll have one more thing to do before your next hub session. This is, as you might have recognized, the same room that Ornstein and Smough were fought in back in the first game...and the screw elevators on either side of it (the end with the Bonfire) are still functioning, allowing you to ride them to the former residence of (the illusion of) the amazing che- Gwynevere once more. She may have long moved on, good for her, but she left her Sun Princess Ring (40/107) behind for you; swap your Estus Ring out for it right here and now, then return to the Bonfire and, from it, to Firelink Shrine.

Quite a lot to do here since you've killed another Lord of Cinder. First, head up to Ludleth, who will give you Anri's Straight Sword as thanks from its former owner, and Transpose the Soul of Aldrich into Lifehunt Scythe (13/35). Next, run over to Andre and give him the Giant's Coal for some tender dialogue (and, y'know, more Infusion options or whatever), then Reinforce your Estus Flask to 12. To the left, you can find Greirat returned and still alive, having been saved by Siegward, though his new offerings aren't of great importance. On the other hand, however, handing over the Easterner's Ashes to the Handmaid will let you purchase the Wood Grain Ring (41/107) (increases equipment durability) from her. Sell what you want, use your Soul Chunks, and raise your Ashen One to level 76 with the following specifications: Finally, place the Cinders of a Lord on the throne to the left of Ludleth to anoint Aldrich, then Travel to the Distant Manor Bonfire and head down the stairs toward the other half of this snowy locale - the Irithyll Dungeon.

On this first set of stairs, you'll see two Irithyllian Slaves just standing there...menacingly!...who will run away as soon as you get close. Ignore them for now and carefully look toward the left at the landing where the stairs turn to the right, where a Pontiff Knight is waiting to jump out at you when you pass. Kill him first, and by the time you finish, the Irithyllian Slaves will have brought back a Fire Witch, so dispatch them and run up close to the Fire Witch to take him out more-or-less safely, then return to the top of the stairs and drop off the side to pick up a Rusted Gold Coin, as well as down to the ground to retrieve a Large Titanite Shard behind two more Irithyllian Slaves. Now, head outside and, if Enkindled, you'll be invaded by Alva, Seeker of the Spurned, who apparently had a falling-out with his wife Zullie and is now taking it out on you - he's not the most dangerous mad spirit you've dealt with so far, but he can hit from any range with his Arbalest and wields the Murakumo, a curved greatsword that lets him perform a brutal three-slash combo with ridiculous reach, so as always, be prepared to roll at a moment's notice. Defeating him will earn you your own Murakumo, and since the path terminates in a steep drop into the abyss, turn left into the archway and down the stairs to find your next Bonfire (Irithyll Dungeon) and, well...the dungeon. Once you've lit and rested at the Bonfire, proceed into the hall beyond to find two walls lined with cells. On the left, you can retrieve a Rusted Coin (which will cause its former owner to scream very loudly and collapse, just for the hell of it) and lift a gate to reach a Large Titanite Shard. At the end of the hall, you might see someone walking past with a red-hot poker; this is a Jailer, and he's about to become your most hated enemy type because not only do hits from that poker prevent you from using your Estus Flasks, but when their lantern turns red, your maximum HP starts draining until they die or it turns back to blue! You'll want to sneak or run up to cut them down as fast as you can before either (temporary) effect occurs, though with your damage output that won't be too hard. Once the first one is down, turn right and collect a Fading Soul while dodging the Hollow that'll try to tackle you just a few steps further on.

At the intersection several meters ahead, two more Jailers will pass through, so be on your guard and don't let them catch you with those damn pokers. Ignore the item at the end of this hall for now and cross the bridge, where you'll find another Jailer on the right. When he's dead, enter the first cell in this hallway and go through the two holes in the wall, collecting the 2 Pale Pine Resins (applies magic to your weapon) along the way, and leave the poor Wretch on the wall alone to lift the gate in here and, after opening the door to the left to create a shortcut, turn right and lift the gate to the first cell you find to retrieve the Jailbreaker's Key. Now, head back across the bridge and turn left to not only collect the Large Titanite Shard at the end, but open the window grate and drop down onto a ledge containing the Bellowing Dragoncrest Ring (42/107). From there, drop onto the stone steps below and take out the Peasant Hollow waiting with a shotel, then go up the stairs, pick up the 2 Homeward Bones on the right, and go back into the dungeon through the open door on the left, where you'll find not only a Crystal Lizard that'll drop a Twinkling Titanite, but your first hostile Wretch that'll attack you with a catalyst from the cell on the right -goes down in a couple attacks, though. Further ahead, you'll see two Cage Spiders that somehow made their way from the Undead Settlement...aaaaaaaaand a room with THREE Jailers right behind them, just to make you, specifically, miserable. The saving grace here is that they can more-or-less be engaged one at a time; lure out the one closest to you by smacking him with a Firebomb, then run over and cut down the one next to the stairs as fast as you can before finally killing the leftmost one that was staring at the wall. After killing the Wretch in the adjoining room and collecting the Simple Gem behind it, go up the stairs and return to the hallway where you collected the Jailbreaker's Key. Cross the bridge again and this time, after turning left toward the window you opened, turn right into a side-hall with stairs at the end leading down to another Jailer and several more Cage Spiders. Only five of the latter are actually alive (the ones with proper lighting on their limbs) and the Jailer can be quickly cut down by dropping off the side of the stairs on top of him, so once they're all gone, head through the end of the hall and turn right to find another Large Titanite Shard (along with a disgusting Infested Corpse that'll lunge at you from the corner as you pick it up).

Doubling back along the hallway here, turn left at the first open cell and cut down four Hollows to collect the Old Sorcerer Set, then proceed to and open the cell at the end of the hallway to kill a Corpse Grub, which will reward you with Great Magic Shield (7/34). Return to the window you opened earlier and drop out onto the stairs again, but turn right this time and dispatch the two Peasant Hollows waiting for you, starting with the one on the right so he can't get many shots off. Through the archway behind them, kill the Mimic on the right for an Estus Shard and keep going to encounter seven more Peasant Hollows - since two of them wield crossbows, cut down the melee ones as quickly as you can so you can focus on those two unhindered, and when they're all gone, descend the ladder at the corner turn of the corridor leading down to a door you can pull open...to find yourself at eye level with another Giant Slave. Well, you made a shortcut here but don't want to draw this fella's ire just yet, so go back up the ladder and to the other end of the corridor, where you can pick up a Soul of a Weary Warrior and drop down the hole here to land on a different part of the ledge that the Giant Slave is using as a pillow, where heading along the uneven rocks to the left will bring you to a corpse bearing the almighty Pickaxe, as well as the entrance to yet another sewer filled with Hound Rats. Enter the sewer, exterminating the Hound Rats as you go, and collect another Soul of a Weary Warrior as you make your way to the end of the tunnel, where you'll find two chests and hear Basilisks croaking nearby - the one on the left is, in fact, a Mimic, and killing it will let you retrieve the Dark Clutch Ring (43/107) (increases dark damage, but decreases defense), while opening the other chest will give you the Old Cell Key...and, uh, cause five Basilisks to drop into the tunnel.

Move back toward the entrance as you carefully separate and take them out as best you can, then enter the hole in the wall to find a couple Giant Hound Rats to put down and a corpse with 4 Dung Pies. Open the gate here and turn left to quickly collect a Large Titanite Shard before running outside (away from the several Jailers behind you) to come across this strange scene: These fellows seem to have died while simply meditating in the direction of some mountaintop ruins: isn't that odd? You'll be coming back here for one of the most bewildering scene transitions in gaming history later, but for now, retrieve the Dragon Torso Stone from the dead half-dragon and head up the nearby stairs to a lift; as you first ride it up, turn around and walk off of it when you reach a ledge several feet above the ground to retrieve Lightning Blade (14/35) from a corpse hanging over the edge. After dropping down to the ground and pulling the lever to the left of the stairs to bring the lift back down, ride it up for real this time and proceed into the hallway for a Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier and another door to open that'll create a shortcut to the hall leading outside/past the three Jailer room. Once you've taken the lift back down and headed back through the passage, quickly run into the chamber and turn left again to enter a room with five Wretches and the Profaned Coal, which is the last one Andre needs for Infusions. When they're cleared out/collected, peek out of the entrance to this room, and you'll see SEVEN of those goddamned Jailers walking around a pillar in the center of the room. It's legitimately suicidal to try and rush them all at once, particularly because their HP-depleting stare can reduce your bar to 0, but there's a more-or-less safe (albeit slow) way to cut them down one at a time; whenever you see the procession loop around the pillar, wait until the Jailer at the end of the line has rounded the bend and is closest to you with the rest of his buddies facing away, like so:

When things are arranged right, get that Jailer's attention by either running into his line of sight or pelting him with a Firebomb, which will lure him away from the group, and kill him right away before repeating the cycle until everyone's down. Now, you're free to collect Alva's Set from behind a pot and 2 Embers from corpses around the pillar, then return to the room that formerly housed the Profaned Coal and open the gate on the other end of the wall with the entrance, which will bring you to a corridor where, on the left, you'll find a Mimic that'll give you 2 Titanite Scales upon death. Proceed along this corridor and open the gate at the end to enter a cell that houses not only the Xanthous Ashes, but the Dusk Crown Ring (44/107) (reduces FP consumption from spells at the cost of reduced HP)...sorry in advance about the scream that the corpse holding this will let out when you pick it up. With all that done (and the remaining locked gates inaccessible for now), head out the large archway at the end of the room and down the stairs outside to the Profaned Capital. ...well, you're not quite done with the dungeon yet. After picking up the Large Soul of a Weary Warrior on a corpse in the clearing here, begin crossing the bridge - and be confronted by a Fire Gargoyle that'll fly over from the rock wall to the right! These guys are quite sturdy and possess a range of attacks using their spears and hammers, all with fire tacked on, but luckily, they won't be doing much damage per strike and can be staggered, letting you cut them down decently easily if you stay on the offensive. Cross the bridge after he goes down and descend either the ladder or the rocky steps to the floor of the tower, then climb the other ladder (surrounded by a suspicious amount of fallen ladders) to find the body of the most lovable scoundrel from Dark Souls II, Laddersmith Gilligan, who apparently died doing what he loved; what a chad. His body holds an Undead Bone Shard and his gesture, "Stretch out" (26/33), so once you've got those, light the Bonfire (Profaned Capital) nearby and return to the Firelink Shrine for some more trophy progress.

Though you haven't defeated a boss recently and don't necessarily have a ton of Souls to your name right now, there are more than a few things to do right now - most of them with your boy Andre! First and foremost, hand over the Profaned Coal, and though reluctant to use something so laden with the Abyss, he'll honor your request to use it...and with that, you finally have all possible Infusions available to you! It's time to knock out the remaining 14 of these for the related trophy, as you should only need 1-2 weapons on-hand to spread them across (you can Infuse one element into a given weapon, then re-Infuse it with another without using a Shriving Stone). If you're using backup saves, make one before starting these to reload afterward so you can recoup the Souls spent, but otherwise, go to Infuse Weapon in Andre's menu and enhance a different weapon to each of the following types: 1. Heavy 2. Refined 3. Raw 4. Crystal 5. Simple 6. Fire 7. Chaos 8. Lightning 9. Blessed 10. Deep 11. Dark 12. Blood 13. Poison 14. Hollow Nice not to have to worry about that one anymore, huh? While you're with Andre, Reinforce your Estus Flask as well and double back to the Handmaid, whom you should give the Xanthous Ashes to before selling your excess inventory, particularly all those Gems that you don't need any more; the author got up to 103,000 Souls this way. Next-to-last, after grinding (if needed) to ~107,000 Souls - use Central Irithyll as your farming location for now - raise your Ashen One to level 79 with the following specifications: And finally, burn that Undead Bone Shard to go up to 13 Estus Flasks +8, then return to the Profaned Capital; it's time to delve into the abyss.

From the Bonfire, descend the ladder that you used earlier to the base of the tower and drop out through a broken section of the wall opposite the ladder, where you'll want to turn left past several statues of bearded men toward a wooden walkway; on the left here, there's a ladder leading up to a corpse in the tower with 2 Rusted Coins. After returning to the street and walking a few more feet, another Fire Gargoyle will fly up to accost you - and when he's down, head up the walkway into the adjoining building. Here, you'll see a Crystal Lizard down the first hall, but ignore it for now and turn left into a corridor that will lead you to a second Crystal Lizard to chase down and kill before another corridor on the right brings you back to the first Crystal Lizard, which you can now pursue without falling into the pit that originally separated you from it; these two will give you 2 Twinkling Titanite, all told. Proceed to the end of this hall and turn left for a Rusted Gold Coin, then head through the opposite doorway to reach a wooden platform overlooking...sigh...another poison swamp (in this case, though, it inflicts toxic, which is way worse!). Before dropping down into the much, walk to the right and pick up 3 Blooming Purple Moss Clumps (cures toxic, put this in your Quick Items right away), then land on the closest strait of land below and start dispatching the Sewer Centipedes lurking in the water. Once you've picked up the Purging Stone nearby, turn to face the cavern entrance underneath the platform, where you'll see an item in the distance: you're guaranteed to get afflicted with toxic by crossing the distance to it, so make sure your Blooming Purple Moss Clumps are ready to use and run over to retrieve the Cursebite Ring (45/107) (reduces curse buildup), as well as the Hollow Gem to the right of the entrance if you're willing to put up with the two Sewer Centipedes in here for that long. Now, head around the side of this building to find a Shriving Stone, then up the stairs here to reach a door that leads to...well, maybe the most disgusting enemies in the game. These Monstrosities of Sin are durable, lumbering ogresses with hands for heads that can inflict a lot of damage with their melee attacks and grab you to not only bite down and inflict gradual damage like Mimics, but drain your hard-earned Souls away too! It'll be rough dealing with three of them at once, but you can make it easier by attacking them as they start to grab you for an instant riposte, and the two that start out sleeping can get stuck in the doorway to greatly mitigate the risk they pose as you attack them.

Once the coast is clear, pick up 3 Purging Stones and return to where you were outside to go up a stone ramp at the "front" of the building and climb up the ladder there to a ledge encircling the middle of the structure. Walking along this, you'll come to a hole in the wall with the fourth and final (thankfully non-respawning, like her brethren) Monstrosity of Sin, and once she's been put down, you can get the Sorcerer's Set from the corpse leaning against the altar here. Behind the altar, cut down a Mimic for the Court Sorcerer's Staff and return to the ledge to take the stairs up to the roof, where a real asshole of a unique enemy awaits - the Court Sorcerer, who'll both attack you with sorceries at range and smash you into the ground with the same staff he's casting with by just using it as a greathammer. You can't really stagger him, so to minimize the damage you take, roll through the combos and spells he unleashes until you find a pause to exploit with a single attack before repeating until he falls, where you can collect Logan's Scroll (god, it's been a while since you got one of these for Orbeck, huh?). Nearby, you'll see the circular centerpiece of the roof with an archway to pass through: Dropping down into this will land you on the top of the altar you saw earlier, allowing you to collect Wrath of the Gods (15/35) and return to the roof. Collect the 18 Poison Arrows on the right-hand side of the roof if you want and finish ascending the stairs to find yourself back in Irithyll Dungeon, at hip level with the Giant Slave. Turning left, you'll find the Jailer's Key Ring at the end of the passage, allowing you to open all the gates that remained locked at the end of your previous excursion here - then, when you turn around and head back, you'll find that two Jailers have appeared, but you can quickly cut them down before they diminish too much of your HP or even attack you. Now, drop down to the ground outside through the broken portion of the wall and prepare to battle not only the Giant Slave (same tactics as before), but far, far too many Hound Rats that'll come pouring out of the walls to harangue you, though the Giant's attacks can and will kill some of them for you. When the Giant Slave falls (which should also coincide with the Hound Rats leaving you alone), collect the Titanite Chunk he drops, the 2 Large Titanite Shards on the ground, and Profaned Flame (10/27) on a nearby corpse.

See the barred window nearby? Looking through it, you'll see none other than Siegward, having been falsely imprisoned and currently ruminating on how best to escape; as you can guess, he'll need your help for this. First, head through the large arch and turn right to find a Mimic that holds 10 Dragonslayer Lightning Arrows, then climb the ladder to a pair of wooden awnings above the ledge that the Giant Slave was sleeping on. Jump over to the other one to pick up 9 Lightning Bolts and drop onto the Crystal Lizard to get its Titanite Chunk, as well as the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight nearby. From here, turn around and descend the ladder beneath the first awning to reach the top of the arch you passed through moments ago, which leads back to the sewer, and retrace your steps to the toxic swamp (ideally not using a Bonfire along the way to keep the enemies you've already killed dead). Taking the ladder and stairs up to the roof of the building here, look over the stairs from the edge of the roof, and you'll see this window missing its bars: Run and jump off the roof and head up the stairs beyond to reach the cell holding Siegward, which you can unlock with the Old Cell Key - and as thanks, Siegward will give you an impossibly valuable Titanite Slab! Plus, the corner holds the ever-useful Covetous Gold Serpent Ring (46/107) (raises the chance of enemies dropping items), so this was well worth the effort. Talk to Siegward one more time and return to the floor where the Giant Slave stood to enter the SMALL archway, where a lift will take you back up to the Irithyll Dungeon Bonfire. Ready to unlock all those cells you had to skip the first time around? Sure you are! 1. First, open the last cell on the right in the passage beyond the Bonfire for a Rusted Gold Coin. 2. Next, run down the adjoining corridor to the hall filled with Cage Spiders and turn left after you pass them to open a cell with the Prisoner Chief's Ashes. 3. Finally and most importantly, Travel to the Profaned Capital Bonfire, climb the other ladder from the base of the tower that connects to the rock bridge, and return to the chamber with the patrolling Jailers - rather than kill them all again, wait for this gap in their ranks... ...and rush inside up the stairs on the left to the corridor with a single Jailer to cut down. At the end of this (keep an eye out for the patrol), open the gate and head inside to meet your final mentor:

Karla. She may not believe she deserves it, but Offer to help her and then Save her nonetheless, and she'll teleport to Firelink Shrine to become a teacher of the dark arts, as well as the only one who can take the tomes you've been holding onto until now. In fact, how about you follow her there? Return to the Firelink Shrine yourself with a Homeward Bone and, after giving Logan's Scroll to Orbeck so he doesn't abandon us, find Karla under the stairs to the left of Andre and Ask to learn dark sorceries, then give her the Quelana Pyromancy Tome, Grave Warden Pyromancy Tome, and Deep Braille Divine Tome (she'll initially reject this one, but offering it again will coerce her to accept). Now, return to the Profaned Capital and take, at last, the ladder past the Bonfire down to the diagonal land bridge crossing the city. See the four Jailer Handmaids around the large fire in the distance? Well, so long as they're all chanting, that fire will be launching fireballs at you endlessly, so you better run like hell while you're in range! To start, descend the land bridge until you see the Fire Gargoyle approaching you, at which point you should double back to the base of the ladder to fight it on better footing/without dealing with the fireballs; then, cross the bridge (stopping to collect 8 Onislayer Greatarrows along the way) to reach a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior and enter the archway next to it to reach a hall filled with gold, silver...and charred corpses, the former residents of this land. On the left, you'll see another group of four Jailer Handmaids staring at the wall - descend the stairs and quietly walk over to quickly take them all out in succession (they're far more dangerous at a range than up-close, so you should be fine), then turn around to battle the next Fire Gargoyle patrolling further down the hall.

Past him, you'll reach an intersection with the fog door leading to the resident Lord of Cinder on your left; ignore that for now to turn right and kill the Jailer Handmaids around the fire, which will cease to launch fireballs at you once you've done so, before heading down the stairs toward the pillar on the right and the end of the broken road to retrieve 2 Rusted Coins. Additionally, with the fire disabled, it's safe to return to the bridge and drop down onto the broken arch (from the area pictured below)... ...to pick up the Onislayer Greatbow and descend the rubble to the road where you were. The last chamber of this hall holds eight Jailer Handmaids and, in hiding, a Fire Gargoyle - this can be a taxing battle due to just how many enemies you'll have to take on at once (getting too close to the Jailer Handmaids will cause the Fire Gargoyle to growl and alert them, so stealth isn't really an option), so expect to get pelted with several fireballs and need to use quite a few Estus Flasks as you navigate through the crowd, prioritizing the Jailer Handmaids in groups of 2-3. When the coast is clear, you'll see two chests at the end of the room; BOTH are Mimics, to be taken on one at a time, and they'll drop 2 Rusted Gold Coins and the Greatshield of Glory for you. Everything that can be done here has been, so it's time to pass through the fog and face the reclusive lord of this Profaned Capital: Yhorm the Giant. The kind of boss that the Giant Lord wishes he could be, Yhorm is technically the strongest and most durable opponent in the entire game; he has a massive amount of HP and equally absurd defense, and that's before you start contending with his insane reach and the soul-cleaving damage that each of his machete strikes inflicts. Oh, and at half HP, he lights himself on fire to hit you for additional damage with every attack, on top of leaving trails of flame in his path and unleashing shockwaves every time he stomps on the ground! If you were to do this legitimately, you'd assuredly get your ass kicked several times over... ...good thing you're not. First of all, because you've been helping out Siegward, he'll join you in this fight (in a cutscene that automatically plays right after you enter the arena) to fulfill his promise to Yhorm, an old friend, without increasing the latter's defense since he's not a proper summon; he'll be doing plenty of damage with the tactic you're going to use AND will draw Yhorm's attention for basically the entire battle, which makes your job exponentially easier. Secondly and more crucially, because of how powerful he is, Yhorm actually provided a means for others to put him down - run right over to the throne he was sitting on as the fight begins, and you'll find a corpse next to a note that reads "Only the storm can fell the greatwood".

The corpse bears the Storm Ruler, which you may recognize from Demon's Souls, and it plays a near-identical role here; quickly swap out your Sellsword Twinblades for it while Siegward keeps Yhorm busy and get relatively close to the latter, then hold L2 to begin charging wind around the blade, and when the surging wind increases in size, press R1 to unleash a massive slash that'll shave a full tenth of Yhorm's HP (almost 3,000 damage) right off! The key to winning this fight quickly and relatively painlessly is to spam the hell out of this attack (which Siegward will also perform with his own Storm Ruler), which rarely misses due to its incredible range and frequently staggers Yhorm - it takes a bit to charge up, but Siegward is more than capable of buying you the time that you need. Too bad you have to put this guy down at all... Strategy Video Yhorm the Giant Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the one good lord falling, you'll receive the Soul of Yhorm the Giant and his Cinders of a Lord... ...and, if Siegward survived, you can talk to him one last time and receive a final Siegbräu for your jolly cooperation (it's important to let him say all his dialogue without skipping any of it in order to not glitch out the next step of the storyline). Afterwards - and while ignoring the new Bonfire for now - in a surprising change of pace, you'll be teleported back to the High Wall of Lothric for the final Lord of Cinder in a cutscene. In front of you will be Emma, now on her last legs; speak to her, and she'll reveal herself to be the one who summoned you before imploring you to remind Prince Lothric of his duties as she dies, leaving you the Basin of Vows that will let you advance into Lothric Castle proper via the statue behind her. However, do not approach it yet; you've got quite a few things to do before going any further, so instead, use a Homeward Bone and return to the Firelink Shrine.

First, head to the Handmaid and give her the Prisoner Chief's Ashes, then sell off your excess inventory, which you should have quite a bit of by now. Next, go to Andre and, with the aid of those Titanite Chunks you've found, Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades to +7 (the last few levels will be worthwhile, but slow-coming). Now, since you don't need to Transpose the Soul of Yhorm the Giant for any trophies, consume it and your other Soul Chunks before raising your Ashen One to level 84 (use the Fire Gargoyles near the Profaned Capital Bonfire if you need to grind for Souls for that last level) with the following specifications: Before progressing the plot from here, you'll want to place those Cinders of a Lord atop the rightmost throne (fittingly the second-largest) and return to Yhorm's arena (via the eponymous Bonfire, which thankfully was automatically lit for you), where you'll see an item sparkling in the pool of water on the other side of the chamber - run over to it, and you can collect all of Siegward's equipment: his armor, his Pierce Shield, and his copy of the Storm Ruler (boy, will that make NG+ and NG++ easier...). Next, Travel to the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire (boy, ain't that a pretty eclipse lighting up the sky?) and head through the graveyard to return to the intersection outside the former boss chamber of the Curse-rotted Greatwood, where one more inverse summon sign awaits: Sirris needs your help killing Hodrick, her grandfather, and he's just as much of a pain in the ass as you remember him being, even 2-on-1. He hits proportionately harder than he used to and loves to riposte you if you attack him from the front, so let Sirris distract him while you cut his back to ribbons, and do your best to interrupt his Estus Flask usage. Once you win, return to the Firelink Shrine with a Homeward Bone and talk to Sirris next to the Fire Keeper, where she'll offer to become your knight - Accept her knightly vow, and you'll now have a summon to call upon for the last three bosses of the game!

From here, Travel to the Pit of Hollows Bonfire and retrieve Hodrick's armor, the Sunset Set, from in front of it; then, Travel to the Cemetery of Ash Bonfire outside the Firelink Shrine, head into the cemetery itself and turn left to take out that Ravenous Crystal Lizard what was giving you so much trouble at the start of the game, and double back past Iudex Gundyr's arena toward the hill, where on the right side (next to the Hollow that you kicked off the edge after that first boss fight) you'll find the Sunless Shield leaning against a gravestone. Now, return to the Firelink Shrine and Travel to the Vordt of the Boreal Valley Bonfire to run back up to Emma's chamber, where you'll want to swap out the Sun Princess Ring for the Flame Stoneplate Ring and outfit your Quick Items with Red Bug Pellets + Gold Pine Resins/Bundles. Why? Well, you're going to approach the beheading knight statue behind Emma's former seat - but before you can do anything with it, you'll be met by the fearsome and alluring Dancer of the Boreal Valley. Enchanting as she may be, the Dancer can prove to be one of the most challenging bosses you've faced thus far if you're not ready. The main threat here is her long reach, swift movement speed (with animation cycles that can make it look like she's always just about to attack again), and heavy usage of fire in her techniques - the Flame Stoneplate Ring and Red Bug Pellets will do a lot to keep you alive during this, as her first sword is constantly aflame and pretty much every other attack she performs involves burning you. More than any other boss, rolling is the key to survival and victory here; the Dancer is best attacked from behind and underneath, so she can't grab you mid-combo, but that doesn't preclude her from swinging around and slashing at you, so be ready to spam at a moment's notice. Moreover, as soon as you're ready to attack her for the first time, use a Gold Pine Resin and you'll find it lasting you for most of the fight while greatly speeding up how fast you cut through her HP.

Speaking of, at half HP, the Dancer will homage Sulyvahn and pull out a second sword brimming with dark, transitioning to a dual-wield style that's even harder to avoid. Though she'll still unleash Dancer of the Boreal Valley fire and dark with variants of her previous attacks (including one where she sinks a blade into the ground and drags it in an arc, leaving a trail of its element that then explodes) and generally become even more dangerous, her most brutal attack here is a long, rapid series of spinning slashes that'll take her halfway across the room. When you see this revving up, roll like hell away from her and don't stop until she does, as even with your defenses, this can easily combo you to death. Otherwise, your strategy remains the same; get behind her and cut her rear to pieces, backing up whenever she fixes her sights on you, and this'll be over quickly. Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Strategy Video With the former princess laid to rest, you'll receive the Soul of the Dancer (do not consume this!)... ...and a new Bonfire (Dancer of the Boreal Valley).
