Before going any further, use this to return to the Firelink Shrine and Transpose the Soul of the Dancer into Soothing Sunlight (16/35), then head back to the Bonfire and place the Basin of Vows at the statue, which will somehow cut its own throat and fill the basin with blood, dropping the ladder above it and allowing you to climb up. From here, rather than proceed into the rest of the castle, you're instead going to turn left...because it's time to explore the Consumed King's Garden.

Once you're outside, ignore the locked door on the right and head down the stairs to pick up a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior, as well as face a Cathedral Knight for the first time in a while - it'll be more awkward and dangerous fighting him on this narrow walkway, but you're substantially more powerful than you were the last time that you faced one, so he shouldn't pose much difficulty. Past him, a lift will take you down to the forest proper; make sure to run off the edge of the elevator as it reaches an encircling ledge below, as this will let you emerge onto a set of stairs overlooking the forest below and keep you from having to wade through the toxic sludge that permeates the floor of this area. Below, you'll see an already-transformed Pus of Man roaming around, but he isn't a threat to you yet. First, descend the stairs on the right to pick up an Estus Shard before taking the other stairs down to a broken series of steps that bear a Titanite Chunk. Now, you're going to drop down into the sludge and quickly run to the solid ground ahead; on the far side of it (relative to where you landed), turn right toward the corner of the building you emerged from to find a Ring of Sacrifice. The Puses of Man patrolling this patch of land are...well, to put it bluntly, very annoying to fight because they can attack in basically any direction, dish out boss-level damage when they do so, and even at this point in the game will require several slashes from you to put down - that said, they do have a hilarious weakness to fire, and while you haven't got the stats to use any pyromancies and those Charcoal Pine Bundles/Resins are too valuable to waste on normal enemies, those Firebombs you've been lugging around will work just as well. Lob one at a Pus of Man, and they'll flail in pain for several seconds, long enough for you to run over and cut through more than half their HP before backing up and repeating the process.

At the stairs here, take out the first Pus of Man that walks around the perimeter of the area and climb the steps to face another Cathedral Knight, and once he's down, descend the stairs on either side of the platform to dispatch the two remaining Puses of Man on the straits, leaving you free to collect the items in the area (there are still Rotten Slugs in the sludge and some Hollows that can transform into Puses of Man, but you can cut them down lickety-split). It's suggested to run down underneath the platform, quickly collecting the Claw, 2 Black Firebombs, and Shadow Set, and running back out between the Rotten Slugs before using a Blooming Purple Moss Clump to get rid of the toxic that you almost certainly built up from that. On the other side, a corpse near a tree guarded by a couple Rotten Slugs holds a Human Pine Resin, with the stairs on the left hiding another body with a Dark Gem underneath them; head up the stairs to collect a Titanite Chunk and drop off the right side onto the stairs, which lead to a platform with a summon sign for none other than Hawkwood. Since turning left will bring you to the boss, turn right instead and head along the path to the left of the bottom of the stairs to collect not only a third Titanite Chunk, but another 2 Human Pine Resins. The archway here will take you to a lift - unlike before, you do want to ride this one all the way (this time) to cross a bridge at the top and reach an outdoor section of the castle filled with Hollow Thralls and two Hollow Priests. Though the Thralls will go down in a single L1 slash apiece, you'll want to kill the Priests first so they can't empower the Thralls; afterward, open the door at the top to create a shortcut back to Lothric Castle and collect the Titanite Chunk and Titanite Scale from the corpses next to the door and at the bottom of the first set of stairs, respectively, prior to taking the lift back down...and THIS time, you're going to get off (or, rather, drop off) at the ledge roughly halfway down to reach a walkway leading to some stairs.

At the bottom of these, you'll find a corpse bearing the Dragonscale Ring (47/107) (reduces damages from backstabs) and another Hollow Priest to cut down, preventing him from buffing the two Cathedral Knights waiting below. These guys are wielding only greatswords and no shields, so they're best taken on by rolling through their slashes and performing one attack at a time until they go down, but you have a decently large open area to battle them in, so you should be okay - the one under the arch will drop a Magic Stoneplate Ring (48/107) (reduces magic damage taken). With all that said and done, head through the arch and the fog door beyond (equipping Gold Pine Bundles in a Quick Item slot beforehand) to confront the eponymous Oceiros, the Consumed King. Remember how much you loved fighting Vordt? No? Well, not to worry, Oceiros is even worse! His first phase isn't so bad, granted; he'll just wave his staff around cautiously, trying to protect his unseen child, and if you're close enough he'll unleash a pestilent mist that gradually damages you while you're in its range...but he still does quite a bit of damage with both, so don't let down your guard for even an instant. Staying close to him to keep your attacks going is the name of the game here, as he'll frequently backstep or leap into the air to slam down upon you, but otherwise you have some breathing room... ...and that vanishes the second he hits 70% HP (yep, can't even have a half-health threshold like the other bosses), where he'll realize that his child is gone and go completely mental by degrading to a far more feral and bestial mindset and pose. Now, Oceiros will lunge across the arena, perform several swipes in succession, fly through the air to breathe crystals across the ground, and even spin around when you're close enough to attack you with his limbs AND tail. Make no mistake, you're liable to die several times to this phase because his damage output and attack speed are just that ridiculous; the trick to staying alive at all is to stay as close as you can to his hind legs, which will prevent his forward lunges and claw swipes from hitting you (as well as give you some time to heal up as he rushes away from you) while also allowing you to "safely" keep getting attacks in. In fact, the several-second animation of Oceiros howling in grief as he transitions to this phase is a great opportunity for you to use a Gold Pine Bundle and hit him for as much damage as you can, as it's the last time he'll be that vulnerable during the fight. Just expect to die, die, and die again here before you succeed.

Strategy Video Oceiros, the Consumed King Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the mad ruler joining his child, you'll receive the Soul of Consumed Oceiros (do not consume this!)... ...and gain a new Bonfire (Oceiros, the Consumed King), which you'll want to use to pop back to the Firelink Shrine real quick. Don't worry, as you will be back.

First and foremost, head up to Ludleth and Transpose the Soul of Consumed Oceiros into White Dragon Breath (8/34) for 10,000 Souls; then, run over to Andre and use those Titanite Chunks to Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades to +8 (as well as the Estus Shard to Reinforce your Estus Flask and go up to 14). While you're here, if you talk to Greirat now that you've (briefly) entered Lothric Castle, he'll offer to loot it for you - do not let him, as he'll always die on that run and the items you'll get from handing over his ashes to the Handmaid aren't required for any trophies. Speaking of, sell off your excess inventory to her (except for the Catarina Set, since you'll make use of that in NG+). Then, after talking to the Fire Keeper for an ominous question, raise your Ashen One to level 88 with the following specifications: Now, return to the Oceiros, the Consumed King Bonfire and proceed through the stone doors beyond it, where you'll enter a hall filled with the corpses of Man-Serpents. As you walk between the gravestones, you'll come across a LIVING Man-Serpent that (like the rest of his ilk) you should take out quickly, as he can attack pretty damn fast with its knives. In the room past him, you'll come across the familiar sight of a corpse leaning against a stone altar, one who holds a new gesture, "Path of the Dragon" (27/33), that you'll use to access a special area later. After opening the chest to the left of the corpse and the chest at the top of the stairs for 2 Titanite Scales, you might think that you've done all there is to do here... and you'd be wrong. See that wall behind the second chest? Well, attack it, and you'll dispel the illusion sustaining it, allowing you to cross beyond into what looks like a cave - but is actually the Untended Graves.

This world must look hauntingly familiar, and it is; but you won't learn why until much later. The layout is identical to the Cemetery of Ash that you journeyed through at the start of the game, but with new enemies and item placements, so be wary. First, proceed to and light the Bonfire (Untended Graves) here, then keep walking into the crossroads, where you'll find a Shriving Stone. Here, you're going to turn left toward what looks like the exact grave you rose from when the bell tolled, surrounded by three Corvians and a Corvian Shaman - all four will go down in a couple of attacks, but you'll want to beeline toward the Shaman so he can't attack with poison and fire while you're dealing with the rest. In the coffin, you'll find an Ashen Estus Ring (49/107) (increases FP restored by Ashen Estus Flasks) on , isn't that nice! Now, return to the crossroads and retrieve the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight from the same body that once held your first Ashen Estus Flask, then keep going toward that same set of ruins you once explored before to encounter two Grave Wardens and five Starved Bone Hounds, the former of whom have been buffed sufficiently that they'll take about 5 attacks to put down and the latter of which...well, they may not have much HP, but they're still annoying. Thankfully, once they're down, you can collect 2 Titanite Chunks from the left and right paths past the arch here (both formerly guarded by those Starved Bone Hounds); if you're feeling masochistic, you can still go through the valley on the right to face not one, but TWO Ravenous Crystal Lizards, who each drop 2 Titanite Scales but otherwise aren't guarding anything. With that done, exit the ruins through the large gap in the rocks toward what used to be the hill overlooking the Firelink Shrine...only all you can see now is darkness unending. Cheery stuff.

Additionally, if you're Enkindled, you'll be invaded here by Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild, here to avenge the Crystal Sage as his protégé. Hilariously, she's far more dangerous than he was due to her spamming of sorceries, ability to parry your attacks, and fondness for chugging Estus Flasks when you give her enough space to do so, but if you keep the pressure on and pursue her up and down the hill, she won't have much space to blast you with - just watch out for her occasional rapier stab mixed in with the spells. Past her, the Bonfire that once stood is gone, and the slope ahead of you has quite a few more Hollows than before; however, you can skip most of them. Ignore the right turn on the slope in favor of running off the edge toward the coffin you looted all those hours ago, killing Hollows along the way, to pick up a Hidden Blessing from behind it, and drop from there to the ground just in front of the large arch, where you'll see a summon sign for none other than the Sword Master between a few more Hollows. You can ignore that, though, since he'll be as useless as he was against Vordt, in favor of passing through the arch to the arena that first tested your mettle...and the true form of the man that kept the gate to the Firelink Shrine: Champion Gundyr. This is what Iudex Gundyr, intended Lord of Cinder, was supposed to be in power and skill - and as this fight progresses, you're going to be damn glad that he was weakened to a shell of himself by the time you got there. Champion Gundyr will get up as you approach him, no sword-from-the-stone-pulling needed, and you'll have a brief opening to get some slashes in as he reaches for his halberd...but that's where the easy part ends, as he'll be attacking you relentlessly from this point on. Like Iudex, Gundyr mainly performs powerful slams and stabs with his halberd, but they do a SHOW SPOILER Champion Gundyr

LOT more damage now and come out much faster, in addition to flowing into each other quite rapidly. Additionally, your former strategy of staying behind him while you attack won't work anymore because he'll just plant his boot right in your face and send you flying across the arena, and if you're close in front of him, he'll perform the same grab as the original that throws you a couple states over. Was it mentioned that even if you dodge some of his telegraphed vertical slashes, the blade will kick up chunks of rock that hurt you if they make contact? Another drastic and deceptive change from the original fight is that at 50% HP, Gundyr doesn't undergo any sort of transformation: he just really decides to take this seriously, turns his eyes red, and starts coming at you like you ran over his mother. Not only does he hit even harder and faster now, but he'll bust out some new techniques too - upward swings of the handle of his halberd that launch you into the air, running lunges that end in a long thrust of his halberd, and even an earth-shattering stomp to launch you back. The one weakness remaining in both phases is that his combos are just about always two attacks long, with a brief cooldown period at the end of the second; this is where you want to rush in, get one attack in, and retreat. This strategy will take you through the whole fight, though obviously with a lot more rolling in the second half, but you can still expect to burn through way more Estus Flasks than in most other boss fights - you were told to put respect on Gundyr's name, yeah? Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the champion failing his task once more (or rather, for the first time), you'll receive the Soul of Champion Gundyr (do not consume this!)... ...and an identical, yet different Bonfire (Champion Gundyr) to light and rest at. Of course, you're not done here yet; if the rest of the Cemetery of Ash has been reduced to this and the rest of the world is covered in dark, what's become of the Firelink Shrine? It's time to find out, so open those doors at the end of the arena (after collecting the Black Knight Glaive, hallowed be its name, from the right side of the arch you passed through earlier) and start climbing the hill toward the structure. Along the way, though, you'll be stopped by, of all things, Black Knights: one standing on the main stairs with a greataxe and another walking down the left side with a greatsword. Dispatch them both and continue to the entrance, where turning right will bring you to another Black Knight guarding the Hornet Ring (50/107) (boosts damage of critical attacks) while turning left will bring you up the path where the Sword Master once stood, with an (ironically easier-to-deal-with) Black Knight awaits you instead.

After collecting the Chaos Blade from the corpse at the top, navigate your way up the steps leading over the entrance, where you can retrieve a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight before heading inside to find...well, nothing and almost no-one, least of all a fire burning in the hearth. However, there's plenty to find here nonetheless; for starters, the empty Bonfire holds a Coiled Sword Fragment, an invaluable item that functions as an endlessly-reusable Homeward Bone (yep, you can finally sell those off now), so put that in a Quick Item slot now and never look back. Behind it, you'll find the Shrine Handmaid inexplicably alive and...maybe not well, yet up for conversation, at least. Talking to her won't exactly elucidate what's going on here, but you'll want to go into her wares and purchase the Priestess Ring (51/107) (increases FTH). Past her, at Andre's usual spot, you'll find his Blacksmith Hammer...missing him already...and down the path to the left where Yoel of Londor used to be, you can pick up the Hollow's Ashes. With all that accounted for, use the Coiled Sword Fragment for the first time and return to the "real" Firelink Shrine; sure is nice to hear that music again, huh?

Lots to do this time around, mainly because you've gone and visited the most lore-important area of the game. To start with, head up to Ludleth, who'll (if you picked up the important item needed for the second playthrough, which we'll get into later) recognize that you've visited the Untended Graves and offer something of an explanation, moreso if you talk to him afterward - the main thing, though, is that you'll want to Transpose the Soul of Champion Gundyr into the Prisoner's Chain (52/107) (adds five levels each to VGR, END, and VIT at the cost of taking slightly more damage...this is more or less the best ring, or at least the most widely used one, in the entire game, so swap out the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring for it immediately). Next, at the "normal" Handmaid, give her the Hollow's Ashes and, for the first and only time, purchase Gundyr's Set for an across-the-board improvement of your armor stats (as well as a mean fit), selling off your excess inventory as usual. We're unfortunately a couple of Titanite Chunks away from being able to fully Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades, and none of the merchants have anything new for us...but you can still go to the Fire Keeper who's become so dear to us and, after consuming your Soul Chunks, raise your Ashen One to level 91 with the following specifications: Now, return to the Dancer of the Boreal Valley Bonfire and climb the ladder; it's time to siege the castle.

Up the ladder from the Bonfire, take the path ahead to find a Hollow Priest pacing in front of a Lothric Knight, the former of whom you'll want to take out first so he can't buff and heal the red-eyed warrior. Beyond them both, pick up the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight and head right up the stairs to find a regular Lothric Knight approaching you - lure him back into the room you were and do your best to cut him down quickly, as a second one will be joining him shortly and, even though you're much stronger now than you were the last time you were fighting these enemies regularly, they're still a handful to take on in multiples. The hallway beyond the stairs has a Hollow Priest playing dead on the right, so slash him to ribbons before he can do anything and proceed into the room beyond to find the next Bonfire (Lothric Castle). Ascending the stairs on the other side of the room, you'll find a chest on the right that contains the Prayer Set (notably great at mitigating curse, so you'll want to hang onto it), and the walkway on the left holds a Titanite Chunk while leading to a battlement outside with, surprise surprise, more Hollow soldiers waiting for you. Fight your way up the stairs, likely enjoying how easy it is to kill them now, and make a sharp left past the barricade down a short flight of stairs to retrieve another Titanite Chunk...then hightail it back to the Firelink Shrine (either from the Bonfire or with the Coiled Sword Fragment) and run over to Andre to finally, FINALLY Reinforce your Sellsword Twinblades to +10! With your weapons maxed out, you're as strong as you'll ever be damage-wise, so return to where you were and, instead of turning left, take the archway on the right inside the tower. You'll see the item waiting for you next to the ladder, but ignore it until you've killed the Winged Knight that's going to drop down onto you from the floor above; trust us, it's satisfying to kill this bastard in six presses of L1 after all that the last one you faced put you through. When it's safe to do so, collect the Twinkling Titanite and climb the ladder to the next floor, where the outline of an arch in the stone wall indicates the presence of another illusion you can dispel by attacking, bringing you to a corpse in front of painting of a Winged Knight that happens to be carrying the Winged Knight Set and another body to the left of that with the Sacred Bloom Shield. Back outside, rush up the stairs to take out the five Hollow scattered around the battlements, paying particular heed to the ones wielding an axe and halberd that take more punishment than the rest, and retrieve the Large Soul of a Weary Warrior and 2 Titanite Chunks from the nearby corpses.

Once you climb the next set of stairs here, you'll see a wyvern in the distance...and, surprisingly, another Bonfire (Dragon Barracks) on your left! Light and rest at it, collecting the Ember in the corner as well, and proceed through the arch next to it to find a set of stairs leading up to the battlement before the bridge that the wyvern is perched on. At the top, turn left to find and cut down a red-eyed Lothric Knight for the Greatlance he was guarding before taking an action most bold: run right across the bridge and, just as a second wyvern lands and begins breathing fire alongside his brother, drop off onto the ledge on the far side and head underneath the bridge to collect the penultimate Hollow Bone Shard. Now, on the right side, drop down onto and kill the un-transformed Pus of Man with his head in his hands, then repeat this with the Hollow that's walking toward you from the other end of the passage so you can get yourself the other 2 Titanite Chunks on the corpses lining the floor and the Twinkling Titanite on the body hidden at the end of the passage. Double back along the passage and up the stairs through the archway to collect the 3 Lightning Urns behind some boxes on the left, then step into the outdoor hall beyond and start running right to catch a Crystal Lizard for its 2 Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier. However, you're going to quickly be (gradually) ambushed by not one, not two, but FIVE rogues, who thankfully go down in one attack each (as you'd expect) but can still get quite a bit of damage in with their Throwing Knives if you don't take them on 1-2 at a time. At the top of the stairs past the lot of them, you'll find a Winged Knight to kill and a good view of the Pilgrim Butterflies, the final form of those Hollows grown into trees, taking flight over the castle...oddly entrancing, aren't they? Go down the stairs on the other side of this platform to dispatch the Hollow that was lobbing Undead Hunter Charms at you earlier, letting you collect the Sniper Crossbow and 11 Sniper Bolts from the body at his feet.

Double back down the set of stairs to where you fought the rogues, collect the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier from the body draped over the edge near the stairs, and drop down to return to (and rest at, if needed) the Bonfire. Now, return to the bridge and this time, drop down onto the closer of the two ledges, where turning right will let you pick up the Titanite Chunk from the body hanging over the ledge and heading left will take you to a suspiciously empty clearing. A crossbow-wielding Hollow will be your only opponent to start with, but as you get closer, one wielding a halberd, another tossing more Undead Hunter Charms, and a third swinging an axe will all rush down toward you, so make sure to engage them one at a time to avoid getting ganged up on (ESPECIALLY with your Estus Flasks likely nullified for the moment). Beyond them, you'll want to ignore the stairs on the right for the moment and proceed through a large arch to find two kneeling Lothric Knights - for an easier fight, lure one of them over to you with a projectile and take him out alone, then sneak up on the other one and combo him to death (it's better to save the one on the left for last, as he has a shield). Now, return to and ascend the stairs to find yourself staring at one of the wyverns, as well as a Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier against a pillar and a Raw Gem to the right, before descending the steps to the right of where you entered to discover a second Outrider Knight. You're much better equipped to take this one on than you were with the first encounter, even if there's no way to cheese him to death, but don't think for a second that he can't kill you if you're not constantly rolling through his combos and slashing at him from behind. Your reward for defeating him is not only an Irithyll Rapier, but FOUR chests containing 3 Twinkling Titanite, a Titanite Scale, and the Spirit Tree Crest Shield. Back up this flight of stairs, look up at the wyvern and prepare yourself to run past it (likely taking damage from its flames along the way) as you head toward the archway to the left of where it's perched (but NOT at the end of the road past the bridge, that comes later):

Inside, you'll find a large room filled with explosive barrels...and a couple of Hollows with some Firebombs to share! Dash up the stairs in here to kill them as quickly as possible; some normal Hollows will assault you along the way, but they're easily dispatched. Once the enemies on this side of the room are gone, collect the 3 Black Firebombs in the corner on the ground floor and climb the ladder (or take the long way around the stairs) to deal with the four Hollows waiting on the other side. Once you've picked up the Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier from a corpse hanging over the edge here, look to the end of the room, and you'll see the claws of the golden wyvern poking through the doorway, covered in the same dark miasma as the Puses of Man -getting close to attack it will result in the exact same draconic monster bursting out to fight back! Luckily, being bound to the wyvern's claw prevents this thing from moving anywhere, and it's astoundingly easy to defeat: just pelt it with a Firebomb, exploit its subsequent flailing by moving in and attacking, and you should be able to kill it by the time you drain your stamina bar. Conveniently, this thing dying will take the wyvern with it, netting you 2 Titanite Chunks and 2 Embers while also, somehow, rendering the white wyvern on the other side of the bridge inert. While facing the other wyvern through the archway, turn around and exit the building through the opposite doorway, where you'll want to turn right, pick up another Titanite Chunk, and proceed until you reach a walkway overlooking the bridge, where a body draped over the edge carries a Titanite Scale. Drop down here and loot the corpses along the path leading up to the gate for a total of 2 Embers, 6 Lightning Urns, and a Refined Gem. Now, if you're wondering how to get the gigantic gate open (or, rather, how to get on the other side of it), the path lies at the top of the stairs in the room filled with explosive barrels.

On the right side up here, you'll see a faint glow coming from behind an archway leading outside -run outside and quickly kill the Hollow bearing this lantern, as well as the two rogues behind him, to pick up the Titanite Scale nearby. With that done, return to the room and dispatch the four Hollows sitting/standing around the tables one at a time before attacking the Mimic at the far end for its 3 Titanite Scales, as well as the Pale Pine Resin to the left of it. Through the large archway here, you'll find a lever that, when pulled, will slowly open the gate; then, to the right, you can pick up a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior before dropping off the side to engage with the Hollow Priests patrolling the hall, THEN the red-eyed Lothric Knight and normal one on the lower floor (alternatively, you can double back down the stairs and draw out the red-eyed one by simply standing at the gate in his line of sight, but this runs the risk of him being buffed and healed by the Priests). After collecting the Ember from a corpse on the left side of the stairs, ascend them and follow the path to the left outside, where you'll see the fog door leading to the next boss. Ignore that steadfastly for now and explore the rest of this area, starting with the body on the left bearing a Sunlight Medal (only 29 more to go! Don't worry, it's even worse than it was in Dark Souls II) and a lift past it that'll take you back to the first proper room of the castle that you entered - gotta love that layered design philosophy. Ride the lift back up and keep going left around the corner of this building to find and climb a ladder to the roof, where a corpse in the back-left corner holds a Titanite Chunk and the adjoining narrow roof on the right connects to the upper level of a different wing of the castle. Here, you'll see two Hollows standing guard that'll whip out crossbows when you get close enough; don't run over to engage them, though, until the bigger Hollow wielding an axe lurches out of the building behind them and runs out to attack you, where you can lure him to the other side so you're not getting pelted with arrows as you cut him down.

Behind them, a ladder will take you down to a library where a body in the corner holds the Knight's Ring (53/107) (increases STR), with the hallway opposite it guarded by yet another red-eyed Lothric Knight, whom you can thankfully cut down pretty easily because 1) he's wielding only a greatsword with no shield, and 2) he'll take a few seconds to enchant that greatsword when you get close, giving you ample opportunity to start comboing him. Beyond him lies the familiar and somber Altar of Sunlight, which you'll be giving Sunlight Medals to later in the game, and praying at it with will grant you the game's best gesture, "Praise the Sun" (28/33)! Oh, and after opening the chest on the other side of the room for another 3 Titanite Scales, pushing open the door here will bring you back to the area with the stairs, giving you an easy route back here when combined with the lift. Back outside, turn left again toward the inert wyvern and drop down through the gap in the railing toward its tail, where you'll want to immediately roll backward into the nearby room to avoid the sludge spit out by the Pus of Man writing on the wyvern's foot. As before, smacking it with a Firebomb will let you quickly cut it down to size for another 2 Titanite Chunks and 2 Embers, as well as exposing the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight on a body draped over the edge once obscured by the wyvern. Moreover, inside the room that you were hiding in, the final Mimic awaits with the Sunlight Straight Sword...and a little something more. So, pretty much every non-boss enemy in Dark Souls III has what's called a "drop table" - a list of 2-6 different items that they have varying chances of dropping, ranging from semi-common to extremely rare. Despite having set items to drop and not respawning until you start NG+, Mimics are, in fact, no different, and you may have learned this already; they have a very small chance to drop a unique helm, the Symbol of Avarice, that fittingly increases both the number of Souls produced by slain enemies AND the chances of them dropping items at all. It's entirely possible to have gotten one or more of these by now just from slaying all the Mimics once, but if you somehow don't have it by the time that you take out this final Mimic, the game (or more accurately, patch 1.15 for it) has you covered, as simply exiting and reloading the game after killing that Mimic will eventually cause a single Symbol of Avarice to spawn in its location. Make sure to get this now - you're really going to need it later.

Up the stairs from the last Mimic, you'll find the Braille Divine Tome of Lothric, which Irina will be more than overjoyed to have. On the balcony past it, drop down to the path leading to the main gate and retrace your steps back up to the area before the fog door, then turn right into a more ceremonial room, where you should see a summon sign for Eygon of Carim on the right. After heading up the stairs, pick up 2 Rusted Coins from a corpse and a Titanite Scale from a chest just past it, then turn left and head out onto a ledge through an archway, where you'll find the Red Tearstone Ring (54/107) (boosts damage from all attacks when HP is low) - a gap in the railing here will, with the aid of the Silvercat Ring, let you drop down and collect Caitha's Chime from the ledge above the two Lothric Knights that you ambushed earlier, though you'll have to retrace your steps through the level to get back here again. Once you've gotten all that done, place Yellow Bug Pellets in a Quick Item slot and summon Eygon or Sirris (to the left of the stairs leading up to the fog door), then pass through the fog to battle the raiment of the third member of the famous dragon-hunting trio, now animated by those Pilgrim Butterflies you've been seeing in the air above the castle: the Dragonslayer Armour. Contrary to what you'd expect from a "dude in armor" boss, the Dragonslayer Armour is a decently complex fight (in terms of what'll be thrown at you), but at the same time, quite a bit easier than it looks. To start with, the Armour is pretty damn tough; it takes many hits to stagger once you manage to get around its wide shield, while its lightning-infused greataxe has great reach and, given your choice of armor, will do a sizable chunk of damage if it hits you (this is why you want to Dragonslayer Armour

consume a Yellow Bug Pellet as soon as the fight begins). It also likes switching to a two-handed grip on that greataxe for a much stronger overhead slam attack, and when you DO manage to stagger it, there's a chance it'll drive the tip into the ground and release a radial shockwave that'll launch you and the spirit quite a ways away - this is perhaps its most dangerous technique because its attacks will also destroy the railings on either side of the bridge that you're fighting it on, so to avoid suddenly falling to your death mid-fight a la the Old Iron King, just back up and maybe heal instead of pressing the advantage and risking yourself whenever it falls to its knees. Oh, and don't try to be clever by running over to the opposite end of the bridge to buy yourself time, because it'll just charge right after you and close the gap in seconds. Then there's the second phase, starting when he's at about 60% HP: more Pilgrim Butterflies will arrive on either side of the bridge and start firing dark projectiles at you, more to distract you than actually deal a lot of damage, but getting hitstunned by them can be fatal as the Dragonslayer Armour continues its attacks (thankfully with no stat increases). Oh, and you have no way of actually harming them, so you're just going to have to put up with them for the rest of the fight. The trick to getting through this phase, and for maintaining an effective assault for the whole boss fight, is to keep moving while Eygon/Sirris keep the Armour's attention, mercifully knowing how to heal themselves semi-frequently. Because you've brought a spirit, the Dragonslayer Armour won't take a lot of damage from each of your attacks, but its attention being divided more than makes up for that, as you can easily get through whole combos aimed at its back without getting hit by any of its attacks. Keep circling around it, staying away from railings it's already broken, and the two of you should be able to kill it without much issue, even with the Pilgrim Butterflies spamming their spells.

Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. When the armor rusts and falls alongside its controllers, you'll receive the Soul of Dragonslayer Armour, which can be safely consumed... ...and can now cross to the other side of the bridge if you aren't already there, where a new Bonfire (Dragonslayer Armour) awaits. Light it, and let's go back to the Firelink Shrine like usual.

First and foremost, give that Divine Braille Tome of Lothric to Irina, who will now have her full array of miracles available to purchase (later). Next, since you're more than far enough in the game, head up to Patches and Talk to him; he should mention Greirat, and this will add the Horsehoof Ring (55/107) (increases stamina loss that enemies suffer from your kicks) to his inventory for you to buy. Finally, sell off your excess inventory to the Handmaid and consume those Soul Chunks, then raise your Ashen One to level 96 with the following specifications: Once you've burned your Undead Bone Shard in the Bonfire to raise your Estus Flask to +9, return to the Dragonslayer Armour Bonfire and climb the steps past the archway, where you'll find a larger set of stairs leading into the main building. Before you go up those, take a right onto a spiral staircase that leads to a Titanite Chunk, then proceed through that imposing arch to enter the Grand Archives.

After lighting the Bonfire (Grand Archives) on the left, head over to the unfortunate corpse of your boy Black Hand Gotthard near the stairs and retrieve not only the Gotthard Twinswords, but the Grand Archive Key, which has only spawned because you've defeated the Abyss Watchers, Aldrich, and Yhorm - no sequence breaking allowed here! Through the doors, you'll find yourself in a maze of bookshelves and stairs...and quickly be confronted by the blue brother of the Crystal Sage! This guy is not hard for you to kill at this point, and you can easily shred through over half his HP in one combo before he teleports; the problem is that when he does, it'll be to a random point in this labyrinth of a room, so catching up to and killing him will be much harder than it was in the actual boss fight. When he DOES "leave", turn right up some stairs to kill two Thralls (one of whom will drop down after you engage the other) and proceed along the path to collect a Titanite Chunk. Next, drop off the edge of the path and run along it to another set of stairs leading to an intersection - turn right, and you'll find a Crystal Lizard that, when hunted down, will give you a Crafting Crystal and Twinkling Titanite. From here, take the first left you come across to find a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight (and another Thrall that'll drop down behind you) and the "main" stairs past it to another proper floor of the room. Once you've gotten the Titanite Chunk to the right of the top of the stairs and dispatched the Thrall that drops to harass you, looking in the opposite direction will bring you to a strange pool of wax surrounded by Grand Archives Scholars, who have all dipped their head in the wax for very serious purposes. You'll notice that one has a flame atop his head, like a candle; run over to and take him out first, as he's the only one who can attack you with spells while the others have merely ineffectual melee attacks and will go down in a single slash each.

When the coast is clear, ignore the pool of wax for now and turn around, then ascend the stairs against the shelves to the right for a Titanite Scale. Now, cross the room to the bookcase hallway on the left side to find a red-eyed Lothric Knight wielding a spear walking toward you - he's not easy to fight in this cramped environment, but taking advantage of his pause when enchanting his weapon to get some attacks in and rolling through his attacks whenever he two-hands it will let you get through mostly intact (or just lure him out to the wax room, up to you). Past the starting position of the Lothric Knight, you'll find a Titanite Chunk on the balcony to the right of the doorway and a Crystal Chime inside the room past the doorway. With that done, approach the pool of wax and, well...dunk your head in it with . Why? Well, proceeding into the unlit room to the right of the pool, you'll see an item against the far wall and TWO Crystal Lizards in the corner, but getting too close to any of the bookshelves here while pursuing them will spawn dozens of violet, ghostly hands that will attack you and build up curse; but only if you don't have a head covered in wax, which otherwise protects you. Dark Souls logic! Once you've killed the Crystal Lizards for their combined 3 Twinkling Titanite and Chaos Gem, pull this lever next to the staircase that one of them likely ran up: Turn left from here, collecting the Soul of a Nameless Soldier along the way, and you'll find that a bookcase against the wall has slid down, exposing a chamber with a chest holding the Witch's Locks and a body bearing Power Within (11/27). Once you have (if needed) refreshed the wax on your head with another dip, climb the stairs in here and turn left to cut down another Grand Archives Scholar standing next to a Titanite Scale past more cursed bookshelves, then a candle-headed one that'll come in through the archway on the right. Just outside here, you'll be within range for the Crystal Sage to begin attacking you again, so quickly run across from the archway to

kick down a ladder as a shortcut, to the right for a Titanite Chunk on a balcony, and finally across the hall to the left to kill a Crystal Lizard for its 2 Twinkling Titanite before you head through the arches at the end to an outdoor balcony, where you'll be safe from the Crystal Sage as long as you stick to the wall pillars. Once you've got the 3 Homeward Bones here, run up the stairs that are now on your left side within the building, kill the three Thralls that attack you, and dip your head in the wax pool here to safely pick up the Titanite Chunk nearby, then return to the floor underneath the Crystal Sage and walk between the two bookshelves in the center to pull another lever that'll lower some bookshelves on the ground floor. To finish off the Crystal Sage, climb the ladder on the right side of the outdoor balcony and bumrush him (if you exited and reloaded the game at any point between your first encounter with him and this one, he'll be back to full HP and will teleport to a bridge in the middle of the room to continue harassing you), then take out the Thralls on the stairs to the right and the Grand Archives Scholar further past them in front of a Titanite Scale (dropping off this balcony onto the bookshelf below will net you ANOTHER Titanite Scale, and rolling off that onto the shelves below with the Silvercat Ring temporarily equipped will let you pick up the Avelyn, a.k.a. the small version of what you dealt with at the Smouldering Lake). To reach the bridge, head up the stairs connected to the left side of the balcony that the Crystal Sage was on after you've refreshed your wax head to kill the candle-headed Grand Archives Scholar and two Thralls here, as well as pass through the cursed hands that'll erupt from the floor unscathed. Around the left corner, pick up a Titanite Scale before you drop through the broken railing past the bookshelf to the right to land on the bridge and finally (if you didn't already) finish off the Crystal Sage, who'll drop the Crystal Scroll for Orbeck! On the left railing of the other side of the bridge, a broken section will let you drop down to kill yet another hapless Crystal Lizard for yet another Titanite Scale...and returning to the floor with the first wax pool, you'll find a conspicuous gap in the bookshelves (near where you retrieved the Titanite Chunk and got ambushed by the Thrall) that leads to none other than a Titanite Slab in a chest.

Make your way back up to the balcony that you dropped off the bridge from and attack the arch-shaped wall on the left to dispel the illusion, revealing one last Outrider Knight in the room beyond. If you don't currently have a wax head, this'll be a tougher fight than normal if you get pressed up against any of the bookshelves because, surprise surprise, they have cursed hands to throw, but otherwise, this Outrider Knight should go down far easier than the first one did, awarding you with the Outrider Knight Set in the process. Through the archway here, you can retrieve Soul Stream (9/34) and the ominous lore it presents, then double back to the balcony you started from and descend the ladder opposite the stairs (after picking up the Titanite Scale behind the table to the left) for a Shriving Stone- this will bring you back to the bridge, on the right side of which is another lever to pull: With the nearby bookshelf retracted by this and a shortcut created to the second wax pool, collect the Scholar's Ring (56/107) (increases INT) from the corpse behind it and head through the passage opposite the bridge to cut down another red-eyed Lothric Knight, who can be taken down in a single combo if you carefully walk up to him without running. Now, cross the bridge and enter the lift on the right, which will return you to the ground floor, and pull the lever at the end of this chamber to lower the bookshelf blocking you off from the rest of the room. Another shortcut achieved! Go back up with the lift, take a dunk in the second wax pool again, and run back to the upper lift area to ascend the stairs on the other side of the chamber, which will bring you to four candle-headed Grand Archives Scholars standing near far too many cursed bookshelves. Clear them out as fast as you can and retrieve the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight from between them, then open the chest to the left of the archway on the other side for 3 Titanite Scales and rush up the stairs, where you'll find a Crystal Lizard (offering a Twinkling Titanite and Refined Gem) and, more importantly, the Fleshbite Ring (57/107) (raises poison, frost, bleed, and curse resistance by about 1/4 of their dedicated Bite Rings) past a whole host of cursed hands. If you're quick, the wax head should last you through all of this!

Through the arch to the left, you'll emerge outside once again and take a ladder on the left down to the rooftops. Moving onto the main roof from here, you can look over the right side to see a lower, narrower roof encircling the building, and dropping onto this will let you collect a Titanite Chunk, then return to where you were through the passage behind the red-eyed Lothric Knight that you took out earlier. Once you're back on the main roof, approach the far edge of it and prepare to battle a Fire Gargoyle that'll leap up, with another Titanite Chunk waiting for you once it's safe. Keep heading along the roofs and ignore the Corvians you see below once you round a corner overlooking a sort of street amid the rooftops in favor of approaching the end of the walkway, which will take you up to another Fire Gargoyle and a Soul of a Weary Warrior. At the top of this path, turning left will bring you to two Crystal Lizards; there is, in fact, a third Fire Gargoyle perched above who'll jump down to ambush you if you go after these little guys, but you can easily kill them for their combined 2 Twinkling Titanite, Sharp Gem, and Heavy Gem before turning your attention to him without being put in much danger. From here, drop off onto the balcony to the right of the path that you took up to this roof, collect 2 Titanite Chunks from the corpse there, and quietly approach the red-eyed Lothric Knight through the arches to combo him to death before he can enchant his greatsword. As you walk along the right-hand side underneath the support beams, keep an eye out for two Thralls that're waiting to drop onto you; either bait them out by running underneath them or knock them down with Throwing Knives, your choice. Proceeding along the walkway, you'll want to kick down the ladder on the right side of the curved section leading to one last candle-headed Grand Archives Scholar that's guarding the LAST Undead Bone Shard of the game!...and an Ember too, probably.

Double back past the ladder and head outside through the archway here, which will bring you to a pavilion where these three warriors wait on the stairs opposite a strange statue: These are the personal guard of Prince Lothric, and they'd like nothing more than to mess you up for getting this far. From left to right, they're Black Hand Kamui, Lion Knight Albert, and Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild (hello, invader!), and you'll want to know those names as you proceed through the strategy section here. The important thing to know is that you cannot lure them down one at a time - even if you approach from the left to try and just alert Kamui first, Albert and Kriemhild will quickly follow him down to jump you all at once. However, of the three, Albert is the only pure melee fighter, which means that he'll be the one to reach you first and start swinging while Kamui and Kriemhild stay back to pelt you with Throwing Knives and sorceries; take advantage of this by retreating up the stairs toward the archway you entered from and behind the railing, which will block most of these projectiles as you cut down Albert (he hits hard, but otherwise goes down in a few hits). Next, Kamui should come running up, so engage him solo and be ready to roll a whole lot since he not only attacks much faster, but will keep mixing in Throwing Knives with those slashes. Lastly, go down and dispatch Kriemhilde, who's actually weaker now than she was as an invader. For slaying all three, you can pick up their unique equipment from their corpses - the twinblades Onikiri and Udabachi, Golden Wing Crest Shield, and Sage's Crystal Staff - as well as one of the game's few Large Souls of a Crestfallen Knight on the stairs they were guarding. In the chamber at the top of the stairs, you'll find a lift that takes you aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaall the way back to the Bonfire at the bottom, giving you an easy skip past all that bullshit in the library, and another set of stairs taking you outside again to the final portion of the castle. Before going any further, turn left up the stairs that lead to the roof of this chamber for a regular Soul of a Crestfallen Knight, as well as a short segment on the opposite side of the roof from that item that connects to the main roof of the Grand Archives. Here, simply walking up the stairs to the central portion of the structure will cause three golden, angelic Winged Knights to descend from the tallest spire, ready to gang up on you...unless you immediately retreat back down the stairs, at which point they'll split up.

Even fought one at a time instead of all at once, these rat bastards suck to fight, moreso than several actual bosses - they have all the toughness and range of regular Winged Knights, as well as the tracking light-pillar attack, but with the added fun of being able to take to the air and crash down into you with brutal smash attacks. Your best bet is to lure them down the stairs, one by one, and only attack them once they've finished a combo or crashed into the roof; if you see them rise into the air and start glowing, run like hell (the pillars can indeed appear right next to them, so that's not a safe spot) and use the space between you two to heal up when needed. The axe-wielding one will be far more annoying than the two wielding halberds, as he can indefinitely throw and respawn his weapons, so save him for last if you can. Killing all three will net you another Titanite Slab, after which you can run to the other side of the roof onto a balcony opposite the top of the stairs on the central tower, where a corpse holds an Estus Shard for you. Speaking of, take those stairs up to a ladder that'll bring you to the room within the spire, where a body with the Hunter's Ring (58/107) (increases DEX by 5; swap out the Carthus Milkring for this to finally hit 40) awaits you. Now, return to the base of the tower (specifically, the set of stairs that you fought a couple of the Winged Knights near) and head inside to find a section of the floor missing; drop through this to, of all things, the rafters of the Grand Archives, where you'll see a massive cage whose floor is covered in feathers. Dropping through the open section of the bars, you'll find the corpse of Heavenly Mother Gertrude and her Divine Pillars of Light (17/35), as well as another open section of the cage that will let you fall to the next set of rafters. Here, you'll want to turn around and carefully run over to a Blessed Gem on the other end of the set of walkways, then approach the Man-Grub that's shooting at you, drop down near him, and kick his ass. Behind him, you'll find a ladder leading down to two chests, containing a Divine Blessing and 3 Twinkling Titanite, and can finally use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and take the lift back up to the top.

Time to proceed toward the highest point of the castle, filled to the brim with barricades and Hollows. On the bridge here, you'll find several Lothric Soldiers patrolling or hiding behind the wooden barricades for you, along with three archers; the suggestion is to just brute-force your way through, attacking the Soldiers on sight and rolling through the arrows sent your way until you reach the foot of the stairs that the archers are standing on, where you should see a red-eyed Lothric Knight approaching. Back up and wait for him to enchant his sword, after which he'll charge after you, and run back until you're out of the archers' range before engaging him, with your strategy otherwise remaining unchanged. When he's down, return to the stairs and wipe out the archers, THEN the three spear-and-shield Hollows, ideally one at a time. At the top of the stairs awaits your final pre-boss challenge: three red-eyed Lothric Knights, two with spears-and-shield combos and one with only a greatsword - the best way to approach this is to lure the greatsword wielder into running down past the other two so you can take him on alone, then split up the spear fellows (even if only by a few feet, though optimally keeping the attention of one while the other goes back up the stairs) so they can't gang up on you. When the coast is truly clear, climb the stairs all the way to the top, where you'll see an impressive blue metal door waiting for you to push it open: ignore that for a moment and turn right to find a tower housing a lift that'll take you allllllll the way down to the church area just before the Dragonslayer Armour arena (and adjacent to ANOTHER lift!), creating one hell of a shortcut for you. What's more, while the lift is settled at the bottom, trigger it and quickly walk off to discover that another lift will rise to fill the gap; take this one down, and you'll find a lone corpse bearing a Titanite Slab in front of the lever to summon the lift. That does it for exploring this area - put Red Bug Pellets in your Quick Items, open those doors, and ascend the stairs toward a foreboding

room, with a summon sign for Sirris to the left of the doorway (though you may not want to call upon her; the reason will be explained below), to finally face the twin regents: Prince Lothric & Prince Lorian. Contrary to what you might expect, it'll be Lorian who comes out to fight you first...and though heavily crippled by the sacrifice he made for Lothric, he can and will beat your ass, mainly due to Lothric happily teleporting him around the arena every few seconds. Lorian himself attacks with powerful slashes of his fire-imbued sword (hence the Red Bug Pellets), and what specific attack he uses largely depends on how far away from you he's been teleported or currently stands. If Lorian is: Right in front of you, he'll perform a relatively fast, horizontal two-slash combo (most common) or a single horizontal slash. Several feet away from you, he'll wind up and perform a lunging thrust with his sword or drag his sword through the ground for an upward slash or swing his sword over his head down onto you, all three of which knock you back. Not in sight, he's either about to drop down onto you or on the other side of the arena, charging up light around his sword before unleashing it in a wave of energy that's guaranteed to reach you. For all of these, the solution is to roll, roll, roll; don't even think about stopping until Lorian himself pauses, because his attacks hurt (the light wave, in particular, can easily take out half your total HP). You can get a couple attacks in per pause, but don't risk any more than that - and when he disappears from sight, roll first on the off-chance that he's about to drop on you, then look around to see where in the arena he is and start running/rolling to the side of his slash direction. This first phase isn't too hard once you get the hang of it, but you can expect to need to heal several times; don't do so when Lorian is charging his blade, but instead when you've rolled behind him during a combo and he's turning to face you, as he's much less likely to hit you during the animation. It's also worth noting that Lorian can still be harmed while teleporting (up until he fully disappears), so keep attacking him until he stops taking damage, every time, and it'll add up.

Eventually, Lorian will fall...but Lothric, determined to be as annoying as possible, will come down and revive him, then join him with a separate HP bar! So begins the second phase, substantially more dangerous than the first - not only does Lorian retain most of his moves aside from the light slash (and, of course, they all do even more damage now), but Lothric will supplement him with two types of ranged miracles: a series of tracking projectiles that'll fire in bursts of 3 about 5-6 times (he'll always unleash this at the start of the phase), and a single, powerful homing arrow that'll knock you flat. Of course, Lorian won't be idle during this, so there'll be several times that you'll be contending with both the rain of projectiles AND his swordplay simultaneously - the best course of action, as you'd guess, is to roll continuously until the projectiles stop, as otherwise you'll be stunlocked to oblivion. Now, how to actually win this fight now that the ante's been upped to such an extent? Well, there are two distinct changes in your favor; Lorian's total HP has been substantially decreased, so you can kill him much faster now, and Lothric's HP is, as mentioned before, completely separate from his brother's...and once it's fully depleted, the fight's over. Granted, whenever Lorian goes down, Lothric will spend several seconds reviving him, culminating in a powerful radial shockwave that'll send you flying if you're still within range at the time - but he can be attacked directly here AND while he's on Lorian's back with no way to heal himself, and every time Lorian comes back, he'll have less and less starting HP, so killing him repeatedly consequently gets easier and easier. It won't always be easy or optimal to get behind Lorian and attack Lothric, so you may have to wait until he's dropped on the ground each time, but patience will see you through this part of the fight.

Strategy Video Prince Lothric & Prince Lorian Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Above, it was mentioned that you might not want to summon Sirris for this fight, compared to the Dragonslayer Armour. There's a couple reasons for this, though one's quite a bit more important to most players than the other: 1. Because she only has a few Estus Flasks and isn't particularly tanky, Sirris is liable to perish in the first phase...and that'll leave you to face the second phase alone with the twin princes still having increased HP/defense. The boss is already hard enough without that kind of handicap tacked on! 2. If Sirris does survive this fight - well, that's the end of her as an NPC. Not only will you never see or be able to summon her again, but her Sunless Talisman will appear on a grave outside Firelink Shrine and the Handmaid will sell her armor, all but confirming her to have joined her grandfather in death. If you don't summon her, on the other hand...well, you can just pretend she's alive somewhere, right? With the reluctant royalty forced to fulfill their duty, you'll receive the Soul of the Twin Princes, which can be safely consumed, as well as their collective Cinders of a Lord... ...and a new Bonfire (Twin Princes). As usual, return to the Firelink Shrine with it - you're in the endgame now.

One thing to note right here and now: you will not be placing the last Cinders of a Lord on their throne just yet, as doing so sets you on the path to the final boss and you've got stuff to wrap up before then. First, run over to Andre and Reinforce your Estus Flask with the final Estus Shard to max out your healing items... ...then hand off the Crystal Scroll to Orbeck, completing his inventory of spells, before subsequently going to the Handmaid and selling off your excess inventory, which should put you around 500,000 Souls - wowzers! Let's put those to good use and raise your Ashen One to level 104 with the following specifications: Finally, sit at the Bonfire and burn that last Undead Bone Shard, putting you at a total of 15 Estus Flask+10! Now, before you brave the final level (and, if you're so inclined, the DLC), you've got one more optional and dangerous area to explore...and in true fashion for the series, the method for finding it is incredibly obtuse, so be glad you've got this guide for it! Since you've already gone through the Consumed King's Garden and found the Path of the Dragon gesture, Travel to the Profaned Capital Bonfire, run across the bridge and up the stairs to the left, and dash between all the Jailers (tanking their HP-reducing stares in the process, as they won't be able to kill you in time) until you reach the exit on the opposite of the room, leading outside to the series of praying corpses facing a set of strange ruins in the distant mountains. Using TP and , set Path of the Dragon in one of your gesture slots, then perform it to trigger an even stranger cutscene...and you'll awaken in the Archdragon Peak.

Welcome to the most mysterious area in the entire game. Starting on a cliffside path, you'll find there's no way back, so head forward, veering to the left to pick up a Soul of a Weary Warrior before engaging another Man Serpent, now in its natural habitat. Proceed to the large stone jutting in the direction of the ruins in the distance, with a Lightning Gem at the tip, and take out the next Man Serpent patrolling the path on the left that you'll take out to the next section of the cliff. Here, after picking up 2 Homeward Bones from behind a small pile of stones, you'll want to rush forward to engage the four Man Serpents on the path ahead, as they'll be hurling fireballs at you until you get within melee range; you can easily kill them two at a time, but hide behind the rock cluster on the right while engaging the first two so you don't get pelted mid-slash by the other pair. When the coast is clear, retrieve the Titanite Chunk from behind the rock cluster and head forward to find the first Bonfire (Archdragon Peak) of the area. After picking up the Ember from the nearby corpse, ascend the stairs to obtain a Soul of a Nameless Soldier from a body on the right and a Titanite Chunk from the one on the left - from here, go up the stairs to find not only a Man Serpent crouched over the side of the bridge, but a larger variant with much more health and a greataxe that'll breathe fire on you if you stay in front of him, though he's otherwise not too difficult to take out. His end of the bridge has a corpse holding an Ancient Dragon Greatshield (gradually restores HP, swap out the Shield of Want for this since you won't be hurting for Souls pretty soon), and the stairs leading down hide a body on the inner side of the steps with a Titanite Chunk. Heading toward the main gate, go past the lever on the left to find a Man Serpent guarding the Lightning Clutch Ring (59/107) (increases lightning damage, but decreases defense), swap out your Hunter's Ring for the Flame Stoneplate Ring, then pull the lever to raise the gate to find yourself in a sudden boss fight: the Ancient Wyvern.

Similar to High Lord Wolnir and Yhorm the Giant, the Ancient Wyvern has a metric ton of HP/defense befitting its size and takes forever to kill the normal way; just like those bosses, though, it has a gimmick that lets you take it out much easier, which is indicated by the red-orange messages you'll see scattered across this arena. Basically, you need to run through a gauntlet of Man Serpents across the ruins, roughly following the path of the messages as well, to reach a high-enough point to perform a plunging attack on the Ancient Wyvern. First, run underneath the Ancient Wyvern's legs, picking up a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior from the intersection if you can, and turn left toward a building with a few Man Serpents waiting to attack you - the Ancient Wyvern will start following you at this point, but the fire it breathes can actually be used to wipe out the enemies for you if you lure them into its path and get the hell out of dodge when the flames start up. Ancient Wyvern Run through the corridor adjoining this building to the next structure, where you can ignore the Man Serpent on the left (unless you want to watch him get roasted alive for a moment) in favor of climbing the stairs on the right to find four more Man Serpents blocking the way. You'll want to hide behind the pillar on the left here to stay shielded from the flames while you dispatch these guys before crossing the bridge toward the fog door, where one more Man Serpent blocks your path (if you haven't already lured him over to the pillar). Climb the ladder on the left side here, rush across the wooden walkway - likely getting caught in a blast of flame along the way - and fall onto a broken stone bridge with another message on it, where you'll see the Ancient Wyvern settle between the two halves of the structure and start breathing fire up and down. Wait until its head is settled close to the ground and it's stopped flaming for the moment, then run off the edge of the bridge toward its head and press R1 to hit it with that plunging attack, killing it in a single blow.

Ain't that a kick in the head? Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the last of the drakes ceasing to be, you'll receive the Dragon Head Stone (no Soul this time)... ...and a cutscene will transport you to the next Bonfire (Dragon-Kin Mausoleum). Light and rest at this prior to heading into the room filled with dragonkin corpses, and a bell will ring, summoning a Drakeblood Knight (hello there, Shulva!); these guys are pretty formidable in their own right, BUT they'll spawn endlessly until you dispatch the Man Serpent Medicant summoning them, so run up the stairs and make three left turns to find the bastard and cut him down, then engage the Drakeblood Knight on your heels, who'll hit for quite a lot of lightning damage if you let him. Killing him, however, will give you his Drakeblood Greatsword (deals lightning and magic damage, worth hanging onto). Now, see this altar between the stairs at the bottom of the room? Stand between the two dragonkin corpses and perform Path of the Dragon again, and you'll receive the Calamity Ring (60/107) (take twice as much damage...for masochists only) from Dark Souls I. Now, with the coast clear, go back up the stairs to pick up the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight from the body in the back-left corner, as well as the Dragonslayer Spear (oh hey, that's Ornstein's...wonder where he is?) from behind a gate in the middle of this back wall. Double back to where you found the Man Serpent Mendicant and head past his position to find not only a lift returning you to the cliffside path, but a balcony through a small archway with a Titanite Scale and a Man Serpent on either side waiting to ambush you. Return to the hallway that you approached the Man Serpent Mendicant in to find another archway leading out to a passage that overlooks the Ancient Wyvern's arena; a body on the left holds a Titanite Scale, and a set of stairs past it leads down to a Stone Lizard, a larger version of the Crystal Lizards that can actually fight back and inflict some brutal hits if you let it, though it can just as easily be combo'd to death.

Now, once you've gotten the Titanite Scale from the body draped over the railing here, go back up the stairs and drop off the edge of the hallway onto the wooden walkway below to return to the arena; turn right toward the bridge that you killed the Ancient Wyvern from, but instead of dropping to the stone once you reach the lower wooden platform, climb the ladder instead to the OTHER walkway and pick up 2 Twinkling Titanite from a corpse near the end, then go back and drop to the bridge, where ANOTHER wooden walkway on the left will let you drop to a couple more platforms and eventually the path that leads to the bell, which you should approach. Retrieve the Large Soul of a Weary Warrior here if you didn't already, and turn right down some stairs to find 2 Embers and 6 Dung Pies, then look to this section of the railing at the bottom: You're going to carefully walk onto the ledge past this broken railing and to the right, past the pillars and columns along the way, until you reach a corpse with the hallowed Ring of Steel Protection (61/107) (reduces physical damage taken - swap out the Sun Princess Ring for this). Back up the stairs, approach the building that you ran to during the boss fight, stopping to collect a Large Soul of a Nameless Soldier on the right, and take out the Man Serpents that come out to greet you before going up the stairs to the left of the entrance for 4 Lightning Urns. In the rotunda beyond with the Man Serpent, kill him and pick up the Titanite Chunk nearby, then look behind where the Man Serpent was standing to find a ladder leading down to 2 Twinkling Titanite. Up the stairs that you took earlier, you'll have to contend with the same squadron of Man Serpents that impeded your path...AND you'll have to take the next flight of stairs up to a broken rotunda, where a normal Man Serpent and a larger one wielding an axe on a chain await you as they guard 2 Titanite Chunks and 12 Lightning Bolts (near a gap in the cobblestones).

With that done, use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Dragon-Kin Mausoleum and go up to the gate (dispatching the Man Serpent Mendicant and summoned Drakeblood Knight along the way), then turn right down the stairs toward a passage leading further into the ruins. As you walk through here, watch out for a Man Serpent hiding in an alcove on the left and try to engage the two patrolling at the end one at a time, since they're both carrying shields to make your life harder. At the end of the passage, you'll find a chamber with two more Man Serpents hiding conspicuously behind the pillars on the left, both of whom are wielding twinblades and who can ACTUALLY overwhelm you if you take on both at once, so try luring them out into the passage to force them into 1-on-1 duels. Once they're down, look down to the right from the entrance to the room, and you'll see another Man Serpent to drop down on who would've jumped you otherwise - heading up the stairs from here will bring you to a large Man Serpent, once again wielding an axe on a chain, to dispatch. Now, climb the ladder on the side of the pillar that you passed on the way up the stairs to reach a corpse bearing the one and only Thunder Stoneplate Ring (62/107) (reduces lightning damage taken), finally completing the set, then descend the stairs to cross a wooden walkway to a stone archway, where you'll find a Crystal Lizard with 3 Twinkling Titanite waiting for you to kill it. Up the stairs that it likely ran to is a chest containing 3 Titanite Scales, and ignoring the other set of stairs in here, head outside to find two more Stone Lizards, the first of whom you HAVE to rush up to and combo to death before the other comes down so you don't get bowled off the cliff by them. When you ascend the stairs, another wyvern will land before you and start breathing fire; you can either run past this thing up the slope to four Stone Lizards OR stay and fight it, which will take quite a while and likely cost you several Estus Flasks, but will reward you with 36,000 Souls, 6 Titanite Chunks, 3 Titanite Scales, and 3 Twinkling Titanite. Don't forget to collect the Soul of a Weary Warrior from the corpse in the archway to the left!

Going up the path, either lure the Stone Lizards down one at a time if you've dealt with the wyvern or run past them all if he's still kicking. Inside the building at the top, you'll find another Man Serpent Mendicant who'll summon not a Drakeblood Knight, but the Unkindled Prince, a reference to none other than Prince Ricard of the first game. Quickly rush up the stairs to cut down the summoner before turning your attention to the Prince, who can be killed in four hits but has a very dangerous Weapon Art to avoid at all costs (telegraphed by him holding his rapier next to his head). Upon death, he'll drop Ricard's Rapier and leave you free to continue up the stairs; turn left here into an outdoor hallway, with a massive bell on the left that you do not want to touch right now. Instead, head into the building on the other side to light and rest at the next Bonfire (Great Belfry) before descending the stairs to further explore the ruins. Here, you'll find two Man Serpents to quickly dispatch and another Large Soul of a Crestfallen Knight on a circular platform between them, as well as another set of stairs opposite the one you just walked down that leads to a chest with 3 Twinkling Titanite and a Stone Lizard waiting to ambush you. Climb the ladder at the edge of this balcony, and you'll come across the Soldier of the Rock, an enemy wielding the equipment of none other than Havel the Rock who will MESS you up if you take him lightly. This fight is gonna require you to be as careful as you've ever been: every single hit from this man's club will crush you into the cobblestones and he's nigh-impossible to stagger while he's attacking, so you need to roll, roll, ROLL through his (thankfully short) combos until he pauses, at which point you lay into him until you either run out of stamina or he starts winding up for another attack. You also need to watch out for the Weapon Art of his greatshield -he'll pause, kneel behind it, and encase himself in even more solid rock and become borderline invincible, so keep circling and don't attack him until it wears off. When the impostor(?) goes down, you can pick up his Dragon Tooth and Havel's Greatshield, as well as another Titanite Slab from underneath the right wing of the wyvern corpse behind him. Now, see this hole in the wall to the left of the corpse?

Equip your Silvercat Ring and drop down through this, then head right to kill another Stone Lizard and collect Great Magic Barrier (18/35). Now, use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and use it to briefly Travel to the Old Wolf of Farron Bonfire, where you'll want to take the lift and then the stairs up to where you fought the Stray Demon so you can collect Havel's Set from a body on the right side of the gate at the end; you can then replace (some of) Gundyr's Set with this for its largely better stats, though you'll have to swap out the Ring of Steel Protection for, fittingly, Havel's Ring in order to keep your Weight Ratio below 70%. Return to the Great Belfry and go down the stairs in the pavilion outside to find an Ember next to a closed gate -there's nowhere else to go now but in the opposite direction, up the path guarded by Man Serpents. However, you need not go it alone; just past the bottom of the stairs from the Bonfire here, you'll find a summon sign for your long-missing friend, Hawkwood, and he'll valiantly help you cut a swathe through all the Man Serpents in your path. You really don't need strategy notes for this part - your pal kicks an impressive amount of ass and should ensure you have little-to-no trouble with the enemies, so just follow his lead until you reach the peak overlooking... . Hawkwood will disappear here after performing Path of the Dragon in front of the altar, and if you follow his lead, you'll receive the Twinkling Dragon Torso Stone; then, on your way back, turn right after the stairs that lead down to the path and you'll find one more Stone Lizard guarding the Dragon Chaser's Ashes. Well, all that's left now is that ominous bell; after returning to and resting at the Bonfire, stock Yellow Bug Pellets in your Quick Items, swap out the Hunter's Ring (or, if you haven't equipped any of Havel's Set, the Ring of Steel Protection) for the Thunder Stoneplate Ring, and studiously ignore the warnings of those messages near the lever as you pull it, creating a sea of clouds to walk on off the platform toward what's considered the hardest boss in the base game: the Nameless King.

SHOW SPOILER One of the mighty Lords and the strongest of Gwyn's children, the Nameless King is one of the most iconic and brutal boss battles in the entire trilogy - but to get to him, you first need to dispatch his stormdrake mount, the King of the Storm. This first phase is, in some ways, a bit more difficult than what's to come; not only are you contending with both Kings at once and thus needing to keep an eye on their individual strategies and attacks, but the King of the Storm takes drastically reduced damage everywhere but his head, which is only within sword's reach about half the time. Here's how it's going to go: the King of the Storm will fly into the large arena with the Nameless King on his back, which is where you'll want to consume your first Yellow Bug Pellet, and will alternate between circling in the air or stomping around on the ground for the rest of the battle, with different attacks and thus different strategies from you for each: While flying, the King of the Storm will occasionally breathe fire down at you, but the Nameless King will be doing most of the heavy lifting by either throwing lightning bolts at you or having the King of the Storm swoop down so he can swipe at you with his spear - you can't really get any damage in during this unless you want to pursue the suicidal tactic of shooting arrows at him, so just keep rolling until he lands. While grounded, the King of the Storm will stomp his feet to knock you back, briefly fly up to crash back down, and most notable crane his head down to start breathing a steady stream of fire across several feet, panning from left to right; meanwhile, the Nameless King will hit you with more spear attacks when you're close enough to the King of the Storm, either normal ones (telegraphed by him simply holding up the spear, angled down at the ground) or a strike infused with lightning that'll surge outward from the point of impact (heralded by him raising the tip of the spear up to the clouds). In all cases, roll through the spear attacks when you can, but otherwise staying between the legs of the King of the Storm until he flies up or leans his head down will largely keep you safe.

As for attacking? Slash the King of the Storm's head and neck literally whenever they're in reach, especially when he's breathing fire, to do the most damage possible (it's possible to stagger him, but don't count on it happening more than once or twice) - if you can't attack those parts of his body, don't attack at all and save your stamina for later.
