You'll probably burn through a few Estus Flasks here, but once you get used to the reach of their attacks, this won't be TOO difficult... ...that is, until you actually cut down the King of the Storm and royally piss off the Nameless King, who'll absorb the power of his fallen friend and come at you with even stronger attacks. THIS is where you're most likely to get your ass kicked, over and over and over and over, if you're not exceedingly cautious; the Nameless King now hits with lightning in every strike and moves far faster than before. Generally, he'll perform a simple two-slash combo with his spear, occasionally following it up with a powerful stab or overhead slam, but these are the safest of his attacks and still put you in a world of hurt, just to paint the picture here. More dangerously, he'll rise into the air and lunge into you with a brutal stab, dash around the arena (either slashing at the same time or just moving out of your range), charge his spear with lightning for a powerful thrust that covers quite a bit of ground, and stomp the ground while you're in front of him to create an Ashen One-launching shockwave. Then there are his ranged attacks! Oh, boy, his ranged attacks. When the two of you are far enough apart, no matter who created the distance, the Nameless King will start getting creative with his lightning: running a current through his spear to slam it down and send electricity arcing out in several directions from the point of impact, holding it in front of him while it charges up before raising it and summoning an ACTUAL bolt of lightning to strike your current location (this requires a borderline perfect roll to evade), and creating tall and wide fields of energy that'll hurtle toward you for lots of damage and stagger if you don't roll in the right direction (perpendicular to the field's orientation). Ironically, this means that the safest area in this battle is right next to the Nameless King, and that's also where your least-risky attack avenue lies - whenever the Nameless King performs his two-slash combo, roll over and get a couple of attacks of your own in, then back up and repeat.

King of the Storm / Nameless King It sounds simple, but the battle itself can get very, very hectic with what he's throwing around, and it's easy to lose your focus and slip up in desperation if he gets 3-4 hits in a row on you; if he does, your best opportunity for healing involves (paradoxically) running back so the Nameless King switches to his ranged attacks, which have more windup and thus give you a longer window to consume an Estus Flask or two in. Above all else, more than any other fight, be patient: it'll be tempting to just burn through your stamina attacking him as much as you can when you get an opening (and especially later in the battle, when he's so close to death), but unless he's staggered -it's very rare, but it can happen - you absolutely do not want to risk getting punished by him powering through your slashes and stabbing you with 1.21 gigavolts. Despite the feared reputation of this boss, the author managed to take him down on the first try and with a couple of Estus Flasks to spare - so following this, you can too. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the last of the lords joining the everlasting dragons, you'll receive the Soul of the Nameless King (do not consume this!)... ...and the clouds will part, letting you freely explore this last section of Archdragon Peak. First, light and rest at the new Bonfire (Nameless King), then proceed along the now-cleared path to find not only the last Titanite Slab only a few yards away, but the Dragonslayer Set on the left near the open gate at the end; Ornstein's armor has fittingly high lightning resistance, so you'll want to hang onto it for the next time you fight this guy. That does it for the penultimate area of the game -return to Firelink Shrine for some preparations.

First, head up to Ludleth for your final Transposition (of this run): Lightning Storm (18/35) for 5,000 Souls. Next, the Handmaid will take those Dragon Chaser's Ashes off your hands, giving you access to all the upper-level Titanite (aside from Slabs, of course), after which you can sell off your excess inventory before raising your Ashen One to level 110 (using the Lothric Knight near the Lothric Castle Bonfire to quickly grind some extra Souls if needed) with the following specifications: Note: the author messed up here and forgot to take a screenshot the first time - make sure to put 5 levels into Vigor at the top as well. Additionally - and know that this is completely optional - if you want to complete Hawkwood's storyline and get a unique item out of it, Travel to the Abyss Watchers Bonfire, and you'll have to fight none other than the man himself, who seeks to claim what makes you a dragon. He's a decently tough fight with his greatsword, but as long as you prevent him from drinking his Estus Flasks, you can cut him down in relatively short order and receive his Twinkling Dragon Head Stone. Now, before venturing into the final area (or either DLC), you have the one task every RPG player looks forward to: grinding!

So, of the eight Covenants you've discovered and "joined" up until now, all but the Way of Blue have ranks you can climb by offering certain items to their respective representatives (at least one of each of which you've picked up by now)...and the six distinct rewards pools include not only unique Rings, but spells that can't be found anywhere else. Yep, that's right - for the third and final entry of Dark Souls, you have to grind for not one, not two, but SIX different Covenant items! Granted, every single one can be acquired through online play (and the guide will list the methods for each if you want to/can go that route), but this guide assumes that you're playing offline for one reason or another, so you're also going to detail how to get what you need from the normal enemies in a longer way (which, as a tradeoff, will make the next step of this section a lot easier). If you're going the online route, you won't need to make any alterations to your equipment other than to, y'know, equip the relevant Covenant item in the Covenant slot to the right of your Armor and Ring slots for each grind: However, if you're doing this offline, you'll need to substantially raise your item discovery by swapping in certain equipment. Put on the Symbol of Avarice as your helm, swap out the Hunter's Ring for the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring, and re-equip the Shield of Want (to make the next step even easier): Note: if you want maximum item discovery for this next section and have The Ringed City DLC, you can find a Covetous Gold Serpent Ring+3 within by following the linked portion of the guide. However, bear in mind that said DLC is hard and will be made quite a bit easier by completing this grind first, which will award you with a ton of Souls to spend on stat boosts. Up to you which path to take!

Look at that perfectly matched fit (and know that the Symbol of Avarice constantly drains your HP while worn, so make sure you're sitting at a Bonfire whenever you're idle)...now, you're going to go over the individual grinds for each Covenant - you can tackle them in any order that you want, but know that doing this offline will take many hours even if you're as efficient as possible (and quite a bit of time online if you're not boosting). Also, for the offline players, this is the best and really only time to use those Rusted Coins and Rusted Gold Coins you've picked up, if for no other purpose than to reduce the grind by as much as possible. Finally, between offline grinds, you should pop back to the Firelink Shrine to sell off all the armor and excess items you'll be racking up, both to unclutter your inventory and to gain even more Souls. Let's begin! Online Players: with the Covenant item equipped, leave your summon sign next to the lever in front of the bell leading to the entrance to the Nameless King's arena with the White Sign Soapstone (purchasable from the Handmaid for 500 Souls) and, uh...wait - every time a player calls on you to help them defeat that boss and succeeds, you'll receive a Sunlight Medal for your jolly cooperation. The caveat is that the summoning player needs to be close to your level to see your summon sign, so that's the only real point at which you can consistently get players finding you; plus, everyone wants some help with that guy, so you're likely to get a ton of Sunlight Medals this way. Praise the Sun!...or you can invade and kill other players with the Red Eye Orb, which somehow gives you the same award. Definitely faster that way. Offline Players: Travel to Lothric Castle Bonfire and sit down at it, then turn to face the Lothric Knight in the doorway, like so:

For this grind, you're going to hit to exit the Bonfire menu, run over to the Lothric Knight as he begins walking out, and cut him down in 4-5 slashes (ideally as he's turning around and before he has time to raise his shield), then collect whatever he drops, turn around, and run back to the Bonfire to repeat the process. Lothric Knights have a small chance of dropping Sunlight Medals (and unlike in Dark Souls II, the chance doesn't go up by "exhausting" their drop table - you can get two almost back-to-back or up to 8 minutes of constant grinding apart, and there's no rhyme or reason to it), and you want 30 of those, so repeat the cycle of running up and comboing him to death (which will give you a tidy 4,500 Souls and at least one piece of equipment or Large Titanite Shard/Titanite Chunk each time). Warriors of Sunlight Note: since you have to play through the game two more times anyway, you're welcome to stop grinding at 28 Sunlight Medals, then pick up the one that spawns in the environment on each subsequent playthrough and collect the rewards below in NG++. Once you've gotten all 30, Travel to the Dragonslayer Armour Bonfire and cross the bridge to enter the doorway to the right of the lift on the other side, where you can pray at the Altar of Sunlight and offer up those Sunlight Medals for its two rewards: Sacred Oath (20/35) and the epic, recurring Great Lightning Spear (21/35)! Online Players: with the Covenant item equipped, wait to be summoned to defend Way of Blue members from invading Rosaria's Fingers players for Proofs of a Concord Kept or kill Aldrich Faithful members that invade the same kind of player for Proofs of a Concord Well Kept, which can be consumed for two of the normal item...if there's any Covenant item that you're going to boost, let it be this one, please.

Offline Players: Travel to the Anor Londo Bonfire and run up the stairs to engage the first Silver Knight that comes down toward you, then his buddy that'll follow him about 15 seconds later, for their rare chance to drop a Proof of a Concord Kept, then use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and start anew. This'll be quite a bit harder than the Sunlight Medal grind if you did that beforehand, as the Silver Knights simply hit much harder than the Lothric Knights AND you're liable to get attacked by the second while dealing with the first, but if you roll through their opening attack, they can easily be cut down in 4 attacks. Make sure to pop back to Firelink Shrine now and then to sell off the many, many Titanite Shards you'll be accruing. Unfortunately, this is probably going to be the longest grind of them all, as the Proofs of a Concord Kept seem to almost never drop no matter how high you raise your item discovery - some players have reported success (or rather, a shortened timesink) by also going after the red-eyed Silver Knight on the right balcony after the two normal ones because he seems to have a heightened chance of dropping them, though the author didn't find any proof for or against this. What did seem to work, however, was continuing to grind after the first Proof of a Concord Kept in a while was obtained, rather than exiting the game to back up the save data - without fail, 2-3 more would come in the next ~20 minutes, after which they would go back to coming sparsely unless one did exit and reload the game to "reset" the drop rate of the item. Using this method drastically speeds up your acquisition of the Proofs of a Concord Kept, so even if you're not backing up your save data, make sure to reload the game every so often while grinding for these.

Note: since you have to play through the game two more times anyway, you're welcome to stop grinding at 26 Proofs of a Concord Kept, then pick up the two that spawn in the environment on each subsequent playthrough and collect the rewards below in NG++. When you've finally got 30 Proofs of a Concord Kept, Travel to the Prison Tower Bonfire and kneel before Yorshka to offer all of them up to her, granting you not only the Darkmoon Ring (63/107) (grants two additional attunement slots), but Darkmoon Blade (22/35)! Online Players: with the Covenant item equipped, invade other players with the Red Eye Orb and defeat them for Pale Tongues. It's that simple! Blades of the Darkmoon Rosaria's Fingers Offline Players: Travel to the Farron Keep Perimeter Bonfire and run forward toward the road leading up to the Abyss Watchers arena, then turn left to take on two Darkwraiths for their Pale Tongues, after which you can use the Coiled Sword Fragment. Even this late in the game, these guys can kick your ass if you're not careful, mainly because they'll be attacking two-on-one; the caveat, however, is that you can cut them down in 3 slashes each. You can also separate them by walking slightly to the right of their line of sight, which will cause the back one (for some reason) to engage you first...and once you do get the hang of fighting them, you'll find that they give up those Pale Tongues way easier than other enemies do their Covenant offerings, enough so that you'll have what you need within 20 runs or so (even discounting that you only need 10, not 30). Note: since you have to play through the game two more times anyway, you're welcome to stop grinding at 4 Pale Tongues, then pick up the three that spawn in the environment on each subsequent playthrough and collect the rewards below in NG++.

Once you have 10 Pale Tongues, Travel to the Rosaria's Bed Chamber Bonfire and offer them to Rosaria for the Obscuring Ring (64/107) (leaves you invisible to other players when you're far away from them and prevents enemies from noticing you until you're close)! Online Players: with the Covenant item equipped, invade and defeat other players with the Red Eye Orb, be summoned by someone with the Red Sign Soapstone and kill them (fastest method), deal the killing blow to a mad spirit as a phantom in someone else's world, or defeat an invading Mound-Maker in order to gain Vertebra Shackles. Offline Players: Travel to the Catacombs of Carthus Bonfire and run forward into the hallway, then turn right once the Skeleton Boulder passes to enter the passage beyond and take out the two Skeleton Swordsmen, who'll go down in two attacks each; then, use the Coiled Sword Fragment and repeat to gain Vertebra Shackles. These are, per the drop tables for the game, rarer than the Proofs of a Concord Kept, but the author found them coming much, MUCH more easily (enough that he occasionally got two back-to-back), and the Skeleton Swordsmen are much easier to deal with than the Silver Knights, though you'll want to be wary of when they attack simultaneously since they'll still be able to rapidly max out your bleed gauge and cut down your HP to a dangerous fraction. The running L1 should provide an edge against their shields, too -thanks again to YostYosteen94 for that strategy! Once you have 31 Vertebra Shackles, you'll be doing two things: 1. First, return to the Firelink Shrine from the Iudex Gundyr Bonfire and make your way to Pickle-pee Pump-a-rum's nest on the roof through the tower on the upper right, where trading in a Vertebra Shackle will give you not only Lucatiel's Mask (completing the set at long last, as you well ought to do), but another gesture, "Call over" (29/33). 2. Travel to the Pit of Hollows Bonfire and offer the remaining 30 Vertebra Shackles at the, well, mound of them on the far end of the water to receive both Bloodlust and Warmth (12/27)!

Online Players: with the Covenant item equipped, you'll be summoned to invade and defeat trespassers (players not in the same covenant) who enter the swamps of Farron Keep for Wolf's Blood Swordgrasses. There's no alternative method that's more direct, so this can be the longest of the online grinds. Mound-Makers Watchdogs of Farron Offline Players: Travel to the Keep Ruins Bonfire and run outside to the bridge, then cut down the three Ghrus standing there for their Wolf's Blood Swordgrasses, then run back to and rest at the Bonfire to repeat. Of all the enemies you've farmed for their items, these are the one of the only two who still have a chance of dropping nothing, but having so many to farm (and being able to cut them down together) should offset this and they go down easily - in fact, you should be getting at least one Wolf's Blood Swordgrass from them once every 8 minutes or so, frequently enough that you can acquire all that you need in under 3 hours, at about the same rate as you got the Pale Tongues from the Darkwraiths. Once you have 30 Wolf's Blood Swordgrasses, Travel to the Old Wolf of Farron Bonfire and offer them to, well, the Old Wolf himself for the Old Wolf Curved Sword, Wolf Knight's Greatshield, and Wolf Ring (65/107) (increases poise)! Online Players: with the Covenant item equipped, you'll be summoned to invade and defeat trespassers (players not in the same covenant) who enter Anor Londo for Human Dregs; unfortunately, directly invading and defeating players will just give you a Pale Tongue instead, so you're forced to use the roundabout method. Offline Players: Travel to the Aldrich, Devourer of Gods Bonfire and run outside the boss arena to cut down the three Devout of the Deep on the stairs for their Human Dregs, then use the Coiled Sword Fragment to repeat - you're going to be very glad that you only need 10 of these because, like the Ghrus, these guys are more likely than not to drop nothing upon death. In fact, your biggest hurdle here is going to be patience; of the six enemy types you've farmed for these Covenent offerings, only the Devout of the Deep vanish upon death...which means that their several-second-long death animation has to completely finish playing out BEFORE any items they've dropped appear, so you'll have to stand there until all the mist dissipates in order to avoid missing drops. Additionally, you aren't lucky enough for the Human Dregs to at least show up frequently - they're not as rare as Proofs of a Concord Kept, but the meme among the game's community is that you're basically farming Deacon Skirts and getting some Human Dregs as a bonus.

Once you have 10 Human Dregs, Travel to the Water Reserve Bonfire and give them to Archdeacon McDonnell's corpse for the last of the trophy-related Covenant offerings, Great Deep Soul (10/34)! Now, if you've been playing offline for some or all of these grinds, this has been a long, arduous journey that's likely taken you about a week to reach the light at the end of...but your (byproduct) reward for doing so is a metric ton of Souls! Aldrich Faithful Spell Shopping If you've done all the grinding online and thus saved yourself a lot of time and agony -congratulations!...but you're going to need to grind out a hefty 272,500 Souls for this next part, which is most speedily accomplished by killing the Lothric Knight closest to the Lothric Castle Bonfire over and over while wearing your Shield of Want, Symbol of Avarice, and Covetous Silver Serpent Ring to maximize the number of Souls drawn from each kill. Once you've got enough money, return to the Firelink Shrine and prepare for a shopping spree. First up is your sullen pal Orbeck, whom you've been neglecting all this time; let's do him a solid and buy up most of his sorceries: Great Soul Arrow (11/34) Great Heavy Soul Arrow (12/34) Farron Dart (13/34) Great Farron Dart (14/34) Farron Hail (15/34) Homing Soulmass (16/34) Homing Crystal Soulmass (17/34) Soul Spear (18/34) Crystal Soul Spear (19/34) Soul Greatsword (20/34) Farron Flashsword (21/34) Magic Weapon (22/34) Crystal Magic Weapon (23/34) Magic Shield (24/34) Spook (25/34) Aural Decoy (26/34) Pestilent Mist (27/34) Cast Light (28/34) Repair (29/34) Hidden Weapon (30/34) Hidden Body (31/34) Twisted Wall of Light (32/34) For buying all that, Orbeck will (when Talking to him twice afterward) give you the Young Dragon Ring (66/107) (boosts the power of sorceries), Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring (67/107) (masks the sounds you make), and his gesture, "Silent Ally" (30/33), as well as his backstory if you Talk to him a third time. What a nice guy!

Up next is Cornyx, your favorite dweller of the swamp, from whom you're going to learn so many of the remaining pyromancies: Fire Orb (13/27) Bursting Fireball (14/27) Great Chaos Fire Orb (15/27) Chaos Storm (16/27) Poison Mist (17/27) Acid Surge (18/27) Profuse Sweat (19/27) Carthus Beacon (20/27) Carthus Flame Arc (21/27) Thirdly, it's time to give Souls to your dear Irina, purveyor of all the non-corrupted miracles: Med Heal (23/35) Bountiful Light (24/35) Tears of Denial (25/35) Force (26/35) Blessed Weapon (27/35) Magic Barrier (28/35) Notably, now that you've purchased her entire stock and ensured that she didn't sell you any dark miracles, when you leave and come back, she'll no longer be sitting in her cove - instead, she'll have migrated to the tower with the dead Fire Keepers (behind where the Sword Master once stood)...to become a Fire Keeper herself! Hooray for a somewhat happy ending. Lastly, head down to Karla, the nicest child of the Abyss, and you'll collect all those corrupted spells: Affinity (33/34) Dark Edge (34/34) Fire Whip (22/27) Firestorm (23/27) Rapport (24/27) Black Flame (25/27) Black Fire Orb (26/27) Deep Protection (29/35) Gnaw (30/35) Nice to finally have one of the spell trophies knocked out, huh? The other two will come easily enough, but that's a task for NG+ and NG++ - for now, let's focus on your last pre-endgame (and pre-DLC) upgrade. If you did all that grinding offline, even accounting for variance and RNG, you should still have upward of 10,000,000 Souls left to spend; and the most logical place is into your levels, which will not only carry you through the final boss and the next two playthroughs (as well as the DLC), but should (some players have reported otherwise, so you might not be able to) also let you swap out the stat-boosting rings you've been relying on for ones with more unique effects by raising your VIT to 40. If you did the grinds online instead, no hard feelings - you can just use this as a template to build toward with the Souls you accrue throughout the rest of this guide instead. Here's what the author went up to at a whopping level 186:

That's right, you're going to branch out into spells! Because the boss fights will be even tougher in NG+ and NG++, the guide is going to advise the use of certain sorceries and miracles, most of which will become accessible between those increases to INT/FTH and the use of certain special rings, for players who're sufficiently-leveled to use them. Speaking of, now that you've reached the soft caps for VGR, END, VIT, and DEX, you don't need the Prisoner's Chain or Hunter's Ring anymore, so swap them out for the Estus Ring and Sun Princess Ring, respectively - you're going to need that increased HP recovery, especially if you're tackling the DLC. Put the Grass Crest Shield on your back, too...and if you were an online grinder, now you know what to look forward to! With aaaaaaaaaaaaaall that done, it's finally time to brave the final area...but if you're so inclined, there are two amazing DLCs to explore first.

Travel to the Cleansing Chapel Bonfire and, at last, speak to Slave Knight Gael, still kneeling next to the altar, so he'll ask you to help his lady; choose to Accept, and you'll be transported into another world within a (scrap of) painting, Ariandel! In the cave that you reappear in, behind you crouches a non-hostile Corvian that'll encourage you to find "a sweetly rotting bed to lie upon" every time you talk to him, and to the right of him lies a corpse with 2 Rime-blue Moss Clumps, after which you can exit the cave to properly enter the Painted World of Ariandel outside. Here, light the Bonfire (Snowfield) and inspect the messages, which will warn you that the area ahead will be brutal; since you're quite overleveled by now, though, you're more than prepared for this gauntlet. Moving through the blizzard along the path, you'll find a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler on the right of the fork in the road as you encounter your first Farron Follower, the final regiment of Farron's Legion who will go down in two attacks each, but can be dangerous if you let them swarm you, particularly the fire-breathing ones. Turning left from the corpse, you'll come across another Farron Follower, this one breathing fire from his torch, and a Giant Fly behind him that can - and should - be cut down equally fast before he vomits on you, allowing you to collect the Poison Gem from the body he was feasting upon. Double back toward the large hill next to the path to kill several more Farron Followers, who'll thankfully engage you more or less one at a time, and take note of the human-shaped trees before heading toward an item in the distance on a snowy embankment...but when you reach it, the embankment will collapse! Now you're stranded from the Bonfire (unless you use the Coiled Sword Fragment, of course), but at least you can collect the Rime-blue Moss Clump from the corpse that comes with you. Proceeding into the forest ahead, you'll see that several Farron Followers are already lying around dead; that would be the work of the Wolves waiting for you behind the trees, with one pack of three close on the left side and able to summon the other seven in the area by howling for them. Engaging them can be tricky because, like real-life wolves, they like to keep their distance by circling around you and attack 1-2 at a time, so more often than not you'll have to run up to them yourself and start slashing, though they thankfully go down in a single hit each.

Once the area is wolf-free, pick up the Rusted Coin from the tree that the first pack was hiding behind and turn right toward a path along the edge of the cliff here, with another Wolf waiting for you. Additionally, you'll see more of the human-shaped trees here...and THESE ones have their "hair" blowing in the wind, which means that they are, in fact, alive and hostile. These Birch Women can attack you with ice breath or motes of flame (depending on whether or not the tips of their branches are alight) or just grab you to slowly inflict frostbite, and you can't lock onto them before they do, but rushing in and slashing them three times will solve the problem pretty quickly. At the top of the path, collecting another Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler will alert four Farron Followers in what'll be the first challenging encounter of the DLC for you, as they'll rack up damage on you QUICK - prioritize the fire-breathing one first and foremost after dispatching the shield-bearing one that runs down to you, and you'll be okay to retrieve the Follower Javelin before dropping down to the hill you explored earlier. Head back down to the forest and approach the edge of the cliff on the left, where you'll find another Wolf...just before a much LARGER one leaps down to attack! This Sif imitator, the Greatwolf, behaves just like the others, but hits harder and has way more HP; however, depleting just half of its health bar will be enough to "kill" it, which translates to about 4-5 attacks from you, rewarding you with 3 Large Titanite Shards. After retrieving the Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler from the corpse in the path here, proceed underneath the cliff that the Greatwolf was perched on, where another Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler awaits you behind a tree on the right. Past the curve here, you'll find a Millwood Knight patrolling in some ruins in front of a prominent tower - these guys are pretty sturdy combatants, but you can negate the worst of their techniques by simply staying close to them and constantly strafing, which will prevent them from performing their charging attacks while you chip away at their HP whenever you get behind their shield.

Once he's down, turn left and dispatch the Birch Woman waiting in the first crumbling building on the side, then prepare for the annoyance of the field in front of the tower; not only are there two Millwood Knights patrolling here with accompanying Wolves, but the tower itself has two more Millwood Knights who've taken up archery with EXPLODING GREATARROWS, which means you get all the fun of fighting both of those mixed with having to dodge what amount to hollowpoint rounds! Thankfully, you should be able to lure the Wolves over to you first and foremost, due to them moving much faster than the Millwood Knights do, and the Knights themselves aren't any more dangerous alone than the first one you fight (especially the one two-handing a greathammer without a shield, as you can attack him much more frequently if you know to get away from the tip of his weapon whenever it's stuck in the ground), but you'll want to make sure a wall or entire building husk is always between you and the tower while you're engaging any of the enemies so you don't get blasted off your feet - if a greatarrow DOES land near you, you have a couple seconds to roll away before it detonates. When the coast is clear, collect a Heavy Gem from the ruins on the left (there's a bow sticking out of the snow near it, if you're having trouble finding it), then run inside the tower to find quite a few dead Millwood Knights, one of them holding a Soul of a Weary Warrior. Now, climb the stairs and you might find the first archer (for the author, he was despawned for some reason) as well as a ladder leading to the penultimate floor of the tower; climb this and turn around to find the other archer staring out at the vista, which will allow you to easily kill him by simply walking over and spamming L1 until he dies or falls off.

Now you can loot this place - taking the spiral stairs down will let you hunt down and kill a Crystal Lizard for its Twinkling Titanite, as well as pick up an Ethereal Oak Shield (better version of the Ancient Dragon Greatshield for HP regen) from a fallen Millwood Knight on the middle floor you passed on the way up the ladder. At the top floor, if you're willing to risk it, run and jump from the broken wooden beam pointing into the center of the tower to the isolated portion of the floor to the right of it in order to pick up the Millwood Battle Axe before dropping down to the stairs to return to the main top floor. Now, at the hole in the wall, walk onto the ledge outside and climb the ladder to the ACTUAL top of the tower to retrieve not only a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior on the right, but the Captain's Ashesfrom a corpse sitting on another wooden beam. Carefully descend the tower to return to the ground and head around the backside of it, along the cliff, for a Blessed Gem next to more rot. Facing the left side of this valley, you'll see a clear path leading upward and to the right; ignore that for now in favor of heading left toward a copse of Birch Women, most of them alight, whom you'll want to clear out prior to heading further down the left side toward two Millwood Knights and three Wolves. Run down and back up to get the Wolves following you - the Millwood Knights will actually despawn if you move far away enough and respawn when you get close enough, so backing up sufficiently will let you battle the Wolves without having to worry about those damn greatarrows -and then, when they're down, approach the Millwood Knight on the left first to bait him back up the slope with his greathammer out and without causing the other to switch to his axe-and-shield, leaving him specifically for last. In the aftermath, you'll be able to collect the Millwood Greatbow and 5 Millwood Greatarrows from a corpse they were guarding.

Returning to that path you avoided earlier, you'll be confronted by the Greatwolf once again, alongside and his normal-sized compatriots, as you head up; if you run back down the slope as the Greatwolf leaps down to you and end up roughly where he lands, you can get several hits in before he begins attacking, letting you reach the half-HP requirement to kill him fairly quickly and leaving you free to engage the other Wolves with much less risk to yourself. Upon reaching the top of the slope...well, the snowbank will collapse once again, dropping you into a valley. Fall off the stone ledges here, collecting a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler from the last one, and proceed across the floor until you reach an intersection with a steep path leading up to the left - follow this, and you'll reach a field of rot on the left where three Giant Flies guard a new spell, Frozen Weapon (not needed for any of the trophies, though, which goes for all DLC spells). On the ridge above, you'll find way too many Birch Women, most of which will be attacking you with fire, and a couple more Wolves just to really make things fun, with only a Large Titanite Shard awaiting you next to the Birch Women whose branches aren't alight (if you do brave this section, you'll want to constantly roll, as getting close enough to attack one Birch Woman will likely alert another one to begin barraging you). Double back down the valley, and as you approach a long rope bridge leading to a comfortingly well-lit chapel, turn right into a cave to finally find the next Bonfire (Rope Bridge Cave). Once you've rested there, head back outside and cross the bridge, which thankfully won't pose any danger from enemies or poor construction; on the other side, up a trail with several praying and non-hostile Corvians, you'll reach the front door of the chapel, outside of which stands Sir Vilhelm:

When spoken to, he'll be more than a bit gruff, but ultimately direct you inside the chapel - after collecting a Hollow Gem from the corpse on the right side of the building, push open the thick doors and proceed into the main room, filled with paintings, to find Sister Friede. In a manner reminiscent of Crossbreed Priscilla, Friede will actually tell you to just leave the painting and return to your quest via the faded-but-usable Bonfire (Ariandel Chapel) in the corner...but the lady doth protest too much, don't you think? You'll be sticking around to explore the other corners of this world, though talking to Friede a second time will net you a Chillbite Ring (increases frost resistance; this and all other DLC rings aren't needed for the trophy). Speak to Vilhelm again outside for a cryptic warning, if you'd like, and climb the ladder next to the Bonfire to see a hidden area with an unfinished painting that'll become important much later, then return to the bridge...and chop that motherfucker down, just like in the Catacombs of Carthus! As before, you can now use the broken bridge (on the chapel side) as a ladder, so descend it to the rocks at the bottom and walk down the hill toward the frozen roots, stopping to pick up the 4 Rime-blue Moss Clumps from a body hidden in a corner on the right side. Now it's time for the gameplay everyone plays Dark Souls for: platforming. From the middle of the topmost root connected to the hill, drop down onto the Farron Follower standing on the root immediately underneath it, kill him, and turn left (while facing the ravine) to find and drop down onto a proper rock ledge with another Farron Follower to dispatch. From here, take the root curving to the right and fall onto the next root underneath the tip of it toward another rock ledge, where a Crystal Lizard holding a Twinkling Titanite awaits you, though it's liable to run into the open air and isn't worth following if it does; on an adjoining root, a Farron Follower with a shield will approach you, so lure him back and be grateful that you have room to roll around on. When he's down, continue along the root, take out the other Farron Follower, and collect the Ember at the end of the ledge before - then, make your way to this part of the main ledge, overlooking the twisting root that's filling the gap in this section:

Drop down onto this, take it all the way up, and fall onto the root that's twisting in the opposite direction to reach the Millwood Knight that's been standing above and shooting those exploding greatarrows at you; take him out up here, and you'll have one less thing to worry about as you keep descending through the area. Speaking of, fall down to where you were and onto that twisting root again, but descend it this time, following the corners it leads to, so you can not only kill a Farron Follower standing at an intersection near the end, but FINALLY take out the Millwood Knight who's been shooting at you this whole time from the ice field at the bottom. With him gone, it's also safe to (if you want) retrace your steps up the roots to the section that you initially dropped down onto from the ledge, where dropping down to the root just underneath it will let you collect the Follower Sabre, though you run the not-inconsiderable risk of falling to your death in the process. Now, on the ice field, head over to a clearing, opposite of the last root you took down and underneath the main spiral of roots, to light and rest at the Bonfire (Depths of the Painting). To the left of here, you'll see an Icy Giant Crab half-buried in the ice, and there's actually a second one that'll pop out to attack you - one at a time might be doable, but both of them at once sucks and you only get a Crystal Gem for bothering to do it, so instead just...run past them! Reaching the snowbank behind the two crustaceans will cause them to lose interest in you, leaving you free to walk along the frozen riverbed and cut down some frozen Birch Women. Speaking of, if you follow the river through the ice walls here, you'll come across a unique Birch Woman who, despite being alight, will screech and swing wildly at you with her arms instead of using any elemental attacks; when you kill this one, you'll be able to collect Snap Freeze from a corpse she was guarding.

Trivia: this specific Bird Woman was originally given unique dialogue and set as a non-hostile NPC in the game's code, though this was changed pre-release to make her an enemy with slightly different attacks, leaving the dialogue dummied out in the game files. This dialogue, as well as her retained proximity to a sorcery created by Pontiff Sulyvahn, would've implied that she was in fact Sulyvahn's mother, yearning for her child to return. Good job giving birth to the guy that ruined the world, idiot. Double back to the start of the ice river and up the slope on the right for 2 Homeward Bones that you definitely don't need anymore, guarded by one last Birch Woman - then, climb the tall ladder to a ledge, with another ladder leading up to a rot-covered wall, to pick up a Titanite Slab (the "early" one that was promised!). Drop down from the end of this ledge to pick up a Shriving Stone and kill two Giant Flies before using the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the ice floor and head right this time, toward a field of flowers underneath a ton of gigantic icicles; drop down, and it'll be time to face the first DLC boss(es): the Champion's Gravetender & Gravetender Greatwolf.

This battle won't truly kick in until you approach the large stone structure in the distance, where you'll find a large grave...and the Gravetender kneeling before it, where he'll get up to engage you alongside three Wolves. This first part of the fight is easy if you go into it right - take out the Wolves right away as they arrive, and the Gravetender himself will only be a human-sized enemy with strong, but telegraphed attacks. The most trouble you'll have with him is circumventing his shield, which can absorb quite a few hits before you're able to knock it aside; you're best off rolling through his slashes and attacking him from behind or while he otherwise doesn't have his shield up, and while you'll only be able to get 1-2 attacks in at a time, his low HP means they'll count... ...then things change when he reaches 50% HP. Not only will the Gravetender call down the Greatwolf (via standing in place and raising his sword, which is a great opening to attack him during) to begin attacking you as well, but he'll switch up his tactics and start pelting you with sorceries. Before you even think about engaging the Greatwolf, you need to finish off the Gravetender, who thankfully won't be guarding nearly as much now that he's broken out a staff and can even be killed mid-summoning. Now it's time to deal with the Greatwolf, by far the harder of the two; he shares Sif and the Royal Rat Authority's tendency to dash around the arena and knock you on your ass, but even though he's not wielding a greatsword or puking up acid to melt your equipment, the Greatwolf is still a force to be reckoned with because his charges and headbutts hit HARD. You'll want to constantly roll through his attack animations, even if they're just starting up, because of how large his hitboxes are (particularly if you see wind gathering around his body, which indicates a brutal dash is coming). Like the aforementioned wolf bosses, though, he's vulnerable to being attacked from behind and between his legs, and he has fairly low HP like the Gravetender (even more so since you've beaten him twice before now, which permanently depletes his HP for the proper boss fight)... ...but he ALSO gets his very own second phase. At 50% HP, the Greatwolf's eyes will turn red and he'll howl - this is a great opportunity to get a few attacks in, but also the last one, as now he'll stack a long frost-breathing attack on top of his other bullshit. You do not want to be hit by this, so make sure you're either retreating behind one of the pillars of the structure or rolling to his side when he starts it up; additionally, you'll need to watch out for the new form of his dash attack, which is preceded by him rushing all around the arena to fake you out (the actual attack is always telegraphed by wind encasing him). That said, his defense doesn't increase at all, so it should only take you 5-6 more attacks to cut him down for good...you just have to get close enough to him to actually land them, and that's easier said than done when he's running around, so ironically the safest time to do so is when he's rearing up to attack you.

Strategy Video Champion's Gravetender & Gravetender Greatwolf Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Note: the stone structure here is, in fact, the same arena that Crossbreed Priscilla inhabited in Dark Souls I. This, along with the presence of the Corvians that seem to be descended from the Crow Demons of the original game, implies that the Painted World of Ariandel isn't just a new painted world in the setting, but has actually been painted over the Painted World of Ariamis, on the same canvas. With the custodians collapsing, you'll gain the Valorheart used by the Gravetender and the Champion's Bones, a unique item that can be burned at the Firelink Shrine to enable access to a PvP arena. Now, let's use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and Travel to the Rope Bridge, where you'll want to descend the ladder to the left of this side of the bridge: At the bottom, run down the cliffside path to kill a Crystal Lizard for its Large Titanite Shard, then head around the corner beyond it to cut down two Farron Followers. Just past them, you can finally fulfill the dream of Tony Hawk's Dark Souls for about 5 seconds by sliding down the icy slope to a somber settlement adjacent to the chapel. Turn right from the bottom toward the side of the slope to find a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler at the cliff edge before you walk along the main path from the end of the slope, past the gate to the settlement up a hill on the left to a cliff overlooking a valley of Forlorn Corvians in...well, they've seen better days, that's for sure. They'll all go down in a single attack once they start moving, but be sure to attack them ASAP as you move through here. Along the upper ledge that you'll drop down onto here, three Forlorn Corvians lie between you and 3 Budding Green Blossoms, and the mostly-drained moat to the side contains a mix of dead and "living" Forlorn Corvians, as well as a Sewer Centipede, on the path leading to an archway that'll take you inside the settlement.

Turning right here (the left path is currently blocked by a gate) will bring you to your first Corvian Knight - and if there's a term that means the opposite of "fucking around", these guys embody it. They are, bar none, the fastest attackers in the game and combine that ludicrous speed with great reach and weapons that build up bleed way, WAY too fast, letting them easily drain you dry in a matter of seconds if you aren't constantly rolling through/behind them (not the easiest thing in the world in this specific encounter because of the cramped surroundings). Oh, and was it not mentioned that they've also got quite a bit of HP and defense, meaning they can take several more attacks from you than you can from them? Yeah, more fun than a barrel of monkeys, these assholes. Once the first one falls, keep going underneath the bridge toward two more Forlorn Corvians circling a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler, then climb the ladder to enter a building with an Ember and, in the kitchen, a non-hostile Corvian! Talk to him, confirm "I am Ash", and learn , which means you have a responsibility to bring fire to Ariandel...and show it to "her". Oh boy... Outside, leave the Forlorn Corvians ignoring you alone for the moment and turn left into another building to light and rest at the Bonfire (Corvian Settlement). Cross the bridge once you've done so and head left up the path, circling around the back of the first house you find on the left along a cliff, where a Forlorn Corvian will rush out at you from the doorway while a larger one pukes poison a few feet away. Dispatch them in that order, retrieve an Ember from inside the building, and cross the other bridge on the far side of the house to drop down to the waterway on the right, where you'll have another Sewer Centipede to take out and a Simple Gem to collect before pulling the lever to open the gate that blocked you off earlier. Now, use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and cross the two bridges again, but go up the ledge to the left of the second one this time, cutting down the Forlorn Corvian in your path, before jumping across the gap between the pointed cliffs that leads to another Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler from a corpse hanging over the Bonfire.

You don't need to retrace your steps again, thankfully - just turn right up another path into the stone structure adjoining the building, where there's a larger Forlorn Corvian to take care of. When SHOW SPOILER the coast is clear, you can leap off the wooden platform behind some barrels and crates down to a promenade with the Crow Quills, though this will necessitate another Coiled Sword Fragment usage, and the stone balcony through the archway will bring you to a Crystal Lizard carrying 2 Large Titanite Shards. Use the Coiled Sword Fragment again and, this time, follow the procession of Forlorn Corvians up the path on the other side of the bridge, which will lead another Corvian Knight to, uh, pogo-jump down and start cutting a swathe through them with another set of the Crow Quills you just acquired. This guy isn't as much of a close-range threat as the first one was (performing only 5 slashes/thrusts at a time and at a slower pace), but he does like to hop around a lot to put distance between you and himself, has a throwing knife-attack that releases five projectiles at once and covers a lot of distance, and generally trolls you by refusing to stay at a consistent range. Thankfully, there's a bridge pillar in the middle of the path that you can hide behind if needed, and otherwise, this one shouldn't give you as much trouble as the first one did. When it's safe to do so, at the end of the path, look over to the right (near the end of the roof) to see this ledge you can drop off of: Doing so will let you enter a room positively filled with rot, where two Giant Flies are guarding a Dark Gem. Drop down from the ledge here to the path below it and walk along, killing the Forlorn Corvians that stand and fall before you, until you reach a short set of stairs leading up to a larger Forlorn Corvian. After you take him out, head behind the raised walkway to find a normal Forlorn Corvian next to a Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler (the room opposite the stairs has enemies, but no items), then climb the ladder at the end of the walkway and drop off the roof to the top of the arch to the left, which will let you run over and pick up another Large Soul of an Unknown Traveler (dodging sorceries from the Forlorn Corvian on top of the roof) before entering the doorway from here, which will put you above the non-hostile Corvian from before. The wooden walkway here leads outside to a STONE walkway that circles around and connects to the rooftop, letting you dispatch the two Forlorn Corvians and retrieve the Crow Talons (used by the first Corvian Knight you faced).

Now, drop off the roof onto the bridge you were previously on and head into the OTHER building to descend the ladder and open the door at the bottom, creating a shortcut; then, return to the bridge, drop off to the stone walkway, and climb the ladder back up to the taller roof, where it's time to cross the interconnected rooftop and kill the five Forlorn Corvians that'll be slinging sorceries at you all the while. Once the coast is clear, enter the tower on the last rooftop and drop through the gap in the floor, where three larger Forlorn Corvians guard the Slave Knight Set - some interesting lore on those pieces, huh? Open the door to head back outside and use the shortcut you just created (on the left) to return to the rooftops, get back inside the tower, and climb the ladder this time to reach an arching bridge. Dropping off the right side here, you can pick up the 3 Rusted Gold Coins that were just out of reach on the adjoining rooftop, then take the ladder back up and continue along the path at the end. Ignore the next bridge here with the Crystal Lizard on it (a Corvian Knight is waiting to jump you on the tower at the end) and keep going until you reach the roof of the other chapel here, where a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior waits for you behind the belltower. On the side of the roof opposite where you walked onto it, drop through the opening furthest from the belltower to land in the rafters and turn left to find a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight at the intersection...along with a Corvian Knight ready to pounce. After collecting that, fall to the floor and quickly open the chapel door, then the gate outside so you can take on that Corvian Knight alone before dealing with the other one, who likely won't want to leave the building; when they're both down, you can pick up the Way of White Corona from in front of the pulpit. Head outside through the front door and turn left, and you'll find a public library to enrich yourself at - a graveyard on the side has a Birch Woman guarding a Young White Branch (for some reason) and 2 Rusted Coins, after collecting which you should head inside to confront a rare miniboss: none other than Vilhelm.

This bastard, like so many enemies, doesn't fight fair; his moveset is limited, but underestimate him at your own risk. Vilhelm primarily attacks with his greatsword, often using its Weapon Art to wreathe it in blackflame and increase its damage output, and the pain he inflicts with that alone is bad enough...but his other hand wields a Dark Hand that not only serves as his shield, but will let him grab you to wipe out 2/3rds of your HP and heal a significant chunk of his own, so THAT'S what you need to avoid at all costs! To cap it all off, while he has no Estus Flasks, he CAN cast Heal twice (usually when he's around half HP), and if you don't interrupt him as fast as possible, that'll just prolong this even further (more so than his constant rolling will) - the author ended up burning through 10 Estus Flasks, so don't expect an easy time. That said, his eventual defeat will grant you not only his sick Onyx Blade, but the Contraption Key that, when used on the lever located on the far wall, will drop the secret set of stairs that all libraries possess, letting you reach the second floor and meet the Painting Woman! This kind young girl has been stuck here for untold ages thanks to Vilhelm, but is now free to paint again as her uncle Gael wants her to. Exit through the doorway behind her and turn right onto a wooden platform, which will bring you to a Bonfire (Snowy Mountain Pass) and a door you can open for a shortcut to the second floor. Once you head up the nearby slope toward the copse of trees, you'll see many Farron Followers patrolling the area - the warning from before to not engage them in groups if you can avoid it, but they're sticking together 2-4 at a time here, so brace for some annoying encounters.

To start, run up underneath the fallen tree trunk and cut down the four Farron Followers that're walking toward the end of the path, then prepare for about four more circling the edges of the ridges to the left and right to notice and attack you as well, 1-2 at a time; when the coast is clear, collect 10 Prism Stones from the corpse against the tree at the end of the path and pass the tree to turn right up onto the right-hand ridge, where three more Farron Followers await while a fourth wielding a bow will rise up at the end of the path to start pelting you. Double back, deal with THAT guy first, then carefully dispatch the three ambushers, focusing on the spear-wielding one before rolling behind the shield-bearing ones, hopefully taking out one relatively quickly so you're not getting bombarded with sword jabs. Beyond them, you'll want to walk up this section of the rocks: At the end, you can drop down into a greener patch, one side bearing a bridge that leads to the tower of the library and another connected to the fallen tree - cross that, take out the two Farron Followers that'll rush you with spears, and collect the Titanite Chunk on the other side. Retrace your steps to the right-hand ridge and ascend the snowy slope on the left side of it (when facing the fallen tree) to find yourself overlooking a pack of Farron Followers that would've jumped you. Let's return the favor, starting by backstabbing the one directly in front of you, then sliding down the rocks on the left-hand side (adjacent to the large boulder) toward another Farron Follower guarding a Follower Shield. Now, heading around the boulder, kill the Farron Follower sitting on the right-hand side before engaging the fire-breathing one on the ridge, which will prompt two more to begin firing arrows; when they're all down, move toward the valley with the bell on the left side and look to your right for a cave with an Ember, two more Farron Followers resting beside it for quick kills.

Keep going through the valley to rid yourself of the two fire-breathing Farron Followers and a spear-throwing one up near the bell, with another two firebreathers (one resting) behind him, so you can safely retrieve the Titanite Chunk from behind the tree at the edge of the cliff at the end. After going back up to the bell, you'll find an intersection of three paths beyond the Farron Follower on the right that you took care of - go down the right path, where another Farron Follower awaits sudden death, and you can make the Bearer of the Curse proud by kicking down a rotting tree with , creating a shortcut back to the library rooftop. Opposite the broken tree stump, a narrow slope will lead you up to a promenade where, on the left, you can see a Millwood Knight standing in an alcove as part of a trio who would've ambushed you had you gone up the central path. Good thing you didn't! Dropping down and mashing L1 as he's turning around will let you combo him nearly to death, though there's thankfully a path leading through/underneath the promenade that you can retreat down for breathing room when he inevitably starts attacking, and when he's gone, you'll want to fall again to the floor of the gorge here to engage the other two. When you do so, the Millwood Knight far to the left (standing in a tunnel entrance) will start spamming Earthen Wrath, his Weapon Art, to create tremors in a wide area around you from basically any distance; as such, you need to try and take him down first, which is best accomplished by running up to him while he's stuck in the animation of planting his greataxe in the ground, getting as many attacks in as you can, then backing up to make him use the Weapon Art again until he's down. If the patrolling Millwood Knight with the shield approaches you during this, don't panic - he won't actually attack you until he's pretty close, so you can circle around the large tree in the middle of the gorge to stay away from his line of sight and wait until he returns to the (relative) right-hand side of the gorge to resume your duel with the other one. When he finally falls, check the tunnel behind him for a copy of his Earth Seeker and go back outside to deal with

the patrolling one, then collect the 2 Souls of a Crestfallen Knight and Large Soul of a Crestfallen Knight from the corpses against the tree and among the rocks to the right and left of it, respectively. From the right-hand end of the gorge, you can drop down to the path where you fought the first Millwood Knight here and proceed onto the snowbank where you kicked over the tree, letting you return to the main intersection. Avoiding stepping on the snowbank at the top of the central path (which would've dropped you into the ambush you just foiled), turn left from the rocks preceding it, cut down the Farron Follower that gets up, and proceed along the path beyond him for another Farron Follower you can backstab and a split in the road. First, turn left to pick up 2 Large Titanite Shards, dispatch a Wolf, and retrieve the Follower Torch (with a Farron Follower rising up behind it when you get close) at the end of the path, then go back up to the right path to contend with several more Wolves along the cliffside. Following this up, take the first left you come across (at the oval-shaped area with the rock in the middle) toward a red-eyed Millwood Knight that'll initially fire greatarrows at you, but switch to melee when you get too close; he can be stunlocked for a second if you get three attacks in a row on him, but otherwise, you'll want to wait until the end of his combos (especially in this enclosed space) to attack him at all. Defeating him will let you pick up the same Quakestone Hammer that most of the Millwood Knights have been using, even though you don't have the stats to give them a taste of their own medicine. On the original path, there should be two more Millwood Knights waiting for you, and if there are, you'll want to lure the one who already has his greathammer out away from his partner firing greatarrows so you can dispatch him in a quieter location, THEN run back and cut down the archer (however, the author only encountered the archer for reasons unknown, which certainly made for an easier encounter). Next to the archer, drop off the ledge and collect another 2 Large Titanite Shards, as well as kick down another rotted tree to create a shortcut leading back to the previous one. For this next section (i.e., once you enter the tunnel at the end of this ledge), you'll actually want to equip the Follower Torch in your left hand, replacing the Grass Crest Shield, like so:

This will restrict you to using only one of the Sellsword Twinblades and attacking with R1 instead of L1 , but not only will your damage output still be more than sufficient here, the presence of the Follower Torch will be incredibly useful in this dark catacomb. Head through the tunnel, and you'll find yourself in the bowels of the main chapel, filled with rot and Giant Flies - you can still cut these guys down in 1-2 attacks each, but if they DO manage to throw up blood-sucking maggots onto you like the Corpse Grubs in the Cathedral of the Deep, the Follower Torch will burn them right off before they can drain your HP! As you move through it, ignore the pit on the right and the 2 Dung Pies that are honestly not worth collecting over it in favor of clearing out the Giant Flies and, when you reach the last one on the left, attacking the wall it was facing to reveal an archway hidden by illusion. Before you go through here, double back and cross the pit with one of the two walkways, where a set of spiral stairs on the left leads up to the door in the main chapel that couldn't be opened earlier, creating ANOTHER shortcut! Rest at the Bonfire here and talk to Friede, who still insists on you leaving...guess you'd better keep exploring, then. Through the archway in the basement, descend the stairs to reach the bottom of the pit, which is absolutely FILLED with Giant Flies; so long as you walk through here carefully and engage them group-by-group, you should be okay. Clear the entire pit of these disgusting freaks so you can collect the Blood Gem from the center and Vilhelm's Set from the far right corner (wonder how he got here...), then walk along the right-hand wall until you find a bricked-up doorway. Strike this to dispel the illusion and pass through, where a Crystal Lizard carrying a Twinkling Titanite is sitting to your immediate right - at this point, you can re-equip the Grass Crest Shield and return to dual-wielding the Sellsword Twinblades. Kill the Crystal Lizard on the floor for its Twinkling Titanite as well and head outside through the doorway, where you'll find yourself at the top of ANOTHER set of frozen roots leading down to the Gravetender arena; to safely reach the bottom, swap out the Estus Ring for the Silvercat Ring and start dropping from root to root, which will eventually lead you to a platform extending outward from the second floor of the structure that holds the Pyromancer's Parting Flame (lets you regain an Estus Flask for every 12 enemies killed) and 2 Homeward Bones from the corpse at the end. With that done, there's only one more optional task to tackle before the last boss here - enter the center of the structure while Enkindled, and you'll be invaded by Livid Pyromancer Dunnel, former owner of what you just acquired.

This guy CAN be a challenging miniboss, as he uses a katana to attack for high damage from a considerable range and a unique pyromancy that pelts you with multiple fireballs, holding an Estus Flask of his own as well...but the author managed to cut him down before he got a single attack in by simply rushing over as he was spawning in and spamming L1 , following him as he rolled away, until he fell, so copying that strategy should net you similar success and his Floating Chaos. With that done, use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the chapel, avoid Friede's dirty looks, and make your way back down to the pit to find a lever on the far side, on a pillar with a chain running up the side. Rotate this with , and a cutscene will play that shows the statue next to Friede being pulled back to reveal a set of stairs leading deeper into the cathedral. Use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire, and to the left of the stairs, you'll find a summon sign for Slave Knight Gael that will uniquely mention him as appearing "elsewhere" - he's going to show up in the second phase of this last boss and not increase their HP or defense with his presence, so you absolutely need to call on him now. Additionally, make sure to add Red Bug Pellets, Black Bug Pellets, Gold/Human Pine Resins, and Kukris to your Quick Items, and consider switching out the Grass Crest Shield for the Ethereal Oak Shield because HP regeneration could mean the difference between life and death here. Above all else, swap out the Estus Ring for the Chillbite Ring and, if you did all your Covenant grinding offline and consequently have the stats for it, sit at the Bonfire to Attune Pestilent Mist to your sole spell slot - if you need a stave because you sold all the others, return to the Firelink Shrine and buy the basic Sorcerer's Staff from the Handmaid to equip next to the Sellsword Twinblades, which you may want to buy anyway because it's just light enough to keep equipped alongside everything else while preserving your roll if you level up your Ashen One with at least a single point in VIT:

With that done, your loadout should look like this (for the moment): A beautiful mess, isn't it? Mercifully, no other boss will require anything this complicated. If you're in the business of doing so, back up your save here and now, then head down the stairs and talk to the hulking Father Ariandel at the end of the hall to face this boss: Sister Friede. This boss is widely considered to be the most aggravating, if not most difficult, in the entire game, and there's good reason for that. Friede's first phase alone is pretty annoying, but trust us, you're going to love it by the time of your 35th run of this damn fight. While she'll move slowly and technically has a limited range with her scythe, her main gimmick is turning invisible, leaping to somewhere else in the corridor, and preparing to send out waves of ice at you for massive frostbite (hence the Chillbite Ring). This is definitely frustrating to deal with, but it can be mitigated and even make this the quickest phase in a couple of ways: 1. Throwing a couple of Kukris at Friede will keep them visible for a minute even when she conceals herself, letting you track her position until they fade (and you can also see where she's moving by a puff of frost where she lands, as well as any objects that she breaks) -she'll also become visible if you get close to her, so you can sometimes see her as she leaps over your head, letting you know where she'll land. 2. When she lands right after turning invisible, Friede will perform a long animation as she winds up to attack you; this leaves her wide open to you running up and laying into her, and if you can get her back to a wall, she won't be able to separate from you with a backward dash, letting you get a full combo in on her. She doesn't have a ton of HP, so this will make a huge impact if you can pull it off.

Once Friede falls, as you'd expect, she's revived by Ariandel...and now HE'LL join the battle as well with much, much wider-range attacks! Luckily for you, your boy Gael will pop in at this very moment to help out, and his presence is invaluable, particularly with the aforementioned unique nature of his summon: in fact, he's so helpful that you'll want to keep him alive through the end of the phase, so here's how to do that: Ariandel will perform slow, but sweeping and powerful strikes with his bowl of fire, generally pounding the ground in front of him with it but also spitting fireballs out in a wide arc and running across the (now wider) arena to catch up to you/Gael, striking the ground intermittently. Generally, because he's so slow, you can evade him by simply locking on and strafing around Ariandel to keep him turning, but you want to keep him stationary for as long as possible because this is where Pestilent Mist comes in; how the spell works is that it drains HP from the target at a fixed rate proportional to its HP, so it kills everything in the game equally fast, with the drawback that it spawns only a few feet in front of you and stays there until it dissipates about 20 seconds later. Ariandel is so large and slow that the mist will keep hitting him as long as he doesn't move too much, but if he runs off, you'll have to follow him and recast. This strategy will safely drain most of the shared HP bar, especially Sister Friede/ / SHOW SPOILER with Gael keeping aggro on himself, and you can keep the damage he does to you within reason by eating a Red Bug Pellet every now and then, but this is complicated by...

Friede, who retains her previous moveset with one alteration: she won't be turning invisible anymore, but gains a powerful healing spell that's heralded by her kneeling down and glowing golden - when this happens (you'll need to keep an eye on her throughout the phase for this specific purpose), immediately shift your attention from Ariandel, switch back to your Sellsword Twinblades, and run over to land some L1 slashes as fast as you can to interrupt and stop the spell before she finishes and undoes a bunch of your progress. Aside from that, Gael will help keep her busy and should generally be okay so long as you don't let Ariandel attack him too much; mix in some rolls as you're strafing the big guy, and you'll come out alright even as she continues spamming frost. Again, the key is to just cast and recast Pestilent Mist on Ariandel, mixing in some physical attacks if he's close to dying or on the move, and eventually, the two will fall (giving you a Titanite Slab on the first run)... ...but they're STILL not done yet, because Friede will come back one more time, this time in her true form as Blackflame Friede. Now wielding the dark flame that Vilhelm loved to spam, she's at her most dangerous and, even though this third and final phase is a 2-on-1 in your favor (you kept Gael alive, right? Sure hope you did...), she can easily cut you down in seconds flat. As Friede rises from the ground and is surrounded by white and black energy, you need to toss a couple more Kukris into her, then eat a Black Bug Pellet right away because, for better or worse - yeah, no, it's worse - she'll be regaining her invisibility and dishing out frost and dark damage in equal measure with her two scythes. In fact, her attacks will get much more aggressive from here on out: She always starts off with a leap high into the air that crashes down in an explosion of dark, necessitating that you roll left right away.

She'll frequently dash toward you for a three-slash combo of frost-frost-dark, ending in an elemental explosion, and then leap back before you can get a counterattack in - best to roll behind her during this. While visible, she'll sometimes stand in place, generate dark flames around herself, and slash her scythes twice at the ground, generating two trails of black flames that'll home in on you for several meters; back up and roll to the left or right of this when you see it happening. Her single most damaging attack, though somewhat rare, is telegraphed by her scythes flashing blue before she rushes right at you, which will lock you in place while she cuts your throat and wipes out nearly half your HP - roll diagonally left of her during her dash, and she'll whiff while you end up behind her with opportunity for a combo. Apparently, she can still heal herself (though not as much), but the author never saw this happen and you probably won't either. However, her worst attack (which the Kukris were in preparation for), because of how often she uses it, is a buffed version of her previous technique, where she turns invisible and relocates three times around the arena, sending out trails of frost the first two times before creating an eruption of dark around and in front of herself after a brief windup period on the third and final landing. The Kukris will let you find her, but don't bother trying to attack until she's already performed the two frost trails since she'll quickly move from those locations. Basically, Blackflame Friede is a monstrously fast and relentless boss - she can perform as many as 10 attacks in a row before backing up and just about never pauses unless she's caught in a windup animation, so fighting her solo means you're constantly, CONSTANTLY rolling through her many projectiles, every hit taking off an average of 20% of your maximum HP and your HP regen barely keeping you afloat, while waiting for the second-long periods between combos where you can get one L1 before she leaps back and starts the whole cycle over again. Not fun, and that's why you want to keep Gael alive until this final phase; he won't do a ton of damage, but he WILL perform the valuable duty of drawing her attention and letting you rush at her back to combo her from behind, ideally with a Gold Pine Resin slathered on beforehand.

She can still be staggered by two consecutive slashes, just like in her first phase, but she's much more liable to counter with a combo of her own that'll lay you flat, so if she ever turns around to you, run out of there and let Gael keep drawing her aggro. Ideally, he'll survive long enough to let you whittle down most of Friede's HP, but it's completely up in the air how much HP he'll start this phase with, so assume that he won't be there for long and that you need to capitalize on every single opening you get...and still, you can expect this phase to kill you several times. Hoo boy. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. When the corruptor of Ariandel finally falls, you'll gain the Soul of Sister Friede, which you can safely consume, and a new Bonfire (Sister Friede) to light and rest at. If you have the other DLC, you'll also notice a second Bonfire against the wall behind where Father Ariandel was stationed, but there's a couple things you can do before investigating that: Travel to the Corvian Settlement Bonfire and talk to the friendly Corvian inside the other building again, and he'll not only give you another Titanite Slab, but fully explain what he wants for the world. Boy, ain't that something? Then, if you return to the chapel and go up the ladder to the hidden room with the unfinished painting, the Painting Woman will be sitting before it and thank you for your help, as well as promise to finish the painting so someone can inhabit it. Isn't that nice of her? Now, go back down to the boss room and over to the other Bonfire, in front of a strange snake-skinned statue. This isn't an ordinary one that will let you rest and Travel, oh no no - instead, pressing will take you to the first area of the next and final DLC, the Dreg Heap. Let's go, yeah?

Welcome to the far, far-flung future of Dark Souls, where all of human civilization has been jumbled up into a trash pile of ruin and the sun is bleeding. Great place for an adventure, huh? Light and rest at the first Bonfire (The Dreg Heap) and head outside to behold one of the most depressing sights in the entire series...along with a "new" NPC, the Stone-humped Hag: Talk to her a couple times and say you have business with her, and though she claims to not have anything to sell, she'll become a merchant with a few wares (fittingly, as the lore around her implies that she's none other than ) and tell you some interesting, if morbid things about the environment you're now in. To the right, you'll see a tower dome with a circular ledge you can walk along for an Ember - and to the left of it, a message left by your ally Slave Knight Gael, telling us to "Take the plunge". Well, that's trustworthy, so walk off the edge into the ashes below (these will cushion from fall damage in this DLC), turning left if you want a better look at what's left of the sun, then off the NEXT cliff toward a walkway below, where you'll see a horde of Murkmen rise from the ashes below to scramble toward you. These guys are Soul Dregs given a physical form and are correspondingly weak - but only as far as their HP goes, as their weapons dish out huge chunks of damage. Stay up here and let them come to you so you can kill them one at a time, remaining far from the edges as you do so. Descending the walkway, turn left to take care of a sorcerer Murkman standing up along the cliff edge, double back past the corpse of a wyvern toward the stairs, and climb these toward the parapet above to reach another new enemy: the Harald Knight, similar in size and shape to the Winged Knights but doing much more damage. You can stagger them with your L1 combos, but remain vigilant for the smashes of their large swords and, on rare occasions, the bellyflop they'll do after leaping high into the air that'll easily halve your HP. You shouldn't have much trouble with him regardless if you expend your stamina bar to stunlock him in place, so once he's gone, collect the Titanite Chunk from behind him and the Aquamarine Dagger from the corpse up the stairs, then return to the platform that all the Murkmen spawned from and walk onto the far stone ledge toward the item...syke, that's gonna collapse underneath you and drop you into an overturned building!

When the ashes settle, you can collect the Soul of a Weary Warrior in front of you and dispatch the sorcerer Murkmen that'll rise up so you can walk around and collect the Twinkling Titanite, Titanite Scale, and Murky Hand Scythe (behind a bookshelf that you can cross from the top of a set of stairs), evading the regular Murkmen that'll occasionally fall from the ceiling. Through the opening in the wall, you'll have a couple more Murkmen to deal with, but as you approach the next message, an Angel, of all things, will descend to start firing lasers at you! Drop down as the message tells you to and quickly collect the Divine Blessing behind where you land before quickly running to the chunk of stone further along the ledge, which will shield you from the lasers for now. When you're ready, rush down the path here and pick up the 4 Lightning Urns on the side of the building, then run and roll along the wooden walkway on the front side of this building, where you can pick up the first of the highest tier of rings (again, not counting toward the trophy but very useful to have): the Ring of Steel Protection +3, which it's well worth swapping out the Estus Ring for at this time. Head inside the adjoining building, a fragment of Lothric Castle, to find two Lothric Knights with roots growing over their armor. They're as tough as their normal counterpart, even with your personal buffs, but you can thankfully take them on one at a time since they won't approach you together. At the coffin at the end of the hall, collect a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight and head out the archway to the right, turning right past a fountain to find and kill two sorcerer Murkmen as well as collect 2 Rusted Coins near the wood-like mass next to the fountain. Through the doorway on the right here, ignore the spawning Murkmen for now, as they'll respawn endlessly until you take out a specific one further on, and collect the Titanite Chunk from the body on the left, as well as the SHOW SPOILER

Murky Longstaff two rooms over, then attack the arch-shaped wall to the left of the latter item to dispel the illusion and reveal a set of stairs. Ascending these and rushing through the rooms, you'll find a sorcerer Murkman with blue energy gathering around his feet - killing this one will stop the others from respawning, so do that and clear out the room, leaving you free to collect the Ember from the corner.
