In the next room, another sorcerer Murkman will keep others respawning, so cut him down first, deal with the rest (the sorcerers will probably kill themselves generating a ghostly apparition to lunge at you), and pick up Great Soul Dregs from the body at the end, then kick down the ladder on the left side of the wooden platform on the balcony and drop off the right side into ashes covering a stone hall, where a corpse slumped over a missing section of the railing holds the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring+3. Now, drop down to the main "street" and descend it, causing a tower to fall over and smash into the building you were in prior. Before going back to that, continue onward and you'll find what's controlling/powering the Angel: a writhing Grotesque Londor Grower behind a broken wall. Cut it down in one attack, and the Angel dies with it, leaving you free of its barrage of bullshit and able to safely head back to the fallen tower, which you can cross to reach a new NPC: Lapp. Seems like a nice and trustworthy fellow, right? Talk to him three times to initiate his questline and continue to the left, dropping down into more ashes to contend with two more sorcerer Murkmen and a third normal one. Falling off the left side from here will land you safely among more ashes, but bring you into conflict with another Harald Knight and several more Murkmen, so be ready for that. When the coast is clear, you can collect a Titanite Chunk from next to a pillar and 3 Homeward Bones from the edge of the walkway, where yet another message from Gael will tell you to take the plunge. Well, if you won't die...no harm, right? Fall off the edge, and you'll land in a familiar location for players of DSII: the Earthen Peak Ruins, complete with its own Bonfire! Light and rest at this, look over the tragic landscape for a bit, then head up the rock formation to the right of the Bonfire (you may have to exit and reload the game) to find Lapp again - talking to him twice will let you in on the location of some great treasure further down the heap in a swamp.

Keep that in mind for later. Briefly, you'll want to Travel back to The Dreg Heap now that you've progressed a bit and speak to the Stone-humped Hag again to Inquire about the Ringed City, where she'll give you some key information about the eponymous location of the DLC. Return to the Earthen Peak Ruins and go up the fallen windmill to find, appropriately, some Poison Beetles that've somehow survived until now, guarding 4 Black Firebombs. Heading down the path from the Bonfire and turning left, you'll be confronted by another Angel that you'll have to hide from behind leftover pieces of buildings; on the left side, there's a Titanite Chunk behind a chunk of stone, and the second wooden shack further down the main path hides not only a couple Thralls, but the Desert Pyromancer Garb -amazing chest ahead, indeed. On the right-hand side of the path, sprint down to a cliff with 2 Titanite Chunks and turn left down a cliffside path that leads to another Thrall, as well as a corpse with the Giant Door Shield. Then, equip the Silvercat Ring and double back to the shack at the edge of the cliff to roll off the left edge and land on a long root below, which will lead you to the Grotesque Londor Grower that will kill the Angel once YOU kill IT. From here, you'll find an Ember against the wall and climb up a root that'll take you to the end of this area; however, instead of turning right, drop off the broken edge of the building to the left to return to the ashes below, head toward that same shack on the cliff, and enter a tunnel on the right with a Thrall lying in wait for you, as well as a corpse holding an Ember near the opening on the left. Drop down off the ledge facing the swamp in here, and the Thrall below will immediately be outranked in threat by the third Angel that'll swoop in to start battering you again, as well as inflict toxic with falling golden specks if you stay in its line of sight (but behind an obstacle) too long.

Quickly run out to the shack just ahead to cut down two more Poison Beetles and pick up 4 Purple Moss Clumps before heading to the right along a fallen tower to retrieve the Desert Pyromancer Gloves and retreating to safety. When you're ready, run across the poison pool (hello, Mytha), dispatch the Harald Knight on the other side, and cross the poison pool in here to exterminate the Poison Beetles and pick up the Large Soul of a Weary Warrior; then, turn left into a dead end full of poison (you'll be glad you picked up those Purple Moss Clumps) to kill another Harald Knight and pick up the Titanite Slab, a.k.a. the treasure that Lapp was telling you of! Now, head back out to the main poison pool and turn right to dash up a curving tree root, which will let you drop onto another tree root and finally move out of the Angel's range/line of sight. At the top of this root, turn right onto the rooftops, run along them (dealing with a Thrall along the way), and drop onto another root leading to ANOTHER rooftop with a Grotesque Londor Grower linked to the Angel flying over the poison pool. Kill this, and you'll now be free to collect: A Titanite Chunk from the tip of a root over the poison pool, accessible by dropping off a root connect to the side of the rooftop; A Loincloth in the middle of a group of Poison Beetles on a rocky patch of ground near the edge of the cliff; A second Titanite Chunk behind some scaffolding with a Poison Beetle near the rocky patch of ground; A Large Soul of a Weary Warrior near a lone tree in the poison pool; The Harald Curved Greatsword from the poison pool section underneath the roots you took to the first rooftop, guarded by a Harald Knight; A Homeward Bone at the top of the path curving up from this same poison pool section, guarded by a Thrall;

The Desert Pyromancer Skirt next to another lone tree on the very far end of the main poison pool, guarded by four Poison Beetles; The Ring of Favor+3 (swap this out for your current one immediately) at the end of a root connected to the poison pool near that tree; And a Titanite Chunk from a smaller root, accessed by dropping off the left side of the larger root. With that taken care of, return to the root you used to reach the rooftops and instead head into the cave on the left. At first, you'll only find a Thrall wielding a dark-infused greatsword...but when you press further on, you'll be attacked by Desert Pyromancer Zoey and two more Thralls! This'll actually be the most challenging fight of the DLC up until this point, due to the cramped quarters and two fast enemies pestering you alongside a barrage of pyromancies from the last Desert Pyromancer - obviously, you need to take them out first and foremost, but expect to lose a lot of HP from fireballs in the process. When it's just Zoey left, get ready for an intense battle of rolling and weaving between her rapid attacks, which at close-range will vary between whip strikes in all directions around herself and a fan of flame from her hand moving back and forth in front of herself, both of which hurt. She doesn't have a ton of HP, mercifully, but if you give her any breathing room after a combo that drops her below 50%, she'll use one of two Estus Flasks and jump right back into the fray, so expect to need a lot of healing yourself here too. Press her back against the wall when you're spamming L1 , and you should be okay. Upon her death, Zoey will drop Flame Fan, the close-range fire burst she was using and abusing, and you'll be free to pick up 6 Prism Stones from the side of the cave, as well as a Desert Pyromancer Hood near the top of the path to complete the set! On the roots at the end of the path, since you already took care of it, the Angel from before won't harass you and you'll be free to leisurely stroll down the right-hand root, where dropping off the tip will land you on a rooftop covered in ashes and another sign left by Gael will tell you to fall down into the broken tower below to reach the third Bonfire (Within the Earthen Peak Ruins). Rest at and Travel from this to the main Earthen Peak Ruins so you can talk to Lapp, who'll congratulate you for retrieving the treasure and reward you with a Siegbräu...bit surprising, that. When you're ready, return to the other Bonfire and make sure you're Enkindled, then summon Slave Knight Gael from next to the dark circle where you landed, and drop down from the tip of the broken tower (you won't die) to face The Demon Prince, once-defeated. ...well, not right away, actually. This actually starts as a battle against TWO bosses: the Demon in Pain and the Demon from Below. Unlike DS1's Ornstein and Smough, though, these foes thankfully have about the same moveset - they'll swipe at you several times with their claws, leap or charge at you from across the arena, and smash their hands into the ground to create a fiery explosion.

Like the Old Demon King, they can also (temporarily) expend the flames in their body and enter a "burned out" state, where their colors visibly dull; here, they retain some of their usual moves, but gain new ones where they expel toxic from their mouths (the author didn't have any trouble with them when this occurred, but make sure to stay behind them when this occurs). Gael is instrumental to making this fight doable and will more than hold his own against the two bosses, drawing their attention so you can focus on one at a time - and that one is going to be the Demon in Pain. Why? Well, you have to kill both bosses, but like Ornstein and Smough, the next phase of the battle is altered by who goes down first. If the Demon from Below is the first to fall, you'll be facing a very tough boss with many wide-reaching fireball attacks that'll quickly deplete your HP and stamina...but if you take out the Demon in Pain before the Demon from Below, The Demon Prince that rises will only gain a fire beam from his mouth that's extremely easy to roll through. When he does appear, you'll otherwise be dealing with the same set of attacks as before, plus a grab (that's more liable to hit poor Gael than you) and a swooping charge telegraphed by him flying into the air. He does more damage and has a wider area of effect on his attacks, to be clear, but with Gael still by your side this will be a prolonged yet easy second phase. Strategy Video The Demon Prince Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Trivia: the original version of the DLC, before it received a rare last-minute change pre-release, implies through the description of The Demon Prince's Soul that his defeat at the blade of Prince Lorian caused him to lose the flame that kept demonkind alive, which marked the beginning of the end of their civilization. The final version instead indicates that the flame is passed down between demons, which is what allows The Demon Prince to reincarnate here.

With the last(?) of the demons finally perishing, you'll gain the Soul of the Demon Prince, which can be safely consumed (alternatively, you can Transpose it into Seething Chaos, if you want all the spells, or the kickass Demon's Scar), and a Bonfire (The Demon Prince) near some ruins on the edge of the hollowed tree. Speaking of, if you head inside those very ruins, you'll find not only the Small Envoy Banner to be used shortly, but the remnants of the first Firelink Shrine, all the way back in Dark Souls I; nostalgic, huh? Walk down through the tunnel beneath the rectangular hole once used by Kingseeker Frampt, and you'll eventually reach the outside once more - approach the cliff, press , and a stunning cinematic will transport you to the titular Ringed City. Once the cutscene ends, turn around to pick up a Titanite Scale, then proceed along the path until you meet this, uh, fellow on the left: Talk to him a few times (you can choose either option when he asks if you serve the gods), and you'll be directed to the church of Princess Filianore at the base of the cliff ahead since you clearly seek the Dark Soul. Ahead, light and rest at the Bonfire (Mausoleum Lookout) before walking to the stairs...where you'll see a ton of Ghosts suddenly rise from the ground and start reenacting the arrow scene from 300 with you. Yep, to survive this next area, you'll need to master timing, at least in terms of running between cover; first, from the bottom of the stairs, turn right and run around the circular base of the platform you were just on to find the Ruin Set, then start running between the sets of graves along the bridge, waiting for the rows of Ghosts ahead to fade (they always do so after firing 4 shots) before you make the next jog. Up the next set of stairs in the distance, you'll see a large figure gesturing in time with the Ghosts rising; this is the Judicator Giant summoning them, and if you want to explore this area properly, you'll need to cut his ass down.

On the right side of the bridge, you'll see a half-circle outcropping, mercifully with no Ghosts spawning on it; run off the edge facing the Judicator Giant, and you'll land on top of a broken hallway that, when you fall off the roof to the floor below, hides a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight behind where you land. You'll also encounter your first Skeleton of the DLC here, wielding a shield and taking a few more hits than the Catacombs of Carthus ones, and beyond him lies a Crystal Lizard with a Twinkling Titanite and a Titanite Scale. Continue along this ledge until you reach a ladder leading up to two sets of stairs, the right of which will bring you to the Judicator Giant - he's going to keep summoning Ghosts even as you approach and attack him, so you'll want to hug his right side and try to roll through the salvos of arrows in-between attacking him (it should take about 7 presses of L1 to put him down). When the Judicator Giant perishes, you'll receive a Divine Blessing (and can retrieve a Titanite Chunk from underneath him) and be free to walk along the bridge, where a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior, Ember, 2 Titanite Chunks, and 2 Budding Green Blossoms among the gravestones. Double back to the platform where the Judicator Giant sat and descend the stairs to find the first of three non-hostile Locust Preachers: He'll impart some cryptic words related to Alva, but otherwise won't tell you anything or attack you, so keep going down the stairs and prepare to encounter Pygmy Paladins: essentially basic Hollows that, while easy to kill, like to literally push you around (such as in the direction of the closest ledge) and can even throw a lightning bolt at you, on top of dropping down and crawling up from out of sight to surprise you. At the end of the walkway here, collect 2 Purging Stones from a corpse, then turn left and enter the building to find and light a Bonfire (Ringed Inner Wall). Through the archway at the end of the hall in here, you'll emerge on a balcony outside with not only another Ember, but Lapp, whom you can talk to twice in order to receive a final Siegbräu from him and learn that he's seeking out the Purging Monument to undo his Hollowing and remember who he really is...best of luck there, chap. Head back inside, turn right into the other archway opposite the Bonfire, take out the Pygmy Paladin that jumps you from behind the wall, and descend the rest of the stairs (watching out for a new Pygmy Paladin variant with crystals in his back that builds up curse while he's near you and alive) to find a Hollow Gem.

In the field of flowers past this, you'll encounter another new enemy - a Ringed Knight, substantially more dangerous than the Paladins, who attacks with a longsword he can light on fire and wields a small shield that can take quite a bit of damage, though he's not too bad if you roll through his opening lunge and attack him relentlessly afterward. Around the corner from here, you can find a Titanite Chunk guarded by a crystal-bearing Pygmy Paladin, after which you can descend the stairs to be assaulted by a Hobbled Cleric. These guys have a unique miracle that lets them create a decently large damage-dealing circle on the ground, so cutting them down is your first order of business whenever you see one; if they duck underneath the stone on their backs, you can kick ( L + R1 while unarmed) them over to deal double damage. Head inside the circular building and deal with a few more Hobbled Clerics before running onto the chandelier in the center of the room, then OFF of it onto the lower floor to kill another Hobbled Cleric and collect a Twinkling Titanite. On the ground floor of this building, you'll be confronted by a spear-wielding Ringed Knight who'll pose a greater than the last due to his longer range, ability to hit a wide area around himself with his swings, and medium-sized shield that'll absorb a lot more damage - it's best to fight him in the center of the room where you have the most mobility. Collect the Shriving Stone from the body against one of the pillars in the center when the coast is clear and climb the short set of stairs leading outside to a LARGE set of stairs where three Harald Knights patrol; dealing with these guys one-on-one may be perfectly doable, but two or three at once is borderline suicidal, so you'll want to run allllll the way to the top of the stairs here, wait for the "frontmost" Harald Knight to near the top of the steps, and get his attention while the Harald Knight behind him walks back down,

allowing you to take on all three alone. However, before you go down the stairs to deal with the last one, go to the base of the highest set of stairs here and collect a Titanite Chunk from the left side (with another Pygmy Paladin waiting to pounce) before crossing the small bridge above the stairs to dispatch the Pygmy Paladins who'll otherwise be raining lightning bolts down upon you. Once you're on the other side of the bridge, retrieve 2 Mossfruits (temporarily boosts bleed, poison, frost, and curse resistance) and head through the corridor on the left to face another longsword-wielding Ringed Knight, with the stairs on the left bringing you to another confrontation with the Alva, Seeker of the Spurned (around the corner to the left of the monument here). Take him out with the same strategy as before, and you'll be given the Wolf Ring+3, with the Black Witch Set of his late wife just behind him. Poor bastard...return to the main stairs and head to the top, where you'll see that the door in the arch is suspiciously illuminated - walk up to it, and you can talk to Shira, Knight of Filianore. Speak to her several times and, when asked, name Gwyn as your god to be tasked with killing the only dragon left in the entire world, Darkeater Midir, which she'll give you the Sacred Chime of Filianore to help accomplish. Now, descend the stairs, making sure to dispatch the Hobbled Cleric and crystal-bearing Pygmy Paladin on the left just past the first bridge, and when you approach the second bridge, two Pygmy Paladins will pop up on the left to throw lightning bolts at you - cut them down and pick up the 2 Mossfruits in the alcove here before crossing to the other side of the stairs, where an alleyway filled with crystal-bearing Pygmy Paladins will lead you to a balcony with another spear-wielding Ringed Knight and, on the left side, two Pygmy Paladins (and a third crystal-bearing one who'll drop down on the right) that'll need to die first so you can battle WITHOUT getting electrocuted every 5 seconds. When the coast is clear, pick up the Ringed Knight Spear from the right-hand side and cross the bridge if you want to hear another Locust Preacher ramble about ol' Orbeck, then wait for two of the newly-spawned Harald Knights to go up the stairs before dropping down and killing the one who stays near the swamp below; it'll make your life much easier if you take out the other two with Pestilent Mist when they come down, but otherwise do your best to split them up.

When the coast is clear, collect the Large Soul of a Crestfallen Knight off the bottom of the stairs and venture into the swamp (thankfully not poisonous this time) to collect a Titanite Chunk before turning left, collecting the item from behind the fallen parapet, and running past the Hobbled Clerics (really not worth fighting en masse) to pick up a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight. Climb the tall ladder here, and you'll reach not only the Locust Preacher from before (who'll talk about Sirris this time if prompted), but a set of stairs leading up to a Crystal Lizard carrying 2 Twinkling Titanite (he'll likely run over the side, so only pursue if you want to) and a bridge with TWO Ringed Knights waiting on the other side. At this point, your Sellsword Twinblades might be on the verge of breaking, and there's a much more important enemy to use them on, so...run right the hell past these guys once they cross the bridge, and don't stop until you've reached the next building beyond them with an open archway. Inside, you'll find Lapp once more (and, y'know, the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring+3 or whatever) - talking to him will reveal that he's yet to find the Purging Monument, and since you don't know where it is either, you can't do anything else here for now. From the ledge outside, you'll want to drop through a broken section of the railing to where you picked up the Ringed Knight Spear, then quickly retrace your steps to the ladder (to avoid drawing the attention of one or both of the Ringed Knights still patrolling on the bridge) and ascend the stairs again, but turn right this time to drop onto a path leading up to a stone tower - where, if Enkindled (and you really should be for all this), you'll promptly be invaded by Silver Knight Ledo, though you won't see him until you enter the tower. This guy is rough to fight, even though he only has one trick in the form of his greathammer; not only does it dish out tons of damage and come out fairly fast, and not ONLY does Ledo himself love rolling away just as you begin your counterattacks (though he thankfully carries no Estus Flasks), but his Weapon Art lets him clad the head of his greathammer in rocks, increasing the damage every strike does and even letting him perform an AoE attack by slamming it into the ground and scattering the rocks outward.

Basically, he's another dark spirit that's tougher than several bosses, even with your level and equipment, so don't take him lightly - your best bet is to attack him while he's stuck in the Weapon Art animation OR backed into a corner where he can't roll away, but you can only get in about 3 attacks at a time before he starts smashing you again. When he falls, you'll receive Ledo's Great Hammer for yourself and can head out the other archway in the tower to collect a Titanite Chunk, and next to the path you took up here, looking over the cliff will let you see multiple ledges that you can drop down onto, delivering you to a very useful upgrade in the form of Havel's Ring+3, which you should immediately swap out the regular one for so you can finally equip the entirety of Havel's Set! Now, drop down to the swamp, return to the main stairs, and head toward the group of much smaller Locust Preachers on the right to pick up a Dark Gem once they flee. Keep going right, and you'll find your first hostile Locust Preacher, who'll attack you with blue energy spears and take several attacks to put down. Up the stairs behind him, you'll find a corpse with 4 Prism Stones draped over a railing and, mercifully, a new Bonfire (Ringed City Streets) to light and rest at. Head back outside and cross the swamp directly from this point to reach another Locust Preacher guarding a Twinkling Titanite before walking along the crystal-covered wall to reach a fallen pillar leading up to a Hobbled Cleric that you'll want to take out now so the Locust Preacher further ahead can be engaged alone. Up the hill beyond this structure, you'll have three more Hobbled Clerics all trying to take you out, so do your best to battle them one at a time and collect a White Birch Bow and Titanite Chunk from the corpses here when it's safe. Descend the hill on the other side, and you'll reach yet another white tree (with another goddamned Hobbled Cleric waiting at its base) with three Young White Branches, worth collecting in order to finish a storyline later. Back into the swamp from here, entering the tower on the left that the Hobbled Clerics are praying to will let you find a Church Guardian Shiv (new throwing item that consumes FP)...though it'll ALSO alert the Hobbled Clerics, so run back outside to the hill and exit the game to reset them to praying when you reload it.

When you're ready, run past the Hobbled Clerics and the Locust Preachers in the swamp, still hugging the left wall, until you reach a clearing filled with dead Harald Knights - and the Iron Dragonslayer, who'll rise up at the end to engage you! This is, in fact, the same Dragonslayer Armour that you fought in Lothric Castle earlier, so its moves and strategy are the same as last time; the main difference is that there's no Pilgrim Butterflies harassing you this time, and the Iron Dragonslayer itself does quite a bit less damage (and has substantially less HP) than the proper boss did, so you should be able to take it down easily on your own, rewarding you with the Iron Dragonslayer Set as well as the 2 Titanite Scales you can pick up from the corpses here. Keep circling around the perimeter of the swamp on dry land, retrieving a Soul of a Crestfallen Knight from underneath a tree in the swamp and a Titanite Chunk from behind a rock near the church in the distance, then run over and take out the Judicator Giant roaming the swamp (this guy can summon a specter of Ledo, so be careful!) for his Hidden Blessing and Titanite Chunk. Once you've gotten the Large Soul of a Weary Warrior near him, head over to a crystalline landmass just beyond him for ANOTHER Large Soul of a Weary Warrior and Titanite Chunk before climbing the hill on the left side for both the Ringed Knight Straight Sword and the last non-hostile Locust Preacher, who'll speak of the sad fates of Irina and Eygon. Doubling back into the swamp, approach the tilted rotunda between you and the large, sunken church to retrieve the Preacher's Right Arm, which will prompt FOUR Locust Preachers to leap out of the muck around you - this is the only time you'll really be threatened by them, but if you back up to the hill and let them come over to you 1-2 at a time, they're still pretty doable as long as you roll through their blue light stick attacks. A small tower beyond them to the left bears another Large Soul of a Weary Warrior, but after that, there's nowhere left to go but the roof of the church where THREE Ringed Knights await you.

Battling all three at once is objectively suicidal, so here's what you'll do: walk onto the roof just far enough to get their attention, then hightail it back into the swamp while the longsword-bearing Ringed Knight runs after you, with the other two only briefly giving pursuit before returning to their patrols. Take out this first Ringed Knight solo in the swamp, then lure out the spear-wielding one that stands closest to you on the roof before finally engaging the last longsword bloke, wherever he ends up by the time you come back for him. On the far side of the roof, you'll be able to pick up a Twinkling Titanite and see ol' Midir fly past to a distant cliff so he can start staring at you...menacingly! Briefly equip the Silvercat Ring and drop off the left side of the roof, facing Midir, to walk along the lower wall of the church and take out another spear-wielding Ringed Knight to collect the Black Witch Veil from behind him. Return to the rooftop, drop off the OTHER side of the far end onto the rocky terrain, and continue heading right toward a stone tunnel to reach a room with a door leading back to the Bonfire. While you're here, Attune Chameleon to your one slot, equip a staff of your choice (if you have the INT), and return to the prior room to find this engraved wall to the right of the doorway: When read, the engraving will tell you to "Show your humanity" - and, in the typically vague Dark Souls fashion, this means you need to transform into a Humanity sprite in order to reveal a secret ladder. How? Well, both Chameleon and the consumable Young White Branches, when used, disguise you as an element of the surrounding environment, ostensibly to camouflage you from enemies; in this case, though, using either of them in the swamp (just down the stairs from the Bonfire and past the Locust Preacher there) has a chance of turning you into that Humanity sprite (if it doesn't, rolling will dispel the disguise so you can try again), and walking back to the engraving will drop a ladder for you. If you're using Young White Branches, consider making a backup save before you try this so you don't run out if you have reeeeally bad luck.

Once the ladder's down, climb it aaaaaaaaaaall the way to the top and drop out from the ledge onto the field of flowers below, where going along the right side will bring you to ANOTHER Judicator Giant that, at least, you should be able to kill before he makes too many summons. Moreover, two Ringed Knights are patrolling here, and you'll want to engage the longsword-wielding one before the spear-wielding one since he's still the easiest of the variants. When they're all down, descend the stairs on the far edge of the field and climb down the ladder to reach the ledge leading to the second bridge above those main stairs. First, head along the left side toward a Pygmy Paladin so you can pick up the Dragonhead Shield, then cross the bridge for a Large Soul of a Crestfallen Knight...and the Purging Monument that Lapp was talking about, on the right. This can be used to remove sin (not relevant since you haven't killed any NPCs...right?) and reverse Hollowing, but its main purpose for you is to advance Lapp's storyline. And hey, look at that, the ledge where you got the Dragonhead Shield is right above the bridge leading to where he's holed up, so drop down, head over to him, and Speak of the Purging Monument to tell him where to go - speak to him again if you ALSO want him to pledge himself as a true friend to you, what a sweetheart. With that done, use the Coiled Sword Fragment and return to the Bonfire, then head through the shortcut door back out to the rocky area, taking the left path down and turning right before the bridge to descend a path toward a Titanite Scale. There's a Ringed Knight further down this path, so lure him back up to the larger area to take him on without risking a fall into the void, and when you're done, you can find a Dragonhead Greatshield underneath the bridge at the bottom of the path.

With that done, it's time to (once you're at full HP) cross the bridge...where Midir will begin breathing fire down upon you! There's not really any way to avoid getting hit by it unless you time your roll just right, and you're more or less forced to because the safe spot you can hide in - a tunnel in the rock wall on the right side - is just far enough away that you won't be able to run to it before the first breath of flame reaches you, so you're going to take quite a hit. Luckily, once you do get inside and kill the Pygmy Paladin waiting for you, you'll be completely safe; now, you'll be playing a timing game. First, collect the 2 Titanite Scales from the corpse on the other side of the tunnel, then double back to pick up the Soul of a Weary Warrior on the path. When Midir unleashes another blast of fire in response to seeing you, wait for it to pass (along with him, as Midir will be flying across to the other side of the bridge and spend several seconds roosting there) and then book it down the path, ignoring the other item there (as it's literally Rubbish) in favor of falling off the left side of the path toward a ledge several feet down with another 2 Titanite Scales. From here, head up the ledge, dispatching the two Pygmy Paladins along the way, toward the mine entrance underneath where Midir was stationed, quickly getting the Large Soul of a Weary Warrior several feet away on the path, before rushing inside the entrance. Heading up the stairs to the left, you'll see a Crystal Lizard, but the ground will give way just before you reach it - and as some Skeletons come to harass you, you'll be invaded by the Moaning Knight! Despite the, uh, suggestive name, you're basically just fighting Eygon here, complete with heavy-hitting slams of his greathammer and a Weapon Art that produces a powerful shockwave after he points his weapon at the ground. However, if you lock him into a corner (such as in the room next to where you fall) and start spamming L1 , he'll be stunlocked and then dead in short order, giving you the Blindfold Mask. Collect the Lightning Gem from inside the room and keep going up the stairs, with a Simple Gem awaiting you on the right side, to eventually reach another broken section.

Drop down from here and turn around to walk over the rubble next to the entrance, which will bring you to a room with none other than Lapp in a, uh...familiar position. Talk to him, and he'll indicate that there's some nice treasure over the edge of the ledge outside, so peer over it (at the red cloth) and - oh, god dammit, it was all along! EVERYONE BOUGHT IT! EVEN HIS IMMEDIATE FAMILY BOUGHT IT!...well, actually, this helps you out because you've dropped to the exact lower staircase needed to reach the rest of the tower. Going up the stairs here will let you drop to another staircase that, upon doubling back down, holds a Blessed Gem. Head up the stairs from there until you reach a room with a ch- nah, you're all too smart for that by now, it's a Mimic, so cut it down and retrieve the Ring of the Evil Eye+3 from it, then keep climbing the stairs until you reach the next room, where some Skeletons will stand in your path as you go up the straight stairs within to reach the OTHER side of the stairs you originally started on. Kill the Crystal Lizard on the right if you want/can for a Titanite Scale and Twinkling Titanite before heading up the stairs one more time to reach the Bonfire (Shared Grave) and resting at it; you can also retrace your steps/drops down to where you found Lapp to get Lapp's Set, then use the Coiled Sword Fragment to get back up. Now, heading out the doorway from the Bonfire will bring you to another bridge - where Midir will fly down to fight you For RealTM (not really)! When you're in front of him, Midir will breathe fire as before, but you can largely prevent him from doing so by hugging the area underneath his chest/next to his arms, which you'll be attacking - he does have an HP bar to deplete, though not a proper boss one. That said, he won't be idle while you do so, swiping his arms across the area and likely knocking you on your ass more than once, so be prepared to heal up during the brief lulls between his strikes and to do so often. When his HP is about 70% depleted, Midir will rear up and start breathing fire directly at the ground, only for the fire to turn to white energy before he turns his head and runs it across the bridge; make sure you're NOT on the bridge (as the author was) when this happens, because a series of purple explosions will occur in the wake of the beam.

However, you'll have a great opportunity in the aftermath of this to land your remaining attacks, as Midir will stagger and collapse once you get him down to 10% HP, with going down to 0 SHOW SPOILER sending him falling into the ravine here. Don't worry, you can have a proper fight with him later...if you want. Keep crossing the bridge to collect a Titanite Scale and enter the building at the end. Before heading up the stairs on the left, attack the wall to the right of them to reveal a Hobbled Cleric to put down, then attack the wall behind him to pick up a Large Soul of a Weary Warrior and the wall behind THAT to retrieve Lightning Arrow, with the stairs themselves having a Crystal Lizard that'll drop 2 Titanite Scales once you chase it down. At the top of the steps, you'll enter a room with a statue of Gwyn in the center, holding an item you'll get shortly; ride the nearby elevator up to the shortcut door leading back to the Ringed Inner Wall Bonfire, so open that, rest to re-Attune Pestilent Mist (if you can), and get back on the elevator, but turn left to find and step through a doorway hidden in the shaft. Turning left in the hallway this links to, collect the Ember and attack the statue to the right of it, revealing ANOTHER hallway that leads to Filianore's Spear Ornament (item for the totally optional Covenant of this DLC) and a loooooong ladder, at the bottom of which lies what seems to have been a place of communion with Kaathe, containing the Antiquated Plain Garb and the Violet Wrappings. Still want to fight Midir? This is the place for it - ignore the summon sign for Shira, Knight of Filianore no matter what strategy you're about to use and drop through that to a crystalline lake far, far below. Equip a staff if you have Pestilent Mist ready and head over to the slumbering form in the distance to finally, FINALLY battle Darkeater Midir.

You might think that, given how other massive bosses in the series have worked, the safest option here is to stay underneath Midir's belly/behind his tail and attack his legs - and you'd be suicidally wrong. Contrary to what many, many boss fights have taught you, the safest and best place to attack from is right next to his head - and even that's going to be a challenge. For starters, Midir has THE most HP of any boss in the entire trilogy and the defense to go along with it, so the battle will take quite a while no matter how efficient you are, and not only do his basic claw and tail swipes cover a HUGE area, but he loooooooooves to dash (with little telegraphing + for huge damage) and hop all over the arena, making it a chore to keep up with him unless RNG favors you. Plus, when he's REALLY far away, he'll start lighting you up with fire attacks, and when you're behind him, he's liable to rear up on his hind legs and breathe fire downward, spreading it across the area and invariably hitting you no matter how much you roll. Hell of a last optional boss... That said, attacks on his head do double damage and you can easily get 3-5 in between strikes; the trick is learning to tell which set of attacks he's about to unleash (two swipes of his claws, a few bites from his head, or breathing fire from his right to the middle) so you can roll through them properly and exploit the momentary pause after each one. He's most likely to swipe his claws, so watch for those tells more than any other and you should get through the first phase more or less okay. If you want (and have the stats for it), Pestilent Mist will do more damage to him than anything else and his enormous hitbox means he won't be able to escape it unless he crosses to the other side of the arena, which he's unlikely to do if you stay near his head, so consider using that to speed this up. At 50% HP, Midir will gather dark to himself and unleash it in a radial explosion...but you can survive this unscathed with constant rolling and go right back to attacking him as before, as he doesn't gain any new attacks that he can unleash at close range. Additionally, at about 10% HP, if you've been attacking his head consistently, he'll collapse from being damaged so much and basically let you get your last few slashes in for free. It's just that "easy"!

Strategy Video Darkeater Midir Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Trivia: the cavern that Darkeater Midir is fought in heavily resembles, and may in fact be, the cave that the First Flame is shown being discovered in during the opening cinematic of Dark Souls I. With the last dragon being put to rest, you'll receive the Spears of the Church and the Soul of Darkeater Midir, which can safely be consumed (or Transposed into Old Moonlight if you want all spells), as well as a new Bonfire (Darkeater Midir) in the middle of the cavern. Travel back up to the Ringed Inner Wall Bonfire and make your way back to Shira for a Titanite Slab, then return to it with the Coiled Sword Fragment and take the elevator down again, but when you step into the hidden doorway, turn right this time and you'll be able to drop down onto the statue of Gwyn so you can retrieve the Chloranthy Ring+3 from its hand. Head outside at long last, feel the daylight(?) for the first time in a while, and pick up 5 Budding Green Blossoms from a corpse on the left as you head toward the last Ringed Knight, uniquely wielding paired greatswords that hit hard, but leave him wide-open to attacks after each combo and prevent him from using a shield, so with enough patience he's even easier to kill than the longsword ones are. Once he's down, you'll receive those Ringed Knight Paired Greatswords and can continue along the path (the Divine Spear Monument to the right is what you can offer Filianore's Spear Ornaments to if you really want to work on the Covenant, and there's a Ritual Spear Fragment behind it that can be used as a powerful ranged attack when fighting on behalf of the Covenant) to the stairs, the left side of which will let you drop down and pick up 2 Twinkling Titanite, then return to the path by dropping down again to a ledge below it. At the top of the stairs, when you reach the doors of the church, the deep voice of Judicator Argo will order you to turn back and stop risking the spread of the Abyss...but you're gamers and you don't LISTEN to instructions, so open those doors, enter the fog, and prepare to face the penultimate boss:

Halflight, Spear of the Church. Now, if you're playing online for some reason, this boss fight will have another player (a member of the Covenant) sub in to fight you, and all bets are off for how difficult that will be - but if you're offline, well, the NPC you get instead is a pushover, at least relative to most other bosses. To start, Argo will summon none other than a Painting Guardian to pelt you with Church Guardian Shivs, but both of them can be cut down in relatively short order (and you should prioritize Argo himself, especially while he's stuck in the animation process); a short time later, Halflight will appear. He attacks very fast and has a pretty wide range of abilities (including homing balls of light and a Ritual Spear Fragment), but most of them do a normal amount of damage or can be hidden from behind the pillars here - the tricky part is not getting stunlocked by them and actually landing your own attacks, as Halflight both rolls a whole lot and keeps his stupid shield up most of the time. The author found that there's not really a consistent time for openings, so just slash at him whenever he's close and you might land 2-3 hits out of a full combo, which will make quite a dent thanks to his low HP. At 50% HP, even if he's dead, Argo will summon one more Painting Guardian, and once again you HAVE to prioritize him because, if left alone, he'll heal quite a bit of Halflight's HP and can do so repeatedly. His moveset is otherwise the same as the first one, but taking him down will be harder now with Halflight spamming his ranged attacks; once he's dead, though, Halflight himself won't have gained any extra power or techniques, so it's just a battle of attrition from then on out. If you do find yourself having trouble with this fight and need a second attempt, Patches can be summoned from the right side of the front doors of the church for one last bit of jolly cooperation.

Strategy Video Halflight, Spear of the Church Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. With the last Spear of the Church put 6 feet under, you'll receive a Titanite Slab and another Filianore's Spear Ornament, leaving you free to run to the back of the church through the doors on either side of the arena and up the stairs to reach a Bonfire (Church of Filianore). Behind you is a lift that'll take you up to a long set of stairs, and at the top, you'll open the doors to find Filianore holding a shell...and when you touch it with , a cutscene will have her finally wake up, . Ah. In the ashes that follow, you'll find a new Bonfire (Filianore's Rest) and can head through the opening in the wall to gaze upon the wasteland. Turn left and circle around the remnants of the church to find not only a Pygmy begging for salvation from "Red Hood", but, inexplicably, the same dual-wielding Ringed Knight still patrolling, now dropping ANOTHER Titanite Slab if you kill him. Once you've done so, use the Coiled Sword Fragment, Attune Vow of Silence if you can, then head outside again and turn right this time after you pass the long wall to enter a set of ruins, where will invade you for your role in ending The Ringed City. She's honestly tougher than Halflight was, owing to her spamming of Lightning Arrow and several Estus Flasks, but if you use Vow of Silence to disable the former and press her with combos to interrupt the latter, she'll go down in relatively short order, though you'll want to watch out for her Weapon Art that creates a shockwave and triggers a random effect. Once she's dead, you'll receive her Crucifix of the Mad King and can return to the room where you once spoke to her in order to pick up Shira's Set.

With that done, though, there's only one thing left to do (that will, admittedly, let us do a couple more things afterward): face the final boss of the DLC and, chronologically, the Dark Souls universe. Equip some Poison Pine Resins and head to the left again through the archway in the ashes, and a cutscene will play as you face your (almost) final foe... . Welcome to one of the most spectacular, heartbreaking, and tough bosses in the whole trilogy. Pumped up on the dark blood of the Pygmies, Gael is much stronger and faster than he was as a summon, and consequently, you're in for a hell of a fight. In his first phase, Gael will limit himself to arcing and lunging slashes and stabs of his greatsword, which hit hard but do leave him open to a couple of attacks after each combo and, on occasion, when he staggers of his own accord from one too many attacks performed (the author found that the best attack to exploit/punish was his leaping downward stab, as the telegraphing makes it easy to see coming and roll through). Make no mistake; this battle will take a while no matter how efficient you are because Gael has so much HP - patience is absolutely the name of the game here, and the only way you'll survive to even see the next phase is by rolling, rolling, ROLLING through his combos, ideally toward him. You can, however, speed this up with Poison Pine Resin since he happens to be weak to that element, but you'll have to find a safe few seconds to apply it first. At 66% HP, just to fake you out, Gael will fall to his knees, seemingly defeated...but the blood of the Dark Soul will revive him, even stronger than before, and NOW the fight really begins. Gael will continue performing his slashing and stabbing attacks, only with his animated cloak now mirroring them after a second-long delay for extra damage; this is where rolling toward him comes in handy, as the invincibility frames will protect you from the cloak attacks and let you get behind him for your own. Additionally, he'll use one of two ranged attacks when you're far enough away from him: an upgraded form of his light disc where he spawns five that rocket outward and come back to him, and a barrage of bolts from his repeating crossbow that'll track you for a few seconds, though both can be easily evaded (the discs by rolling through them and the bolts by strafing to the left or right). Honestly, this phase is somewhat easier than the first one, if only because you get more opportunities to attack him from behind after his combos...but it's not the last one.

At 33% HP (yep, he's just built like that), Gael will undergo one more change - he'll stop and groan while his cloak writhes before unleashing dozens of red skull projectiles that'll fan out and land on the ground around him. Run away when he does this because not only do the projectiles themselves hurt, but the spots where they land will be struck by lightning a moment later, and you SHOW SPOILER absolutely don't need that on top of everything else he's throwing at you (also be prepared for it to happen again, as you'll likely see it once or twice more). Otherwise, this phase is identical to the second, save for a chance for him to unleash more skulls at the end of some combos. Even if you're being as careful as possible, you can expect this to drain all your Estus Flasks and maybe even force you to use a Divine Blessing, as the author did; Gael will push you to your limits like no other boss does, and as the inheritor of the Dark Soul, that's to be expected. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. Trivia: Gael is meant to mirror the Ashen One, Bearer of the Curse, and Chosen Undead in many ways, as a formerly nameless and lowly Undead sent on a lengthy and exhausting journey for an inscrutable task that he won't live to see the result of completing. However, the most famous aspect of his design is his greatsword, notably and visibly worn down and broken by past battles - in its current state, it looks exactly like an enlarged version of the Broken Straight Sword you can acquire early in all three games, wielded only by mad Hollows. When Gael finally falls on the edge of the apocalypse, you'll gain the Soul of Slave Knight Gael, which can be safely consumed, and none other than the Blood of the Dark Soul, as well as one last Bonfire (Slave Knight Gael) if you ever want to come back and gaze upon desolation. Now, with everything else laid to ruin, there's two more things you can do:

Return to The Dreg Heap and go out onto the ledge where the Stone-humped Hag was; you'll find her body with the Old Woman's Ashes, and since you were nice enough to talk to her, the Angel she's turned into in the distance won't attack you. Rest in peace... Travel to the Ariandel Chapel Bonfire and go up the ladder to find the loft now in flames and the Painting Woman unbothered. Handing over the Blood of the Dark Soul to her will have her thank you for your help, and you can even choose to have the world she's going to paint named after you - but talking to her a second time will result in the sad knowledge that . Oh, cruel irony... And with that, both DLCs are fully completed - time for the endgame.

h: Kiln Of The First Flame (To Link The Fire)
t: Well, it's time at last. In the Firelink Shrine, once you've Transposed or used up your Soul Chunks and leveled up accordingly, place the final Cinders of a Lord upon the central throne, which will trigger the Fire Keeper to approach the Bonfire; when you speak to her, a cutscene will ensue that sees the Cinders (and Ludleth) being burned to light the way to the Kiln of the First Flame (in the far, far future of the setting), which you'll automatically be transported to. Before proceeding into this final, final area, light and rest at the new Bonfire (Flameless Shrine) to return to the Firelink Shrine and go up to what's left of Ludleth to collect his Skull Ring (68/107). Now, from the Flameless Shrine, go up the stairs and outside to witness one of the most quietly tragic and awe-inspiring sights in the trilogy, set untold eons in the future, then use the Bonfire to teleport to the landmass in the distance, where one more Bonfire (Kiln of the First Flame) waits for you to light it - if you have The Ringed City DLC but haven't gone to it yet, another special Bonfire to the left of this one, in front of some graves, will teleport you there. From here, all you have to do is walk up the ashen stairs, past the flash-melted pillars from the first game; along the way, you'll want to swap out the Ring of Steel Protection for the Flame Stoneplate Ring, as well as equip Red Bug Pellets and Gold Pine Resins (you'll be using both quite liberally). At the top, with the bleeding sun in view, you'll meet the final boss in a very familiar pose: the Soul of Cinder. You're facing the deific incarnation of everyone who's ever Linked the Fire - yes, that includes the Chosen Undead and the Bearer of the Curse - and regardless of your intentions, they're not going to go down without one hell of a fight. The Soul of Cinder intentionally fights very much like a player would; it's the only boss in the entire trilogy that can completely switch up its strategies and fighting style at the drop of a hat and will keep you on your toes the whole time. The current style is indicated by the weapon it's using (or rather, what it's shaped the Coiled Sword into):

h: Kiln Of The First Flame (To Link The Fire)
t: SHOW SPOILER Soul of Cinder Longsword: the Soul of Cinder starts with this and is at his easiest-to-battle while using it, though that doesn't at all equate to a cakewalk. It'll mainly perform two-slash combos, but is capable of switching into uppercuts, downward slams, and even powerful thrusting attacks. Your best bet for openings to damage it is after the aforementioned combos, where it'll pause for a second. Staff: the Soul of Cinder will spam Homing Crystal Soulmass (5-7 orbs around its head that track toward you when you get close), Crystal Soul Spear (a single large and powerful projectile fired from the tip of the staff) Farron Hail/Soul Stream (dozens of small projectiles rapid-fired, easily stunlocking you to death), and Soul Greatsword (staff is enveloped in a large blade, allowing for melee attacks). The advice? If you don't have Vow of Silence ready to cast, stay the hell away until the Soul of Cinder switches to literally any other weapon, as it's not worth engaging at close range and you need a lot of distance to dodge the sorceries. Curved Sword: the Soul of Cinder will perform some melee attacks, generally two-slash combos, but relies on pyromancies just as often; Fire Orb(hurls a fireball at you from a distance), Power Within (glows red, increasing attack power), Combustion (releases a short-range blast of flame from its hand), and Poison Mist (spews a large cloud of, well, poison mist). It's common to warn players to stay away during THIS style, but the author found it only a bit more challenging than the Longsword style by staying close and waiting for its melee combos. Greatlance: the Soul of Cinder will mainly perform lunging thrusts (sometimes accompanied by an arena-long charge) and wide sweeping strikes, but has access to two miracles that you definitely need to watch out for - Wrath of the Gods (powerful shockwave that'll knock you flat on your ass) and Med Heal (slowly heals itself). As with the other two melee-oriented styles, this is pretty straightforward to fight and you'll definitely want to exploit the Soul of Cinder pausing to heal itself.

h: Kiln Of The First Flame (To Link The Fire)
t: Because the Soul of Cinder's melee attacks are almost always coated in flame, consume as many Red Bug Pellets as you need to survive; it's also weak to lightning, so this is the best time to use up those Gold Pine Resins because every hit has to count here and you need to be patient, only performing 1-2 at a time before waiting for the next opening. It's worth noting that the Soul of Cinder can be staggered, but it'll take quite a lot of hits, so don't count on that. This'll be intense, but once you deplete its HP, the Soul of Cinder will... ...well, the popular saying is lock in as it refills its HP. It'll straighten up, burn the flames within its body even brighter, and coat the Coiled Sword in fire as it starts using an entirely different style: that of Gwyn, the lord of sunlight himself, and unlike in the first game, you do not get to cheese this one with ripostes. The Soul of Cinder will now unleash a completely new set of sword attacks: An overhead leaping slash that can easily cross the arena; A set of horizontal slashes with the coating fire lengthened to greatly extend its range; A kick that can knock you down in a fraction of a second; A frontal grab that'll immobilize and engulf you in a powerful explosion; A running thrust that'll send you flying; And, most infamously, an upward slash (telegraphed by the Soul of Cinder leaning back and holding the Coiled Sword behind himself) that'll launch you into a five-hit combo, culminating in the Coiled Sword being planted in your back and detonating while you're lying on the ground trying to remember what day it is. Avoid this at all costs. The Soul of Cinder is far from melee-bound, though, as Gwyn taking the helm means it can use his famous miracles at any range - a thick lightning bolt that'll either be thrown directly at you as a single projectile, into the ground in front of the Soul of Cinder (if you're attacking it from the front), or into the air to rain dozens of homing projectiles down on you after a few seconds. Even if it's technically simplified from the first phase, this fight is brutal and will see you taking lots of damage if you screw up even one roll.

h: Kiln Of The First Flame (To Link The Fire)
t: Thankfully, the Red Bug Pellets and Gold Pine Resins will be just as useful here as they were before, though finding a window to apply them is tricky; the best time for that and getting a full combo in is after you dodge the Soul of Cinder's five-hit combo, as it'll always plant the Coiled Sword in the ground (with no explosion) at the end and stay there for a few seconds before moving onto a different attack. Otherwise, the slash combos and the leaping slam will give you just enough time to get 1-2 attacks in before retreating to a safe distance, and generally rolling to your right will keep you safe. If you made it this far with a majority of your Estus Flasks intact, expect to burn through most or all of them by the end of this - they really made sure to test your skill with this last dance. Strategy Video Credit and thanks to Boss Fight Database for the video guide. When the red knight finally turns to dust, you'll receive the Soul of the Lords (do not consume this!) and the option to interact with the Flame. In this case, you'll simply walk over and press to Kneel at it, fulfilling your oath to rekindle the fire...for what little that's worth... ...and after the credits roll, you'll get the option to begin Journey 2 (NG+) right away or return to Firelink Shrine first (by selecting No). You'll want to go the latter route so you can do one more thing (two, if you want) before jumping back into the Untended Graves - at the Firelink Shrine, run up to Ludleth's ashes to Transpose the Soul of the Lords into Sunlight Spear (31/35). If you so desire, you can also purchase the Firelink Set, what the final boss wore, from the Handmaid with plenty of Souls to do so, using the rest on levels. Now, got everything you want and need from this playthrough? Sit at the Bonfire and select "Begin journey 2", just like in Drangleic, and let's start over...

Welcome back to the start of the game; you've kept your level, loadout, and everything in your inventory except for Key Items (e.g. Keys and Ashes), but now all the shortcuts are locked up again and the enemies/bosses are substantially stronger. Here begins the most "fun" part of this whole trophy list; unlike Dark Souls I and II, you have to revisit every single location in the game (though, thankfully, not defeat every boss again - just most) during both the second and third playthroughs to collect everything needed for the trophy list because, wouldn't ya know it, +1 and +2 variants of several rings only spawn in New Game+ and New Game++, respectively! You're going to take you through the most efficient path to getting all those, plus the remaining spells, as you work toward the next ending - the End of Fire. 1. Cemetery of Ash: Run through to the end of the first area and turn right at the passage leading out to the cliff overlooking Firelink Shrine; in the area with the Ravenous Crystal Lizard, you'll find the Speckled Stoneplate Ring+1 (69/107) on a grave to the right. On the cliff, light the Bonfire and run down to the arena to pull out the Coiled Sword and take on Iudex Gundyr, whom you'll find to be a hell of a lot easier this time around. Through the doors, run up to the Firelink Shrine and talk to the Fire Keeper, then insert the Coiled Sword into the Bonfire and Travel to the High Wall of Lothric. 2. High Wall of Lothric: Open the door and descend the stairs to light the Bonfire before heading down the left set of stairs and entering the building underneath the dead wyvern to go down the ladder. On the walkway outside, ignore the stairs and cut a path through the Hollows toward the Lothric Knight to reach and light the Bonfire on the top floor behind him.

From the floor below the Bonfire, go down the stairs and through the doorway to the rooftops outside. After taking out the Pus of Man in the center of the praying Hollows, head over to the platform with the ladder and take a running jump from the corner of it to the adjacent roof, where the Fleshbite Ring+1 (70/107) waits next to the fence on the end. Descend the ladders to cross the pavilion below (enjoy kicking the Winged Knight's shit in along the way) and cut a swathe through the patrolling Lothric Knights to first enter the cathedral on the left and speak to Emma for the Small Lothric Banner, then descend to take out Vordt of the Boreal Valley and cross through the doors behind him to fly to the Undead Settlement. 3. Undead Settlement: Light the Bonfire and return to the Firelink Shrine to talk to Leonhard again and initiate his storyline, then go back to the Undead Settlement and run down the stairs to enter the gate and light the Bonfire on the other side. Through the tunnel, hug the right side of the open area with the large tree to avoid most of the enemies and take the bridge on the right, then take the rocky path to the right of the stables to climb up the ladder against the house. Drop off the right side toward the pacing Hollow Manservant, equip the Silvercat Ring, and fall off the end of the cliff facing the tower to open the door and enter, where Siegmeyer will come down on the lift; talk to him to start HIS storyline and take the lift down, then back up to get him up the tower. Manipulate the lifts to get the top one lowered to ground level before turning to face the entrance and riding the top lift up, which will let you step off onto the wooden platform leading to Siegmeyer's next location; past him, in an alcove, is the Life Ring+1 (71/107).

Descend into the pavilion and battle the Fire Demon with Siegmeyer, making sure he survives and that you exhaust his dialogue - then, collect the Pale Tongue from the leftmost hanging corpse on the main building beyond the main bonfire in the pavilion. Use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and cross through the open area again, but this time take the right-hand path on the far side (ignoring the bridge) to reach the narrow alleyway. Run down the alley and past the enemies to the underground room, kill Hodrick if/when he spawns on the other side, and light the Bonfire on the right before entering the graveyard further on - since you don't need his Ring anymore, you can go up to the Giant Archer and get his special Young White Branch so he'll exclusively target the enemies in this areas with the white trees, letting you sit back and chuckle heartily at the sight of the Peasant Hollows getting ragdolled to hell. Oh, and on the left side next to the small hut, you'll find a well with the Poisonbite Ring+1 (72/107). Head through the cottage at the end and up the stairs leading to the Curse-rotted Greatwood, one of two optional bosses you have to kill for something OTHER than a ring. If you want a slower but easier method for victory this time (and have the INT for it), attack the Curse-rotted Greatwood exclusively with Pestilent Mist - fully depleting its HP will skip the second phase and save you the hassle of targeting the weak spots while still giving you the Transposing Kiln and boss Soul. Use the new Bonfire to return to the Firelink Shrine and give the Transposing Kiln to Ludleth, then talk to Leonhard again to receive the Lift Chamber Key. Travel to the Tower on the Wall and take the ladder down from the lower floor so you can unlock the gate, take the lift down, and kill the Darkwraith (quite easily) below. Use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to Firelink Shrine and talk to Leonhard again to advance his storyline.

Return to the lift tower (via the Undead Settlement Bonfire) and descend on the lower lift to the basement that leads to the Road of Sacrifices; up to you if you want to use the door exploit against the Outrider Knight this time, as he's much easier to put down now. 4. Road of Sacrifices: Light and rest at the Bonfire before heading along the main path, dispatching the Corvians, and cross the bridge at the end to reach Anri and Horace, as well as the next Bonfire - you don't need them to take any specific storyline path in this playthrough, so you can treat them as you did on your first playthrough. Descend to the swamp and stay on the edge of the shore as you make your way left, killing the Lycanthrope Hunters along the way, until you reach the next Bonfire; in the swamp directly below this cliff, the Lingering Dragoncrest Ring+1 (73/107) is next to a tree. Getting close enough to pick it up will get you invaded by Heysel again, but you can run into the ruins on the left (through the square- shaped hole in the wall) and fight her in there without worrying about the Giant Crabs. Use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and run into the ruins on the left, up the stairs and straight along the path, to reach and defeat the Crystal Sage, whom you can cut down before he even has a chance to teleport. From there, take the left path toward the Cathedral of the Deep. 5. Cathedral of the Deep: Run along the path and across the bridge to light the Bonfire, then take out the Brigand and Fallen Knight on the stairs before dashing past all the enemies in that hellhole stretch of forest to reach the Cleansing Chapel beyond. Once you've lit the Bonfire inside, head up the slope to the left of the entrance into the winding dirt corridors, favoring the ones on the right so you can reach the top of the cathedral.

Keep going up the stairs until you reach the large blue doors on the top level, then turn right, clear out the Hollows, and navigate the buttresses on the left side to reach the lower platform with the two archers. Cross the bridge from here leading up to the platform with the two Grave Wardens and, from there, open the blue doors up the stairs to enter the cathedral. Proceed through the rooms until you reach the ledge guarded by the Giant Slave, then run for your life along it to the other side and descend all three flights of stairs to face the Cathedral Knight among the pews. Take the stairs on the left up to the main hall, defeat Kirk when he invades, and pull both levers (one among the pillars to the left, the other at the far corner of the pool to the right) to raise the two walls. Climb the stairs next to the Giant Slave on the right and run past the Cathedral Knight and Deacons toward the archway on the left, leading to the lift that'll take you to the front of the hall. Down the stairs past the blue doors here, you'll find Patches impersonating Siegmeyer again; this time, kill him and collect the armor, then cross the raised wall and take the stairs ahead to reach Rosaria, whom you'll offer the Pale Tongue directly to join her Covenant. Because of this, Leonhard will appear near the entrance to her room, so double back and talk to him a few times to advance his storyline. Briefly, Travel back to the Cleansing Chapel to return Siegmeyer's armor to him in the well outside, then return to Rosaria's Bed Chamber and retrace your steps across the raised walls to the pews you ran past earlier. Go up to the tilted altar (summoning Anri and Horace if you advanced their storyline), and on the side facing the fog gate, you'll find the Ring of the Evil Eye+1 (74/107).

Pass through the fog and defeat the Deacons of the Deep for the Small Doll, then return to the Crucifixion Woods Bonfire and run across the swamp toward the strait on the other side, using the ladder trick to easily kill the Exile Watchdogs once again, to reach the Farron Keep. 6. Farron Keep: From the new Bonfire, head outside and turn right, delving into the swamp beyond the trees for the Magic Stoneplate Ring+1 (75/107) before returning to the Bonfire and turning left toward the stairs in the distance, which you'll climb to extinguish the first flame. Through the archway, take the left path leading down and cross the straits of land to extinguish the second flame. Across the bridge from the second flame, take out the Ghrus and light the next Bonfire, then go outside and turn left into a narrow path running along the side of the building to find the Wolf Ring+1 (76/107). In the swamp below, follow the trail of bonfires to the right, kill the Elder Ghrus, and extinguish the final flame to open the doors (this time, Heysel won't invade you) before using the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the Bonfire and climb the ladder on the nearby tower, bringing you to the Old Wolf of Farron. Ride the lift up to the top of the wall and defeat the Stray Demon for its Soul of a Stray Demon, the ONLY boss Soul exchanged for two different trophy-relevant items. Return to the Bonfire, Travel to the Keep Ruins, and summon Heysel herself (her summon sign is located next to the tower to the right of the bottom of the stairs) to receive her gesture, "Proper bow" (31/33), then pass through the opened stone doors, heading up the path to watch the Darkwraiths cut the Ghrus to pieces. Finish off the survivors before battling the Abyss Watchers. From the new Bonfire, return to the Firelink Shrine and Transpose the Soul of a Stray Demon into Boulder Heave (27/27)! Then return to the Abyss Watchers Bonfire and descend the stairs behind it to enter the Catacombs of Carthus.

7. Catacombs of Carthus: Cross the bridge and descend the stairs on the other side, toward the slope that the first Skeleton Boulder rolls down from behind you. Once you reach the bottom and the gate with the Bonfire behind it, follow the path to the left until you come across the pillared alcove filled with pots; the closest corpse, next to the middle-left pillar, holds the Thunder Stoneplate Ring+1 (77/107). Continue following the path around to the right, light the next Bonfire, and take the stairs in front of the next Skeleton Boulder down to the long hall, where turning left and taking the exit at the end will bring you into the adjoining cave. Turn right into the bone-filled cavern and cross the bridge, cutting it down to dispatch the horde of Skeletons following you, before opening the doors at the end and interacting with the chalice on the table to battle High Lord Wolnir (this time around, you can kill him much more safely, or at least speed up the actual fight, by slowly approaching him on the right side, without alerting him, and repeatedly casting Pestilent Mist to drain his HP). Once he's dead, light the Bonfire and double back to the bridge to descend it as a ladder. Run through the stone room down here, using the Mimic to kill the Fire Demon again, and light the Bonfire at the end before entering the Smouldering Lake through the tunnel. 8. Smouldering Lake: Run to the right-center area of the lake and use the Giant Avelyn to destroy the stony section of the ground, letting you drop into the ruins below. From where you drop, turn left (toward the Demon Cleric) and enter the room behind him to light the next Bonfire, then take the stairs down and follow the path to the large room with the multiple Demon Clerics, where you'll want to turn left into the tunnel, take the first right into the room with blue roots, and turn left again before taking the stairs on the right down.

In the long hall, go down the stairs on the left into the room filled with Basilisks and ignore them to run to the other side, toward the large set of stairs leading up to the bridge. Cut down the Black Knight waiting for you and climb the ladder at the end to reach the ledge with the Giant Avelyn. Use the rock tunnel on the left-hand side to safely approach the Giant Avelyn, dispatching the Skeletons and Bonewheel Skeletons, and Skeleton Swordsmen up the slope. On the far side of the mechanism (the cliff edge), you'll find the Bloodbite Ring+1 (78/107) and can use the Coiled Sword Fragment to return to the High Lord Wolnir Bonfire and climb the stairs to reach Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. 9. Irithyll of the Boreal Valley: Light the Bonfire and rush across the bridge, killing the Sulyvahn's Beast that chases you so you don't have to deal with it in the water later, to light the next Bonfire and begin heading up the slope, taking out the Pontiff Knights as you go. Up the first set of stairs, you'll want to prioritize the Fire Witches before dealing with the Irithyllian Slaves, as they'll be able to target you from further away than any other enemy. As you keep going, turn left before the large archway to enter the church and light the next Bonfire, then descend the stairs, turn left outside down the next set of stairs, and keep going down the path until you enter the dark room filled with Irithyllian Slaves. Run to the end of the room onto the balcony and drop off a gap in the railing to the right to find the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring+1 (79/107). Now, use the Coiled Sword Fragment and return to the church to go back outside onto the main path and through the large archway, dispatching the Pontiff Knights and Fire Witch as you go; at the altar beyond it, go around the back side to pick up the Chloranthy Ring+1 (80/107).

At the bottom of the stairs opposite the gate to the left of the altar and follow the railing around from it, you can pick up a new Soul Chunk, two Souls of an Old Hand -then return to the church and retrace your steps to the dark room of Irithyllian Slaves, where THIS time you'll take the stairs down from the balcony at the end into the water and cross all the way to the other side to light the Bonfire inside the tower. Double back outside and head into the tunnel midway along the wall, running past and ignoring the Sewer Centipedes to reach the stairs on the other side, where you should exhaust Siegward's dialogue again before proceeding into the room beyond with the Silver Knights and paintings. Dash past the Silver Knights and turn left up the stairs, where you'll be invaded by the Londor Pale Shade on the steps; dispatch him and the other enemies, then continue up the next set of stairs beyond the statue at the top, as well as the stairs inside the building. Ignoring the Irithyllian Slaves, take out the two Pontiff Knights at the top of the stairs beyond the building and enter the fog, with or without Anri (depending on how you've advanced their storyline), to kick Pontiff Sulyvahn's ass again. After lighting the Bonfire, head outside and turn left toward Anor Londo. 10. Anor Londo: Drop into the hall under the bridge, exit on the other side, climb the stairs, and turn around to run back inside the chapel - cross the bridge here and advance to the third pillar on the left ahead of you to retrieve the Ring of Favor+1 (81/107). Go back outside (activating the shortcut if you like) and dash through the crowd of Deacons to ascend the stairs inside the tower and head up the connecting buttress -it's best to run like hell past the Silver Knights up here until you reach the second buttress leading down to a lower platform, where you'll want to head inside the connecting archway and turn left to find the lever that'll lower the rotating bridge.

Rotate the bridge with the lever at the top and walk onto the adjoining bridge to light the Bonfire, then dash up the stairs past the Silver Knights and turn left to reach the corpse of the Giant Blacksmith inside the tower. Go up the stairs to enter the main cathedral, inside of which you'll want to descend the stairs on the left to dispatch the five Deacons that'll be hurling fireballs at you BEFORE reaching the floor and dashing into the fog door to exterminate Aldrich. Once you're done, Travel to the Distant Manor Bonfire that you lit earlier and descend into Irithyll Dungeon. 11. Irithyll Dungeon: After dispatching the Fire Witch and Pontiff Knight waiting for you below, you'll be invaded by Alva, Seeker of the Spurned on the steps outside, and once you deal with him (or he deals with you...strong bastard, he is), you can descend the stairs in the cliff he emerged from to reach the first Bonfire. On the stone hallway outside, kill the first Jailers as you come across them and cross the bridge, then enter the first cell on the right and cross through the holes in the walls to the hall on the other side of the locked door, which you'll want to drop down from to reach the lower hall. Run outside (to the left) from here to reach the outdoor stairs overlooking the Profaned Capital and head down the stairs to enter a corridor filled with Hollows; turning right and running all the way to the end will let you pick up another Soul of an Old Hand. Descend the ladder from the other exit here and open the door to reach the sleeping Giant Slave - briefly swap in the Silvercat Ring and drop off the ledge here to safely reach the ground floor, then run into the tunnel on the left to reach the lift connecting to the first Bonfire. Ride the lift up, then take it back down and, on the way (while facing the direction of the Bonfire), walk off of it onto a pair of wooden planks against the wall holding the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring+1 (82/107).

Back in the room with the Giant Slave, take the stairs on the opposite side and climb the ladder before heading through the small doorway to land on the overhang above the narrow bridge, which you'll want to drop down onto so you can enter the sewer grate. After running all the way to the end to open the chest and collect the Old Cell Key, take the first right in here, kill the two Giant Rats that attack you, and lift up the gate to enter the room with the patrolling Jailers so you can run past them (to the right) to the stairs outside. Cross the bridge, kill the Flame Gargoyle that flies down, and climb the ladder inside the structure to light the Bonfire. A detour before you keep going: Travel to the Rosaria's Bed Chamber Bonfire, and you'll discover that *gasp* she's been murdered! Inspecting her corpse will give you the Black Eye Orb, and taking that to the former chamber of Gwynevere (via the elevators on either side of the Aldrich, Devourer of Gods Bonfire) will cause it to begin quivering - use it in here, and you'll invade the world of her killer, none other than Leonhard. This guy...well, he's a right pain in the ass with not only three Estus Flasks to undo your progress as you fight him, but a couple fairly damaging sorceries as well, the most damaging of which is his Soul Greatsword. However, what you REALLY have to watch out for is his Weapon Art, where he'll hold up his shotel and fire off a spinning energy disc that does a LOT of damage (especially with your reduced HP) and covers a long distance, so prepare for a lot of rolling. Once he's down, you'll receive his Silver Mask and Crescent Moon Sword...as well as the Soul of Rosaria, the true prize here that you'll need to go to Ludleth with so you can Transpose it into Bountiful Sunlight (32/35). Sorry, Rosaria, you'll get to live next time!
